## [0.9.0rc414]

**The MCP wire round-trip — a carrier that crosses the wire comes back a carrier (`#T1092`).** Before this rc, an exact-algebra carrier with no `serialise_native` branch fell through `_json_fallback` to `return repr(obj)` and crossed the wire as a metadata **string**. `zeilberger` handed its `certificate` back as `"BiPoly(k_degree=1, exact-ℚ[n,k])"` — prose about the object that is the entire point of the op. This rc gives every such carrier a wire form, gives the wire a **structural inverse** it never had, and ships the gate that can report the property false.

### The `$srmech_carrier` envelope — and why an envelope rather than more coercer rows

`serialise_native` is **structural** (it walks the value); `coerce_param` is **declared-type** (a table read off `returns.type`). There was no structural inverse, so a carrier nested inside a `dict` / `list` was serialised out and **could never be reconstructed in** — and that is where the mathematical content lives. **119** registered ops declare a bare `dict`, 39 a `list`, 23 a `tuple`. Adding ~20 per-type coercer rows would not have touched the nested case at all.

A carrier now rides as `{"$srmech_carrier": "<name>", "value": …}` — the by-VALUE peer of the `$srmech_handle` by-REFERENCE envelope the rc16 handle grammar already established — and the new `deserialise_native` rebuilds it at any depth.

**The `value` payload is not new grammar.** Each one is the wire form the **compiled** implementation already reads: `srmech_carrier_marshal` has consumed exactly these nested exact-ℚ shapes since rc191/rc223 (`SRMECH_CARRIER_POLY` / `_BIPOLY` / `_SCALAR` / `_TRIPOLY` / `_QBIPOLY` / `_ELLRATIO` in `c/include/srmech.h`), and the Python `_pairs` / `_from_pairs` bridges that feed it are the same functions the encoders call. So the two implementations already agreed on the payload; the envelope adds only the tag saying which carrier it is. **This shaped the design**: the rc414 research brief proposed a fresh `{"x_low": int, "cells": […]}` shape for `QPoly`, which would have minted a SECOND, divergent encoding of an object the C peer already reads as `[x_low, rows]`. The shipped form is the one that already existed.

**16 carriers gain a wire form:** `Poly` · `BiPoly` · `TriPoly` · `QPoly` · `QBiPoly` · `EllMonomial` · `Theta` · `EllRatio` · `One` · `ChainSpec` · `RecoverableFold` · `QMat` · `Qalg` · `CarrierSpectrum` · `ThetaSum` · `ThetaBracketSum` · `MockQSeries`. `CDRegister` / `SedenionRegister` ride the `$srmech_handle` envelope instead (see below). Measured on the carrier registry: **21 of 26** evaluable carriers now survive a round trip; **0** cross as a repr string.

### Three SILENT-CORRUPTION defects — each returned a different, well-formed object with no exception

- **`cascade.the_one` DROPPED the winding triad.** rc408 (`#T1078`) made `w` a **declared, pinned parameter**, so from rc408 an MCP caller could SET the winding and could never READ it back — the round-trip returned a well-formed `One` **at rest**, silently. `One._to_jsonable` / `one_from_jsonable` now carry `winding`; `spinor` and the `(−1)^Σw` `spinor_sign` are re-derived from it exactly. The key is spent **only when the triad is non-rest**, so an unwound `One`'s dict is byte-identical to every prior release and the agreement with the compiled object-model engine is preserved exactly where it already held (the `genome.amplify` precedent — `n == 1` costs no bytes). *This defect was held in place by its own gate*: `test_one_dict_contract_is_the_three_adjoint_fields_only` asserted a WOUND One serialises to exactly the three adjoint fields. That test is re-aimed at the property it was standing in for — the adjoint is w-BLIND, which is still true and still asserted.
- **An `EllMonomial` repr was read back as a SYMBOL NAME.** `EllMonomial(1·q^2)` → wire `"EllMonomial(1·q^2)"` → `_to_ellmonomial`'s string branch → `EllMonomial(1·EllMonomial(1·q^2)^1)`, a different valid monomial. The outbound branch removes the input; the string branch now **rejects** a token containing `(`, `)` or `·`, because a symbol name is a bare identifier and never contains those.
- **`cascade.sedenion_register` emitted a NON-DETERMINISTIC payload.** The class ships no `__repr__`, so the default one carried a **memory address** and two identical calls produced different bytes.

### Capability gaps closed in BOTH directions

- **`QPoly` / `QBiPoly` lost `x_low`.** Not only a missing outbound branch: the inbound `_to_qpoly` could not express a Laurent `QPoly` either, because `QPoly.from_coeffs(seq, x_low=0)` takes `x_low` as a **separate parameter** and the coercer passed only the list. A Laurent polynomial came back re-based at `x_low=0` — a different polynomial. Both halves land here or neither would be worth anything.
- **`CDRegister` / `SedenionRegister` are handle-shaped, not value-shaped.** Each holds a `D`-wide hypervector store behind mutating methods and inherits object identity, so the thing a consumer wants back is the live object. They ride `$srmech_handle` under `kind` `"cd-register"` / `"sedenion-register"` — `_handles.register(obj, *, kind, name=)` was already generic, and its module docstring anticipated exactly this.
- **`ChainSpec` did not round-trip through its own parser.** `serialise_result` emitted the step key `class_id`; `parse_chain_spec` requires `class`. The advertised schema publishes `spec: "object"`, so a schema-obedient client was instructed to send the value guaranteed to raise `AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'steps'` — the rc408 anti-pattern verbatim. The wire form now emits `class`, and `"ChainSpec"` maps to a real `_to_chain_spec` (it delegates to `parse_chain_spec`, so there is one definition of what a chain is) instead of the `_identity` pass-through.
- **`Qalg` had no wire form** — see ADR-0012 C5 below.

### `srmech.biology.coupling.fold_identity` is REGISTERED (registry 559 → 560)

Not a new op: shipped and `coupling.__all__`-exported since task #723, named in `RecoverableFold`'s own class docstring — and carrying **no ToolEntry**, while all seven of its `coupling` siblings had one. It was therefore absent from `describe()`, from the MCP tool list, and from every registry-driven census. **That invisibility had a measured cost**: a research leg reading the coupling module concluded `RecoverableFold` "cannot be gated" while its purpose-built three-valued gate (`EQUAL` / `NOT_EQUAL` / `UNKNOWN`) sat 215 lines below the line being read. An op invisible to introspection is, for an LLM consumer, an op that does not exist.

### `mcp_callable=False` — the first one since the field was introduced

`srmech.introspect.publish` is now excluded from the advertised catalog, with an `mcp_unavailable_reason`. It is the **only** candidate that survived examination; the rest **dissolved**, and the corrected scope is worth recording:

- the ~19 exact-algebra carriers were un-**encoded**, not un-**callable** → the envelope above;
- `sedenion_register` / `cd_register` → the handle envelope;
- **`run_chain` — REJECTED, explicitly.** `spec` is a `ChainSpec` and `coerce_param` mapped that type to the `_identity` pass-through, so the JSON object a client sends arrived raw and the op raised `AttributeError`. The advertised schema publishes `spec: object`, telling the client to send exactly that. **This is a MISSING COERCER, not a missing capability**, and marking it uncallable would have renamed a fixable defect into a permanent limitation. `resolve_chain` likewise: registering the returned closure through `_handles` round-trips and re-invokes correctly.
- **`get_tool_schema` — removed from the candidate list without a flip.** It was a candidate only because its over-MCP rendering (`dataclasses.asdict`) *disagreed* with the canonical `to_jsonable` (2,572,811 vs 2,501,642 bytes, five extra keys) — the same object with two renderings, and which one a consumer got depended on which door it came through. `_json_fallback` now prefers an object's own `to_jsonable`, so the two AGREE. Removing the wrong rendering by removing the op would have been the wrong repair.

`publish` does not dissolve because its obstruction is not its TYPE but its **shape in time**: a `with`-block scope cannot span two JSON-RPC calls, and a handle that survived the response would outlive the request. **This is also the first live exercise of the C `mcp_callable` / `mcp_unavailable_reason` round-trip**, which had never run with a non-default value — verified against a rebuilt `libsrmech` (registry 560, advertised 559).

**Four strict-zero assertions were re-aimed, not deleted.** `excluded == []`, `"== 0" in doc`, `pending == set()` (×2) and `len(schema.tools) == expected + 0` all encoded *"zero excluded, forever"* — the **mirror image** of the stale hardcoded `7` that rc407 removed. Each is replaced by the property it stood for and by no literal: **every excluded entry carries a reason**, **no advertised catalog contains an excluded entry**, and **the advertised catalog is exactly the `mcp_callable` subset** (an equality, derived on both sides — the old `spectral_names <= mcp_names` subset check over 7 hardcoded names could not see the advertised catalog silently losing entries it did not name). `test_mcp.py`'s `_ADVERTISED` list, which parametrises **two** coverage sweeps, gains a floor so exclusions cannot drain it one at a time.

### ADR-0012 clause C5 (CHAINABLE) — flipped from `CLOSED in-rc` to gated, honestly

C5 requires a producer's output to feed its designed consumer over **every advertised transport**. It was marked `CLOSED in-rc`, three separate sentences in the ADR asserted it was gated, and it was **refuted by execution on the exhibit written into the clause itself**: feeding `equal_temperament_partials`' own `ratios` into `spectrum_tier` over the wire raised `TypeError: expected Q, Qalg, int or an (int, int) pair; got str`, because the ratios are `Qalg` and `Qalg` had no wire form — `Q` gained its `[num, den]` branch at rc231 with the comment *"never a lossy float, **never a bare repr string**"* and the algebraic peer never followed.

It went green because **there was no C5 instrument**: §3.3's instrument table lists C2, C3 and the prose op-refs, and every exercise of the exhibit (`tests/test_music_commensurability_rc362.py:231`, `:244`, `:280`, `:522`) calls the ops **directly** — the one transport the clause is not about. All three "gated" sentences are corrected in place rather than silently rewritten, because an ADR sentence saying a clause was gated turned out to be the only evidence anyone had that it was. Also fixed: C3's citation of `srmech/amsc/carrier_schema.py`, a path ADR-0010 moved and which no longer exists.

### `tests/test_wire_round_trip_rc414.py` — the instrument, with its own lies enumerated

The **outbound converse** of `test_all_param_types_json_coercible` (the inbound exhaustiveness ratchet). Three ways this gate could have manufactured green, each closed:

1. **Bare `==`.** `coerce_param(…, 'Vec')` returns a plain `list` and `Vec.__eq__` accepts any flat sequence, so `back == v` is True *while the carrier is gone*. The verdict is the conjunction `type(back) is type(v) and back == v`; `EQUAL_BUT_TYPE_LOST` is its own reported class.
2. **A `has_coercer` MISS is not a pass.** A table miss returns the value unchanged, so it can compare equal to itself. Those are `PASS_NOCOERCER` and count as failures; the one honest exception (a value rebuilt by the STRUCTURAL envelope, which needs no declared-type row) is detected positively from the wire sentinel.
3. **Enumerating nothing.** `test_the_gate_enumerates_something` runs first and asserts the floors before any population is used.

Equality is **per-carrier**, because `==` is not the identity operator for everything srmech ships: `RecoverableFold` goes through `fold_identity` with `UNKNOWN` recorded as its own bucket (an honest decline is not a failure); the two registers cross by reference, so their claim is **identity**, which is stronger than equality; and a carrier with no `__eq__` at all (`CarrierSpectrum`) is judged on wire-identity under its own label, never silently as value equality. Ceilings are **down-only**: 5 carriers not round-tripping, 3 whose shipped `construct` example does not evaluate, 131 ops declaring a return type with no inbound coercer. The gate parses with `srmech._json.loads` (srmech's own JSON front door) so it exercises the native `srmech_json_parse` against the format srmech emits; it is honestly **stdlib-out / srmech-in**, because `srmech._json` ships no `dumps` by design — and it is `serialise_result`'s stdlib `json.dumps(default=…)` that carried the defect.

### Fixed prose that had gone false

`README.md`'s `handle_pending: 0` claim (two places, both in the **PyPI long-description**); a CHANGELOG line claiming `write_packed_graph` is `mcp_callable=False` (live: `True`, `None` — the flip was described but never made); ADR-0012's *"~60 assertions across ~54 test files"* and the same figure in `docs/srmech/CLAUDE.md`, both **re-measured with the predicate stated** (`== <total>` in `tests/` → 73 lines / 66 files, plus `EXPECTED_N`, which that predicate cannot match — an unstated predicate is why the number could not be re-measured and went stale twice).

`tools/ripple_gates.txt` gains four targets: the round-trip gate plus the three `mcp_callable` surfaces, none of which was listed — `ripple_check.py` went **green** on an exclusion flip while CI went red.

## [0.9.0rc413]

**Phase 1 purity, part 1 — the dotted-callable resolver moves OUT of `srmech.mcp` and into core (`#T1094`).** `describe()["tools"]["total"]` **HOLDS at 559** — no op added, none removed. `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays **12**; no signature change, no C symbol added or removed. All 6 generated files are byte-unchanged (`tools/regen_all.py --check` clean), because nothing this rc edits feeds a generator. Pure-Python relocation plus caller repointing.

- **THE DEFECT.** `_resolve_dotted_callable` — the robust dotted-name walker that tries *every* split point, not just the last dot — was defined in `srmech/mcp/_tools.py`. Two of its three callers are **core**: `srmech._handles.resolve_operator_name` (the `chiral_dual` operator-name grammar) and `srmech.dsl._alias._resolve_target` (the `[[alias]]` config rung). Both imported *upward* into the MCP adapter. ADR-0009 §4 exempts `srmech.mcp` / `srmech.llm` from the capability invariant precisely because they are **host glue**; core depending on host glue inverts that exemption and makes the adapter non-removable. It now lives at **`srmech/_resolve.py`** — a top-level private core module, peer to the existing `_handles.py` / `_json.py` / `_toml.py`, chosen so that every edge points INTO core and no new package edge is created (`_handles` is itself top-level, so any subpackage home would have added one).

- **The measurement, with a baseline that FAILS.** Copy the package, `rm -rf srmech/mcp srmech/llm`, exercise the two core rungs:

  | | rc412 | rc413 |
  |---|---|---|
  | `resolve_operator_name("srmech.cascade.chiral_flip")` | `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'srmech.mcp'` | resolves → `chiral_flip` |
  | `dsl.alias("my_gcd", "srmech.math.cyclic.gcd")` | `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'srmech.mcp'` | resolves → `gcd(12,18) == 6` |

  **The honest caveat, because it is the part that could have produced a false green:** a *module-import* sweep over the mcp-less tree reports **0 failures at BOTH rc412 and rc413**. Both old imports were function-local, so the dependency was a **call-time** one and an import sweep cannot see it. The table above is the measurement; the import sweep is not evidence of the fix and is recorded here so nobody re-runs it and concludes the edge never existed.

- **The `[class]` rung's weaker resolver is LEFT ALONE, and that is the decision, not an omission.** `srmech.dsl._class_catalog._resolve_op` splits on the last dot only. It is not a duplicate awaiting a merge — it is a **narrower contract**. Measured this rc over real `module.Class.method` triples enumerated from the shipped package (N = **307**: every class defined in its own module, public methods only): the core walker resolves **307/307**, `_resolve_op` raises `ModuleNotFoundError` on **307/307**. Unifying them would therefore *widen* what a user-registered `[class]` TOML `op` may bind — a behaviour change to the class rung with its own design question and its own test. **Over every population srmech actually ships, the two agree exactly**: ToolEntry names **0/559** divergent, class-catalog op-refs **0/31**, alias targets **0/7**, cascade-catalog dotted ops **0/1**. So the split costs nothing today and stands on purpose. `_resolve_op` keeps its `lru_cache` and its `.cache_clear()` attribute (two tests call it); a new guard pins that attribute so a later "just unify them" cannot silently drop it.

- **The `inspect.ismodule` inner fallback is NOT dead code — it was filed as dead and the filing was wrong.** It never fires across a sweep of the 559 registry names, and the `srmech.cascade.sedenion_register` case its original comment cited genuinely no longer needs it (`srmech/cascade/__init__.py`'s `from .sedenion_register import sedenion_register` rebinds the package attribute back to the function). Both observations are true; the conclusion "therefore remove it" is false. **Measured:** 27 submodule/callable name collisions exist in the tree, **24** leave the parent package attribute bound to the MODULE, and **two are reachable from a bare `import srmech` interpreter and resolve ONLY through this branch** — `srmech.apokatastasis.zeilberger` and `srmech.introspect.search`. Deleting it turns both into `DottedNameError`. The branch was justified by an example that had since stopped needing it, which is exactly how it came to look dead. `tests/test_resolve_dotted_callable_rc413.py` pins both survivors, pins the *premise* that they are still module-shadowed (so the test cannot pass vacuously if the tree stops shadowing them), and proves the branch by **counterfactual** — a subprocess stubs `inspect.ismodule` to constant-`False`, the observable equivalent of deleting the branch, and asserts both names break.

- **The MCP layer's own error contract is unchanged.** `MCPToolError` stays in `srmech/mcp/_tools.py` — it is an MCP-layer concern and `_entry_by_name` raises it for genuinely MCP reasons. The core walker raises the new `srmech._resolve.DottedNameError`, and `invoke_tool` re-wraps it, so `_server.handle`'s and the Anthropic adapter's `except MCPToolError` keep turning a bad tool name into a JSON-RPC error response rather than a traceback. **The deliberate break:** `_handles` / `dsl.alias` resolution failures now raise `DottedNameError` instead of `MCPToolError` — `srmech.dsl` raising an *MCP* error was itself the inversion this rc removes, so it is corrected rather than shimmed. No compatibility alias is left in `srmech.mcp._tools`; a guard asserts the old name is gone, since a shim would quietly re-create the edge.

- **And this rc caught ITSELF authoring the same defect one rung up, exactly as rc411 and rc412 each did.** The first push wrote the registry total as a literal into `srmech/_resolve.py`'s module docstring — *"ToolEntry names 0/559 divergent"* — inside a paragraph arguing against restating counts. rc410's `test_no_shipped_module_restates_the_registry_total` caught it and took **6 of 16 CI cells red on one root cause** (`1 failed, 13877 passed` on the ubuntu py3.12 full suite; the file passes in isolation, so only the full suite could see it). The docstring now states the finding as **zero divergence with no denominator** — a zero census is basis-free, so the denominator carried no information it needed. The per-population counts live here in the CHANGELOG, which is where a number that moves belongs.

- **Left undone, deliberately.** (1) `srmech/cli/mcp.py` still imports `..mcp._mcpb` / `..mcp._tools` — correctly, since it *is* the `srmech mcp` subcommand; the imports are function-local so the mcp-less core imports and runs, and only that subcommand fails. Not a resolver concern. (2) The walker never attempts to import the **full** dotted name as a module, so `srmech.apokatastasis.gosper` and four siblings raise in a fresh interpreter where the parent has not eagerly imported the submodule; that is a pre-existing latent gap, out of scope for a relocation, and now visible in the measurement above. (3) ADR-0004 §2 still names the removed `srmech.qm.*` path (it is `srmech.physics.qm.*` since rc382) — noted, not fixed here.

## [0.9.0rc412]

**The COMPOSITION GRAIN — `composes` gets a reader, its gate gets the hole closed, and seven rows get hand-traced (`#T1093`).** `describe()["tools"]["total"]` **HOLDS at 559** — no op added. `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays **12**; no signature change; no C symbol added. The generated `c/src/srmech_tool_registry.c` grows the new `composes` arrays, which is regeneration, not an ABI event: `srmech_tool_entry_t` has carried `composes` / `composes_count` / `preserves` / `preserves_count` since rc305, and a caller receives a **pointer**, so populating leaves every struct offset unchanged.

- **THE DIAGNOSIS, and it is rc411's diagnosis one field-pair later.** rc411 found the introspect layer's authored half at 100% and its derived half at 0% — `explanation` and `example` populated everywhere and read by no accessor. The STRUCTURED half is the same defect and was still open: rc305 added `ToolEntry.composes` / `ToolEntry.preserves`, both ride the wheel, both are baked into the compiled-in C registry — and the only things that read either one were `ToolEntry.to_jsonable`, the curated merge and the C serialiser. Not one of those is a question a caller asks. rc411's own brand-new index did not read them either: `search.py::_op_fields` indexed exactly `name` / `category` / `summary` / `explanation` / `example.*`. **Populating a field nothing reads only moves a hash**, which is why this rc ships the reader BEFORE it ships rows.

- **`ToolSchema.composition(name)` — the reader, and the REVERSE direction is the capability.** Returns `{"name", "composes", "composed_by"}` for one op in one call: the resolved full name, the declared ordered sub-ops (downward, as declared), and the ops that declare this one (upward, sorted). Downward was always one attribute access away. **Upward had no reader at all** — the registry could say what `genome_from_graph` is built from and could not say what is built from `mint_strand`, and inverting a directed edge by hand means iterating the whole registry. That is precisely the second call ADR-0012's autonomous-composition standard forbids. `None` when the name does not resolve, so *"no such op"* stays distinguishable from *"a leaf with no edges"*, which answers with two empty tuples; the name goes through `resolve`, so a bare leaf works and an ambiguous leaf returns `None` rather than picking a side. Derived per call and nothing cached, per ADR-0011 — an inverted index held across a profile registration would be stale exactly when it mattered.

  **It is a `ToolSchema` METHOD, not a new registered op, and that is a deliberate ripple decision.** Registering it would take the total 559 → 560 and fire the four-generated-file public-callable ripple for a pure traversal over data the registry already holds. `by_owner` / `lookup` / `resolve` / `resolve_all` set the precedent: registry traversal lives on the object `get_tool_schema()` returns.

  **ADR-0009 parity: no C symbol is owed, and this is not an exemption claim.** A registry traversal is `non_compute`; the obligation on that bucket is transitive standalone-C reachability, and a bare-C host has it — `srmech_tool_registry_count` / `_get` walk the same table and each `srmech_tool_entry_t` carries `composes` + `composes_count`, so both directions are derivable there by the same single pass.

- **`composes` / `preserves` also join the search index — and the honest measurement is that the index is NOT where the value is.** `_op_fields` now emits both when non-empty (an empty field contributes no label and no bytes, the same key-omission `to_jsonable` and the C serialiser already perform, so a leaf op's frame is byte-identical to before). **Measured over the 27 declared sub-op references this rc ships: the `composes` text wins the `why` attribution on ZERO of them**, because a row's own prose almost always already names the ops it composes — only 1 of 27 references has a leaf name that appears nowhere else in its row. So the index inclusion is a completeness fix (the field was silently outside the retrieval corpus for no stated reason) and `composition()` is the reader that answers a question nothing else could. The suite says so explicitly: `test_the_indexed_composes_text_is_reachable_by_a_query` asserts the frame is in the corpus and does NOT assert `why == "composes"`, because pinning an attribution the data does not support would be a test asserting a wish.

- **THE GATE HOLE, measured and closed.** rc305's `test_every_composes_entry_is_a_registered_op` is a real gate — whole-registry, strict-zero, and it does go red on a phantom name. Its hole is ADR-0012 §6.1's named failure mode verbatim: **a strict-zero sweep over a shrinking set is vacuously true.** `cwf_consistency_mod2`'s declaration (landed rc313) was pinned by NOTHING — every `.composes` access under `tests/` was enumerated, and only rc305's genome-only `_EXPECTED_GENOME_COMPOSES` and a round-trip reconstruction in `test_tool_schema_ops_c_rc185` touch the field at all. **Proven by mutation this rc:** strip cwf's `composes` and the declared-edge total falls **27 → 25** while `test_composes_preserves_rc305.py` stays **10 passed**, fully green. The new `tests/test_composes_grain_rc412.py` goes red with the row named.

- **The new gate is three clauses, it carries NO coverage floor, and every clause was proven to fail.** A floor is refused on measurement, not on taste: `tool_schema.py` says of `composes` *"Empty for a LEAF op (the correct default)"*, rc305 actively pins `sha256_bytes` empty, and the identity-resolved call graph puts **231 of 559** rows at zero reachable registered sub-ops even at depth 3. The only way to satisfy a floor there is to invent composition partners — filler shipped into a surface ADR-0012 makes load-bearing. A down-only ceiling on unpopulated rows is refused for the mirror reason: a ceiling presumes the residual should reach zero, and here it must not.

  | clause | what it holds | the mutation that turns it red | rc305 gate under that mutation |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | **1 — non-vacuity** | the set of declaring rows equals a reviewed roster EXACTLY, each with its ordered tuple | delete `cwf_consistency_mod2`'s declaration | **green (10 passed)** |
  | **2 — verifiability** | every declared sub-op is actually CALLED, per an identity-resolved AST call graph | add `sha256_bytes` to `kepler.pin_slot` — a REAL registered op it never calls | **green (10 passed)** |
  | **3 — shape** | no self-reference; the declared relation is acyclic | make a row name itself | **green (10 passed)** |

  Clause 1 fails in **both** directions on purpose: an undeclared population is as much a drift as a deletion, because the field ships into the wheel and into the compiled C registry either way. Adding a row means editing the roster, and that edit **is** the review.

- **Clause 2 is the substantive one: it makes a declaration checkable instead of asserted.** An identity-resolved AST call graph over the live callables — a callee expression is resolved to a LIVE OBJECT through the defining function's globals plus its function-local imports and matched by `id()`, because name-matching would collide the leaf names the registry spells more than once. It descends through unregistered `srmech.*` helpers to depth 3 because the ground truth requires it: `cwf_consistency_mod2`'s two declared sub-ops are not in its own body at all, they sit inside `_cwf_compute_pure` behind a function-local aliased import. It is a **lower bound** by construction — dynamic dispatch and C-side composition behind a thin shim are invisible to it — and that is the right direction to be wrong in: an under-reading makes a true declaration fail loudly and get adjudicated; an over-reading would quietly bless a false one. A shipped **negative control** proves the instrument discriminates rather than attributing everything (`kepler.pin_slot` must reach `atan2` and must NOT reach `sha256_bytes`).

- **The SET is derivable; the ORDER is not — measured over the whole registry.** Identity-resolved depth-1 puts **237 of 559** rows at ≥1 reachable registered sub-op (364 edges); depth-3 puts **328 of 559** (616 edges). Against the two rc305/rc313 ground-truth rows the derivation recovers **5 of 7** declared targets at depth 1 and **7 of 7** at depth 3 — depth 1 scores 0/2 on `cwf` for the indirection reason above. But *lexical* first-call order matches **0 of 2** ground-truth rows: `genome_from_graph` calls `genome_save` / `genome_census` inside a native fast-path that sits ABOVE the pure path a human traced. The contract says ORDERED, so **static analysis supplies the set and a human supplies the order** — which is exactly why clause 2 checks `declared ⊆ derived` and not sequence equality. The opposite direction, `derived ⊆ declared`, is **rejected**: it would fire on 328 rows immediately (a coverage floor in disguise) and would demand declaring `write_packed_graph` on `genome_from_graph`, which the curators deliberately omitted.

- **Population: 2 → 9 declaring rows, 7 → 27 declared references. Every one hand-traced, and the criterion is stated rather than a coverage target.** A row is populated only when all four hold: **(1) POOL** — the depth-≤3 derived set holds ≥3 registered sub-ops, the ~14% of the registry where the tuple carries something a caller could not read off the summary; **(2) LINEAR TRACE** — the pure path is a straight line read end to end, so "call order" is a fact and not a choice; **(3) NO FAST-PATH REORDERING** — either there is no native fast-path, or it is a WHOLE-op replacement calling no registered sub-op, so exactly ONE call order exists; **(4) VERIFIABLE** — declared ⊆ derived, so clause 2 can check it. The seven: `cascade.best_rational_signed` (Class K pin-slot → Class N anchor → Class C re-orient), `math.kepler.pin_slot`, `math.rational.complex_exp`, `math.hdc.klein4_encode_bytes`, `math.hdc.klein4_from_one`, `math.hdc.klein4_compose`, `math.modular_linalg.gf_rref`.

  **Criterion 3 earned its place by excluding rows, which is how you know it is doing work.** `math.laplacian.mat_svd` and `math.hdc.cooccurrence_fold` both clear the pool and both were rejected: each has a **partial** native fast-path that skips registered sub-ops the pure path calls (`mat_hermitian_eigendecompose`; `klein4_bundle_accumulate`), so two different call orders exist and no single ordered tuple is true of both. That is the same defect that makes `genome_from_graph`'s lexical order wrong.

- **`preserves` is deliberately NOT populated, because it is a DIFFERENT FEATURE with a gate that cannot yet tell an invariant from a style note.** They share a Python type and nothing else: rc305 checks `composes` entries for **registry membership** (referential integrity) and checks `preserves` only for non-emptiness. `composes` is a typed traversable edge; `preserves` is unconstrained prose, and the six strings shipped today already span at least five claim-kinds — one of them, on `genome_from_graph`, is `"numpy-free; no abs() — sign-handling stays Class-K pin-slot + Class-C"`, an implementation-discipline claim rather than an invariant of the op, whose language is true of hundreds of rows package-wide. **Any floor on `preserves` is satisfiable at scale with zero per-op information.** It gets the reader this rc and a declared taxonomy before it gets rows.

- **A stale hard-coded cardinal in SHIPPING prose was struck.** `search.py`'s ADR-0009 paragraph claimed the retrieval half *"has been executed in C over all 556 entries"* — a docstring that travels inside the wheel, and stale since the next op landed. Replaced with *"over every entry the registry carries"*, plus a note naming `srmech_tool_registry_count()` as the only spelling that cannot go stale. Continues rc409's removal of hard-coded cardinals from shipped text; the measured figures in this entry are DATED CHANGELOG measurements, which is the surface where they belong.

- **Ripple swept rather than assumed.** `test_introspect_search_rc411.py:153` enumerates the field labels `why` may name and would have gone red on the two new ones; it was widened. The whole tree was searched for other copies of that enumeration and of the `.composes` access (rc411's lesson: its round-1 fixed two copies and a third surfaced only in CI) — there are none. No test pins the `ToolSchema` method surface, so the new method ripples nowhere. `tool_schema_sha256` moves, and nothing pins it as a literal: `test_tool_registry_c_rc184` recomputes both sides and compares.

- **Self-check, WSL2, `HAS_NATIVE=True`, numpy-absent.** `tools/regen_all.py` clean and idempotent across two passes (6 outputs, 2 changed); `tools/regen_all.py --check` green afterwards. `tools/ripple_check.py` — the designated pre-push gate set for any rc that edits a `ToolEntry` — **514 passed, 1 skipped** (7m). The introspect-adjacent batch (13 files, plus rc305 and the new rc412 file) **171 passed, 1 failed**, the one failure being `test_introspect.py::test_env_var_auto_publish` on `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tomli'` — a missing conditional dependency in the local Python 3.10 (`tomli>=2.0; python_version<'3.11'` is declared in `pyproject.toml`; CI runs 3.12 with `tomllib`), unrelated to anything this rc touches. **The full suite was NOT run locally; CI is authoritative.**

## [0.9.0rc411]

**The introspect INDEX — the registry gains the ability to answer "what do you have for X" (`#T1086`).** Three ops, `describe()["tools"]["total"]` **556 → 559**, `n_categories` **HOLDS at 76**. `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 12; no signature change; no C symbol added.

- **THE DIAGNOSIS: the introspect layer's authored half is at 100% and its derived half was at 0%.** `ToolEntry.explanation` and `ToolEntry.example` are each populated for every registered srmech op and held there by a 100% floor (`test_tool_docs_coverage_rc240.py:52,:62`) — and **no accessor read either one**. `ToolSchema.resolve` reads `name`, and only whole dotted segments of it: `resolve("winding_fold")` hits, `resolve("winding")` is `None`. So the registry could answer *"what is the op called X"* and could not answer *"what do you have for X"* — the question a caller actually arrives with. That is a RETRIEVAL gap over content that already ships, not a content gap, and conflating the two is what made it look like an architecture problem instead of an accessor problem.

- **`srmech.introspect.search.search(query, *, k=10, scope="all")` — the index.** Ranks the union of the verb registry (`get_tool_schema()`) and the noun/carrier registry (`carrier_schema()`) over ALL their authored prose. Each record is `{kind, name, score, why, reach}`. `why` and `reach` are load-bearing under **ADR-0012**'s autonomous-composition standard — the answer must be actionable **without a second call** — so `why` names the matched field **and carries the matched excerpt**, and `reach` is the importable call form. A bare field label was measured insufficient: it names the field and still forces the caller to go read it, which is the second call the standard forbids.

- **It is a cascade of the 14, and every stage is a shipped registered op** — not new capability, a registered composition of ops that already ship: **E** `get_tool_schema`/`carrier_schema` → **F/B** `srmech.math.tlv.tlv_pack` → **A** `sha256_bytes` → **G** `srmech.math.search.byte_search` → **N** `srmech.math.q.Q(N−df, df)` → **G** `byte_search` over the name leaf (4× boost) → **E** `srmech.cascade.top_k_by_score`. **Float-free end to end**, not merely at the idf stage: `top_k_by_score` takes the exact `Q` scores with no float cast. No `abs()` — `tf` and `df` are counts and the scores are non-negative by construction, so no Class-K pin-slot is needed and none is faked. The frame join is `tlv_pack` (Class B) and **not** `str.join`; with a bare join the F/B label would be decorative and the cascade-shape claim false.

- **`get_tool_schema` and `tool_schema_view` are now registered rows — the registry did not contain its own front door.** Before this rc the name `get_tool_schema` matched **0 of 556** registered names: the function that *returns* the registry was not *in* it. All three rows go under the existing `introspect` category, a deliberate ripple-minimiser — category count is one of only two published quantities that does not move on a registration, so `n_categories` holds at 76.

- **ADR-0009 parity: `non_compute` / `composes_c`, and NO new C symbol is owed.** This is the bucket the tree already gives every other registry accessor — `get_tool_schema`, `tool_schema_view`, `carrier_schema`, `responsion_schema`, and `top_k_by_score` itself. The obligation attaching to it is **transitive standalone-C reachability** (`test_rosetta_completeness.py:1276`), not a dedicated entry point, and it is satisfied: `tlv_pack` / `sha256_bytes` / `byte_search` are `c_dispatched`, and `get_tool_schema` / `carrier_schema` / `top_k_by_score` are `non_compute` leaves. **This is not an exemption claim** — ADR-0009 §4 exempts only `srmech.mcp` / `srmech.llm` and the `host_glue` rows, and *"Nothing else is exempt."* Introspect is not exempt; it is simply not a compute kernel, and the ledger distinguishes those two things on purpose. `srmech_top_k_by_score` has **0 occurrences** in the C tree, and that is correct rather than a debt: the row is `non_compute`, so it never carried a C-kernel obligation. `srmech_get_tool_schema` and `srmech_tool_schema_view` already exist, so registering their Python halves adds no parity surface at all.

- **ADR-0011: derived on demand, nothing persisted.** The ADR's text on exactly this problem — *"If a legible view is wanted, derive it on demand through the tool surface; do not persist it."* The frame set is rebuilt per call and discarded: no cache file, no memo, so a result can never be stale against a registration one line earlier. The `sha256` frame digest rides on `SearchResult.witness` (a `tuple` subclass, so every consumer treating the result as a tuple of dicts is unaffected), which is the ADR's cache-vs-witness admissibility condition satisfied — and `test_the_witness_moves_when_the_corpus_moves` proves it can disagree, because a witness that cannot disagree is not a witness.

- **Measured, WSL2 numpy-absent, `HAS_NATIVE=False` (the pure path — an upper bound on cost).** Corpus **588 frames** (559 ops + 29 carriers), 2.14 MB; steady-state frame build **46 ms**; per query **65–154 ms**. Corpus results at `k=25`, denominator **588** throughout: `"greatest common divisor"` → `srmech.math.cyclic.gcd` **rank 1**; `"find zero divisors"` → `cd_zero_divisor_witness` **rank 1**; `"get the tool registry"` → `get_tool_schema` **rank 1** (need 6, closed by construction — the name matched 0 of 556 before this rc); `"winding number"` → `srmech.cascade.winding_fold` **rank 1**, against the shipped `resolve("winding") → None`; `"log base 2 of 3/2 exactly"` → `srmech.math.rational.log` **rank 3**; `"which surface lists ops"` → `srmech.introspect.describe` **rank 5**. **Score: 7 of 8**, with need 8 (`TOMLDecodeError`) still REFUTED — **0** occurrences across the whole corpus, unreachable by any index, and fixable only by a registry SCOPE extension.

- **Two of the seven are answered by a POINTER, and the gate says so rather than pretending otherwise.** `"rank of a matrix"` → **rank 2** and `"the exact rational type"` → **rank 5**, but in both cases the returned row is not itself the answer: **0** registered op names contain `rank` (`QMat.rank` is a carrier METHOD, and `describe()['tools']['covers']` says the registry indexes module-level ops only), and the exact-rational answer is a MODULE-PATH correction carried in `example.worked` import lines. `qmat.rank` occurs in **7 of 588** frames and a `k=25` search returns **6 of those 7**. So `test_the_retrieval_corpus_is_answered` asserts *the answer-bearing row is returned*, not *rank 1* — asserting the ordinal there would be asserting a property of one authored paragraph, and it would break on the next prose edit.

- **⚠️ EVERY RANK ABOVE IS IN-SAMPLE.** The scorer was measured against these same queries; the defensible claim is *"the mechanism composes from shipped ops and returns the target at all"*, not the ordinal. **A held-out query set is required before any of these numbers is defended as a quality measurement — that is the first follow-on.** One design prediction did **not** reproduce and is recorded rather than smoothed over, per `[[user_stance_co_equal_dual_construction_is_a_consistency_oracle]]` (the disagreement IS the finding): *"`QMat` ranks #1 in the union basis for 'exact rank of a matrix'"* — it lands at **rank 52 of 588** here, and reaches **rank 2** only under `scope="carriers"`. The likely structural cause is that the scorer has **no document-length normalisation**, so the 29 short carrier frames systematically lose to long op frames. That is a textbook fix and it is deliberately NOT applied here: tuning it against the same 8 queries it would be scored on is exactly the in-sample trap, so it is queued behind the held-out set.

- **THE INDEX SHIPS INSIDE THE CORPUS IT SEARCHES, and that is not free.** Two self-reference defects were found and fixed BY MEASUREMENT during this rc, both invisible to any gate that existed beforehand. (1) The first draft's worked example re-quoted its whole call transcript in `example.output` as well as `example.worked`; because the frame indexes each example sub-key separately, that tripled the term frequency of the demonstration queries inside this op's own row and **displaced `srmech.math.cyclic.gcd` from rank 1 to rank 2 for "greatest common divisor"**. Fixed by holding the field convention strictly — `worked` carries the calls, `output` carries what they returned — which restored `gcd` to rank 1 and dropped this op out of the top 25 for 5 of 8 corpus queries. (2) The example then demonstrated the empty-result case with a literal nonsense token, which **made that token real** and the documented `-> ()` false; the suite's own absence guard caught it. The general rule, now recorded in both the example and the test: an op whose documentation lives in the corpus it searches can never publish a literal never-matches token, so the gate DERIVES its control tokens at run time, after the corpus exists.

- **Count-pin sweep, 556 → 559: 74 pins across 67 files** (73 asserts + `EXPECTED_N`), the precedented sweep from rc383/384/386/387/390/398/399. There is no owner-side dodge — `get_tool_schema()` returns `srmech_tools + profile_tools` at `tool_schema.py:641`, so every pin moves on any real registration. rc410's "don't sweep" conclusion stands for rc410 and does not apply here, because this rc actually changes the count. **Seven PROSE occurrences were de-cardinalised rather than bumped** (`{'srmech': N}`, "every registered entry", "the whole registry"), continuing rc409's removal of hard-coded cardinals from shipped text; five others are explicitly DATED measurements ("measured at rc406", "measured on rc408") that remain correct as written and were left alone. Read individually, never batch-converted.

- **Two shared-source gates had to BOTH be fed, which is the argument for them being single-sourced.** `ToolSchema` and `SearchResult` are introspection records, not operand carriers (the `Run` shape), so both join `tests/coercion_boundary.NON_CARRIER_CLASSES`. It took both gates to find them: the rc205 declared-type ratchet reads the ToolEntry `returns.type` and saw only `ToolSchema`; the rc363 use-derivation gate reads the SOURCE annotation and saw only `SearchResult`. Either alone would have left the other unexempted and the tree red.

- **Four hard-coded cardinals that rc411 itself wrote into SHIPPING prose were struck, and one of them was already false on arrival.** Found by applying the round-2 lesson properly — sweeping the whole tree for every pin this rc moved, rather than only the files that had failed. (a) `search`'s summary said *"Ranks the union of the **556-row** verb registry and the 29-row carrier registry"* — in the very rc that took the verb registry to **559**, and it shipped in the wheel AND in the compiled C registry table. (b, c) `search`'s explanation cited *"6901 tokens that appear only in prose"* and *"~2,850 characters per op"*. Both were lifted from the design brief and **neither was ever reproduced here** — the more serious class, because they read as measurements and had no witness, which is what `[[feedback_computational_provenance_discipline]]` exists to prevent. Replaced with the qualitative claims the argument actually rested on. (d) `get_tool_schema`'s summary said *"matched 0 of 556 entries"* → *"matched NO registered entry"*; the `0 of` is load-bearing, the 556 was context that drifts. The peer sentence in `_register_index_tools`'s DOCSTRING is deliberately LEFT as "0 of 556" — it is scoped by "Before this", it is a genuine dated measurement of the pre-rc411 state, and unlike a ToolEntry summary it is emitted into neither the C registry nor the wheel's introspect surface.

  Regenerated with `tools/regen_all.py --accept-seed-drift`, which is the SANCTIONED path and not a way past the guard: `gen_tool_docs` refuses to overwrite prose it cannot re-derive, and its own docstring sets the rule — *"Editing an EXISTING curated entry still costs one `--accept-seed-drift`, and that is the correct price: the author is replacing authored text and should say so once."* The guard was confirmed to have fired for that reason and no other (the curated `explanation` was verified present and intact, 2,718 chars) before the flag was used. **Re-measured a THIRD time: all 8 ranks unchanged, witness `4a0405d2…` → `e28cceed…`.** Three independent content edits have now left the ranking identical — the only out-of-sample evidence this in-sample result has.

- **Three ratchets fired on the first real CI round and all three were the code's fault, not the gate's.** No ceiling was raised. (a) **`test_selfhosting_import_ban`** — `search.py` did `import json as _json`, taking the stdlib ledger 29 → 30 against a DOWN-ONLY ceiling. `srmech._json` could not serve it: that front door is the **READ half only**, and `json.dumps` is deliberately not self-hosted because `srmech_json_write_ws` declines the non-finite floats stdlib emits. The resolution was neither ceiling nor front door — **the call site never needed JSON.** The frame is an input to a substring scan, not a wire format, so it now flattens through a local `_as_text` renderer. That is also the better engineering: `json.dumps` defaults to `ensure_ascii=True`, so it escaped every non-ASCII character into its six-character backslash-u form — the exact-rational glyph became a literal `u211a` token — in a corpus whose prose is full of `ℚ` / `𝕆` / `→`, on top of `{`, `"` and `:` noise no query can match. Verified after: the literal glyphs are present in the frames and **zero** backslash-u escape sequences remain. (b) **`test_worked_examples_execute_rc354`** — the generated ledger was stale by exactly the three new snippets; refreshed with `tools/run_worked_examples.py --only-stale`, all three execute **ok**. (c) **`test_tool_example_input_schema_rc355`** — `zero_param_with_keys` 12 > CEIL 10. The +2 was **verified to be mine** rather than assumed (the failure message's offender sample included pre-existing rows): `get_tool_schema` and `tool_schema_view` each declared `example["input"] = {"(none)": …}`, but `input` is a KWARGS MAP whose keys are parameter names and both take no parameters. The key is simply gone; `worked` alone satisfies the executed-example floor.

- **Re-measured after those content edits, because this index searches itself.** Editing an `example` edits the corpus — the property that displaced `gcd` earlier in this rc — so the corpus was re-run rather than assumed. **All 8 ranks are UNCHANGED** (1/1/1/1/3/5/2/5 as tabulated above, denominator 588). The frame witness DID move (`17754ad4…` → `4a0405d2…`) and the blob shrank 2.15 → 2.14 MB with the build at 46 ms, so the change was real and the ranking was simply robust to it: the JSON punctuation and escape sequences were noise, not signal. That is a small piece of out-of-sample evidence in a result otherwise entirely in-sample.

- **CI: the per-shard guard is raised 25 -> 40 minutes, and this is NOT rc411's defect.** Stated plainly rather than buried, because riding a shared-CI fix in a feature rc without saying whose problem it is would be the dishonest version. The pure-suite's slowest shard was killed at its 25-minute guard, which reported as three red jobs (the shard, plus the two fan-ins that consume all six shard logs and fail for missing input). The control row is what settles authorship — shard 3, four consecutive runs:

  | commit | shard 3 | result |
  |---|---|---|
  | **`main` a963bd46 — no rc411** | **21m18s** | success |
  | rc411 50a6acec8 | 21m09s | success |
  | rc411 f51e2bcf4 | 21m26s | success |
  | rc411 7ea15a035 | **30m** | KILLED at the guard |

  The slowest shard is a **21-minute** shard **on main**, so 25 was ~17% headroom, not the "generous" margin its comment claimed. rc411 moves it by **0-17 s** — inside run-to-run noise — and its three new ops were measured DIRECTLY in the exhaustive per-op MCP smoke at **~1 s** total (`get_tool_schema` 555 ms, `tool_schema_view` 306 ms, `search` 177 ms; the two registry-returning ops each serialise ~2.5 MB). The raise rides here because rc411 cannot go green without it and the flake will hit any branch.

- **The stale rationale was rewritten, not just the number.** Every premise of the comment above `timeout-minutes` had gone false: "~8-10 min of its 1/6 of the suite" (it is 21m18s), "~25 gives generous headroom" (~17%), and "a false trip still only costs one ~10-min shard" (it costs 21 minutes plus two fan-in jobs). Bumping the digit and leaving the reasoning false is the exact rot this project fights — a stale rationale is how the "five duplicated count-tests" line reached a 12x under-scope. The comment now carries the measured table and cites **`#T1007`** as the note whose SIZING assumption this supersedes; `#T1007`'s split decision stands and is what made the shards measurable at all.

- **UNEXPLAINED, and deliberately not papered over by the raise: rounds 1 and 2 ran ~21m and round 3 hit 30m — a ~43% jump on a diff measured at ~1 s.** Raising the ceiling makes that survivable; it does not diagnose it. Runner noise (these ran immediately after a multi-hour GitHub Actions outage) is plausible and **unproven**. It could not be narrowed: a job killed at the guard uploads no artifact and GitHub serves no log for it, so no per-test evidence exists to separate "uniformly slower" from "hung on one test". That is itself an argument for the raise, since a shard that COMPLETES uploads its `--durations=0` log and the next occurrence is diagnosable where this one was not. If it recurs at 40, variance is not the cause and the number is not the fix.

- **Related, and deliberately NOT acted on here: `#T1051`** already records that the pure-CI floor is five slow ops. A worst shard sitting at **85% of budget on main** is that same problem surfacing as flakiness rather than as duration. Lowering the floor is the real fix; this guard only stops it from being reported as a test failure.

- **Gate: `tests/test_introspect_search_rc411.py`, 15 tests, all failing at rc410 with `ModuleNotFoundError`** — non-vacuity is structural here, not asserted: the module did not exist. It pins the retrieval corpus, the `resolve("winding") is None` control (`resolve` is CORRECT AS IS — this is not a bug report against it), exact-`Q` scores, monotone ranking, empty-not-padded misses, that `reach` strings actually import, and the witness's stability *and* its ability to move. The no-match control asserts its own tokens are absent first, so it cannot decay into a tautology — the first draft used the word "token", which occurs in 19 frames.

## [0.9.0rc410]

**Gates that asked "how many tools?" when they meant "how many tools does srmech OWN?" (`#T1085`).** One shipped product defect plus seven wrong-axis gates, each closed with a test that FAILED BEFORE and passes after. **No op added, removed or renamed; no signature change; `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 12; `describe()["tools"]["total"]` stays 556; zero regenerated C** (proven by `test_regen_all_rc346.py::test_no_generated_file_is_stale`, not assumed).

- **THE HEADLINE IS A NULL, AND IT IS THE POINT: 68 of the 74 registry count assertions are CORRECT and were deliberately NOT touched.** The plan this rc started from was "repoint the ~55 hard-coded `556` count-pins at the owned subtotal". That plan was **measured and abandoned.** The owner census is a single key — `{'srmech': 556}` — and `get_tool_schema()` publishes `srmech_tools + profile_tools`, so with `profile_tools` empty **the owned subtotal EQUALS the total**. Nothing in srmech activates a profile: zero `register_profile_tools` / `load_profile` / `SRMECH_PROFILE` across `conftest.py`'s 862 lines and all 16 workflows. A mechanical repoint would have been **66 files edited, ~74 constants re-derived, zero live defects fixed**, and a real chance of writing a wrong constant that CI *cannot* catch precisely because the right and wrong values coincide today. The honest framing: *"srmech's gates are wrong"* is **FALSE**; *"srmech's gates measure on the wrong AXIS, which breaks any downstream consumer running srmech's suite with a profile loaded"* is **TRUE** — for 8 of 74.

- **THE ONE SILENT WRONG ANSWER: the `.mcpb` bundle attested a third party's tool surface as srmech's own.** Every other item here is a loud test failure; this one escaped the process as a shipped, signed-looking **MPM attestation block** stamped `parser_version: "srmech <version>"`. `_tool_schema_hash()` hashed the unfiltered `get_tool_schema()` and `build_manifest()` took `tool_count` from `len(defs)`, so with any profile active the attestation silently claimed the union. Measured: `tool_count` 556 → **557**, `tool_schema_sha256` `ce41a6c3…` → `f0b2bd5c…`, inside a block still bearing srmech's own parser stamp. Per the MPM discipline the decisive fault is not the count but **re-verifiability**: a consumer re-running that hash against a plain `pip install srmech` could never reproduce it. Both halves now derive from `_owned_tool_schema()`. **The fix is a byte-level no-op on a clean registry** — the two pre-images are identical at **2,457,256 bytes**, asserted directly (byte equality, not hash equality, since the hash is the thing under test) so a "fix" that moved a ratcheted published value could not pass as a bug fix. The four READ-side owner fast-paths had no peer here.

- **`tools[]` is deliberately NOT filtered, and that is pinned in both directions.** The manifest's tool array is the spec-mandated description of what the server actually serves, and it really will serve an active profile's tools; filtering it would make the manifest wrong in the spec's own terms. The attestation is a different claim with a different scope. Both are asserted so a later reader cannot "tidy" one into the other.

- **The op-name SET witness was profile-blind — and no count constant could have fixed it.** `test_op_name_set_witness_rc361.py::_live_names()` read the unfiltered view, so under a profile the **SET** assertion fires *before* the count assertion and reports `added(1): ['<profile>.op']` — a false RENAME. Repointing `EXPECTED_N` alone cannot green it. This is the strongest gate in the tree (it catches same-count renames no count pin can see); `EXPECTED_N` and `EXPECTED_NAME_SET_SHA256` are unchanged.

- **The C-table gate compared an owner-pure artifact against an unfiltered live count.** Post-rc409 `gen_tool_registry.py` REFUSES to emit a profile-owned row, so owner purity is an **enforced write-side invariant** — which makes an unfiltered live count a basis mismatch that reports staleness that does not exist. The count basis is extracted to `_owned_entry_count()` so the new gate measures the shipped expression rather than re-implementing it. `test_generated_table_declares_403_entries` is renamed `…_declares_every_entry`: it never asserted 403 — it has always been dynamic — and the frozen cardinal lived only in the name. (The `~403-tool` claim in the module docstring goes too.)

- **Six gates encoded a PRIOR, WRONG ANSWER to exactly the question this rc asks: they filtered "srmech's own" by NAME PREFIX.** `not t.name.startswith("test.")` is a name-prefix answer to an OWNER question, and it carried justifying docstrings, so it read as already fixed — anyone grepping the literal count would have rewritten the number and left the axis broken. **The prefix was neither necessary nor sufficient**, and measurement is what showed it: the two `test.*` injections in `test_tool_schema.py` are owner `"srmech"` and have been `try`/`finally`-protected since rc409, so they do not leak; while the one genuinely unprotected leak in that file registers owner `"gamma"`, whose names a `test.` prefix does not match at all. The replacement gate is **strict-zero with NO exemption list** — including for the test that documents the pattern, since that is the first hole such a ratchet acquires.

- **One failing test reported as THREE failures, two of them naming unrelated modules.** `test_unregister_profile_tools_removes_all` registered two profile rows and asserted *before* the only call that removes them, with no `try`/`finally`. A genuine failure therefore leaked `gamma.a` / `gamma.b` into the process-global registry and every later count assertion in the same worker read +2. Measured blast radius **3 failed, not 67** — but under CI's `--dist load` the collateral set is worker-dependent, so the noise is not even reproducible. The new gate drives the real test function through its own failure path (rather than re-implementing it) and asserts the registry is clean afterward.

- **Three shipped prose cardinals restating the registry total, one self-refuting in adjacent sentences.** `mcp/_tools.py:432` said *"every one of the 556 entries is advertised … the COUNT is no longer stated here, so it cannot go stale again"* — the sentence before the promise was the violation of it. Plus `introspect/__init__.py:830` and `:1368`. These ship **inside the wheel** and reach users via `describe()` and the MCP tool list; rc409 set the precedent by stripping the same rot from `gen_tool_registry.py:10`. The guard is strict-zero over hand-written `srmech/**/*.py`, exempting the three GENERATED modules — and it **verifies each exemption's file still exists**, so a rename cannot silently widen the exemption into a hole. Its brittleness is named in the docstring rather than papered over: it scans for the *current* total, so a future total colliding with a common constant will make it fail LOUDLY, which is the correct failure mode.

- **The harness, and why it is opt-in.** Nothing in srmech activates a profile, so there was no fail-before state to measure against. `tests/_profile_probe.py` registers one profile-owned `ToolEntry` with snapshot/restore of `_REGISTRY`, as a **non-autouse fixture plus a context manager** — never suite-wide. rc409 deliberately declined a global clean-registry fixture because it would make its own shipped leak DETECTOR vacuous, and that decision stands. Every new assertion is written as `before == during == after` around a live registration, so it cannot be satisfied by an expression that merely stopped measuring; a dedicated non-vacuity test asserts the probe DOES move the unfiltered total, and another pins that the two spellings of "srmech's own" (`by_owner("srmech")` and `RESERVED_OWNERS` membership) still agree — they diverge silently if that frozenset ever grows.

## [0.9.0rc409]

**Facts about the code, written in prose, that nothing computed — and the ADR tree that nothing read (`#T1080`).** Six defects across one class, each closed with a gate that FAILED BEFORE and passes after. **No op added, removed or renamed; no signature change; `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 12; `describe()["tools"]["total"]` stays 556; zero regenerated C** (proven, not assumed — see below).

- **THE ADR TREE HAD NO READER, AND HAD ALREADY DRIFTED.** Census: ZERO tests read `docs/srmech/adr/`; the three greps that mention it are all prose. Twelve ADRs each carry a status on **two** hand-written surfaces that must agree, plus a legend that must define the glyph. **ADR-0010's file header said `🟢 ACCEPTED — execution arc OPEN` while the README index said `🔄 Proposed`** — a live disagreement through the whole rc364→rc408 window. And **`🟢` was used by two ADRs and defined by none**, which is exactly what let the two use it to mean different things. `tests/test_adr_status_coherence_rc409.py` is the first test to read the tree: file header ↔ index row ↔ legend membership, strict-zero. It parses by SEARCHING for `**Status:**` rather than indexing line 3, because `0008`'s sits on line **5** behind a renumbering banner; it reads UTF-8 explicitly and renders glyphs as `U+XXXX` in failures, so a RED result is legible where the console is `cp1252`.

- **`🟢 Implementing` IS NOW THE FIFTH LIFECYCLE STATE — a vocabulary gap, not a relabelling.** The documented lifecycle (`⏳/🔄 → ✅ → 🗑`) had **no state for "decided, being built, shape still being learned"**, so an ADR in that condition had to overclaim `✅` or underclaim `🔄`, and two improvised a glyph instead. Per user direction — *"we wanted to keep it plyable until we knew the shape to fully define it. to prevent many superseeded ADRs"* — a `🟢 Implementing` ADR is **deliberately revisable in place, so it need not be SUPERSEDED merely to change** while its execution arc runs. **ADR-0001** and **ADR-0010** move to it; the legend and the lifecycle line now define it.

- **ADR-0001 no longer says "not yet implemented", because that was false.** `srmech/profile_loader.py` is 989 lines with two test files and two downstream profiles. What is *genuinely* unimplemented is narrower and is now stated as the open question that gates promotion to `✅`: of the six `[profile]` blocks the companion schema declares, the loader validates three and reads **`cli` and `smoke_test` nowhere** — while both real downstream profiles ship a smoke hook srmech never invokes.

- **`"srmech"` was a privileged sentinel that nothing reserved.** `owner == "srmech"` is a DECISION PREDICATE at six shipped sites (the `get_tool_schema()` split; four native fast-path gates), yet `_NAME_PATTERN` (`^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$`) **matches it**, so a profile could legally claim the name. Measured: `unregister_profile_tools("srmech")` returned **556 and left the registry EMPTY**. New `RESERVED_OWNERS` is enforced at BOTH ends — `profile_loader._validate_descriptor` (root cause: the name never enters the system) and `unregister_profile_tools` (defense in depth; it RAISES rather than returning 0, so the calling bug is named rather than silently absorbed). **LATENT, NOT LIVE:** there are ZERO shipped callers — no deactivation path, not an MCP tool, not a CLI route — so nothing in the shipped product wiped its own registry. This closes the **collision** door; the **vacuous-truth** half (`not any(...)` is trivially true on an empty registry, which SELECTS the native path) needs a direct registry-identity check and a rebuilt library to verify, and is explicitly left open. Two comments in `test_tool_schema.py` asserting the exact inverse ("*a no-op for it*", "*can't remove it*") are corrected — neither was an assertion, so nothing would ever have failed on them.

- **Both registry-walking code generators now refuse profile-owned rows.** `c/tools/gen_tool_registry.py` → the compiled-in C table, and — the one easy to miss — `python/tools/gen_tool_docs.py` → `srmech/introspect/_tool_docs.py`, **which ships in the wheel** and is read back by `describe()` and the MCP tool list. The READ side has always enforced this (`tool_schema_view` and three peers refuse the C table when a profile tool is present); the WRITE side enforced it nowhere, so rc409 closes the untouched end of an existing contract. Raises `ToolSchemaValidationError`, not `assert` — a codegen guard must not vanish under `python -O`. **Output is byte-identical and zero C is regenerated**, proven by `test_regen_all_rc346.py::test_no_generated_file_is_stale`, not assumed. Deliberately NOT widened to the other four generators: they read static module tables or TOML from disk and cannot observe a profile.

- **`SRMECH_CATALOG_PATH` was documented and read by nothing.** The real name is `SRMECH_CASCADE_PATH` (`dsl/_catalog.py:76`); the phantom had exactly ONE occurrence tree-wide and never had a reader at any commit. This is the user-facing silent-wrong-answer shape: export the variable, nothing happens, no error, no warning. The new gate is **self-limiting by design** — it checks a name only when the package's own prose calls it an *env-var*, which is 8 tokens rather than the 69 an untargeted `SRMECH_[A-Z_]+` sweep would flag (C status codes, ctypes enum mirrors, compile-time caps — all correct, none needing a reader). Its read-set follows module-constant indirection, and `SRMECH_BUS_SEED` / `SRMECH_BUS_TOTP_WINDOW_NS` are asserted GREEN as live negative controls, because a literal-only scan would report both as false phantoms.

- **The adapter count was stale on three surfaces, one of them public.** `len(ADAPTERS) == 7`; the docstring said "Six" above six bullets, and `python/README.md` said "Six adapters" above a six-row table — **that file is the PyPI long-description**, so the wrong count was on the project page. `substrate_parameterization` now has a bullet and a row. The gate keys on `len(ADAPTERS)`, a live value. **`:29` is deliberately NOT touched and is now guarded AGAINST edits**: *"Notebook §18.3 — five-adapter shared core spec"* is an accurate ATTRIBUTED CITATION (the notebook says "~5 types" and tables exactly five), and "fixing" it to 7 would fabricate a citation. The generative rule this file records: `:3`'s wording is §18.3's own phrase with the attribution stripped — **the cited number stayed correct across two adapter additions; the unattributed paraphrase drifted 5 → 6 → stale at 7.**

- **A COST WAS WRITTEN INTO THE TREE AS A BLOCKER.** `tests/test_profile_loader.py` claimed for many rcs that the entry-point machinery "can't easily be exercised in a unit test without pip-installing a fixture package". **Refuted by execution.** A hand-written `fakeprof-1.0.0.dist-info/` (`METADATA` + `entry_points.txt`) on a `sys.path` directory drives the full real path — discovery → resolve → validate → smoke → cache → `Profile` — with the standard library alone. `tests/test_profile_entrypoint_discovery_rc409.py` covers what had **zero references in `tests/`**: `entry_points(group=…)`, `_enumerate_profiles`, the activation body. Its fixture declares a real bridge surface and asserts `n_assertions > 0`, because **`_run_smoke_test` returns `("passed", "", 0)` for a profile with no bridge and no catalogs** — a minimal fixture passes the gate VACUOUSLY. Negative control included: rename the entry-point group and everything goes quiet. The false docstring is corrected in the same commit.

- **`Task #199` → `` `#T199` `` at 11 live-prose sites, 6 of them in shipped package source.** Topicality adjudicated, not swept: `gh #199` is an unrelated MERGED PR ("ephemerides-spectral 0.9.2 → 0.9.3 PyPI README staleness sweep") while the surrounding prose plainly describes the local task. Converting makes `199` DECIDABLE, which arms the ref guard's strict-zero rule against it in emitted artifacts — measured 0 there before and after, so no cascade. **The two `CHANGELOG.md` sites are deliberately left** to task `#T991`, which owns the ~360-ref changelog sweep: they sit OUTSIDE the `pypi-readme-changelog` markers (so they reach no wheel), they are historical `[0.3.0]` entries, and one shares its line with a bare `Task #198` that individual adjudication has not yet reached.

- **Two `SCAN_ROOTS` declarations added, both because the guard caught them.** `test_ref_notation_emitted_rc348.py`'s meta-test refuses any test that reaches above `python/` without declaring what it reads — it fired on the new ADR gate (`docs/srmech/adr`) and on the codegen guard (`python/tools` + `c/tools`). The ADR directory is watched by `srmech-ref-guard.yml`'s `docs/srmech/**` trigger, not by `srmech-ci`'s narrower one, which is precisely the armed-and-silent gap that meta-test exists to prevent.

## [0.9.0rc408]

**27 ToolEntries hid 35 real parameters of their own callable — the contract was silent about capabilities that shipped (`#T1078`).** Declarations, two new operand types, and the converse ratchet that will keep them honest. **No op added, removed or renamed; no signature change; `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 12**, and **`describe()["tools"]["total"]` stays 556** — verified against a freshly rebuilt `.so`, not assumed.

- **THE DEFECT.** Under *introspect IS the API contract*, an INCOMPLETE declaration is the same severity as a false one; only the failure mode differs — not "calls something that errors" but **"cannot reach a capability that exists"**. The canonical case is the one the user named: `srmech.cascade.the_one` declared `sigma, theta_num, theta_den, terms` while the live signature is `the_one(sigma, theta_num, theta_den=1, terms=24, w=(0,0,0))`. **`w` — the winding triad `(w_saros, w_metonic, w_callippic)`, the three metacycle dials filling the B/H/N ℝ·1 grammar anchors — was absent from the contract** while `One.winding_tower()` / `One.sigma_effective()` demonstrably consume it. All 35 were OPTIONAL (every one had a default), so no caller was ever broken; the capability was simply invisible.

- **WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT.** Nine test files call `inspect.signature` and **none** of them also reads `tool_schema`. `tests/test_mcp.py::test_schema_signature_alignment_no_drift` has guarded ONE direction since v0.5.0rc13 — every DECLARED param must be bindable, so no tool is uncallable. The converse was ungated. `tests/test_declared_param_completeness_rc408.py` closes it: measured against the un-drained tree first, **before 27 entries / 35 parameters → after 0**. Strict-zero, no CEIL, no allowlist.

- **`VAR_KEYWORD` is deliberately NOT required, and that is a finding, not a softening.** The first draft of the gate demanded it and reported 28/36. The extra was `op_provenance.reproject(**rung_override)` — an OPEN KEYWORD NAMESPACE whose keys are validated against `spec.rung_keys`, so a literal key named `rung_override` would be REJECTED. Declaring it by name would have manufactured exactly the declared-but-not-real defect the rc13 gate exists to catch, and the capability is already reachable through the declared `overrides=` dict. `VAR_POSITIONAL` **is** required (the rc10 convention gives that slot a clean name; all three cases already declared it).

- **THE `progress` DECISION — declared, not hidden.** §101 / ABI-v6 `progress` was 11 of the 35, and `tests/test_genome_progress.py::test_progress_is_never_a_tool_wire_param` actively asserted it appeared in NO entry's `parameters`. That guard protected the right thing — a callable must never be advertised as a value a JSON-RPC client can send — by the wrong mechanism: it enforced it by keeping the parameter out of the contract entirely, hiding it from the in-process Python callers who CAN pass it. For a multi-hour genome encode the tick is the ONLY channel that reports working status or accepts a cancel; it fires INLINE on the encode thread (zero concurrency, MCU-safe, no RTOS), is OFF by default, and its `done`/`total` are EXACT integer cardinalities (Class-N — the library never divides, so it is **not** a percentage). It is now DECLARED, never REQUIRED, and typed so no client can fill it.

- **TWO NEW OPERAND TYPES, and the first `"null"` rows in the lexicon.** `host_callable` (the §101 tick; `integrate`'s `compatible` predicate) and `host_rng` (`polar_random`'s Generator) publish JSON-schema **`"null"`** — the only value a client may legally send is *absent*, which `coerce_param` already passes through and which runs the op with the affordance disabled. Publishing the generic `callable` type was rejected: it maps to `"string"` (the "rides as a resolvable NAME" pattern), and a `progress` tick has no such registry, so a schema-obedient client would have been told to send text that the op then CALLS — a guaranteed `TypeError` in a tool that works today. **Telling a client to send a value that cannot work is worse than telling it to send nothing.** Same argument rc362 made for naming the in-process `Qalg` arm: the type string is the operand declaration, not only the wire contract.

- **Two silent JSON-schema degradations fixed in passing.** `tuple[int, int, int]` (the winding triad) had neither coercer nor lexicon row and would have published `"string"` for three ints. `Sequence[tuple]` has had a coercer since v0.7.5rc134 but never a lexicon row, so `genome.chromosome` `genes` and the plasmid `chromosomes` have been publishing `"string"` for a plainly nested ARRAY — the ADR-0012 §4.2 silent-degradation row, found while declaring `genome.genome` `chromosomes` against the same type.

- **Two shipped prose falsehoods this rc created, and fixed in the same commit.** `integrate`'s summary ended *"so it is not in the parameter list"* and `polar_random`'s comment said *"the schema exposes only the serialisable path"*. Both became false the moment the parameters were declared; both are corrected to state the declared-but-unfillable contract. That prose ships — it is emitted into `_tool_docs.py` and byte-mirrored into the compiled `srmech_tool_registry.c`.

- **Ledger movement.** `CEIL_EXAMPLE_INPUT_KEY_MISMATCH["mixed_param_and_prose"]` **15 → 14** — `genome_append`'s example already called the op with a `catalog` key, but the entry did not DECLARE `catalog`, so a real working call read as "mixing parameter names with prose". Lowered in the SAME commit as the drain. **No census pin moved**: the rc407 `host_glue` 21 / `_TOTAL_NON_COMPUTE` 212 populations count public callables, not parameters, and are inert to this change.

**A method deleted 44 rcs ago was still advertised as callable in the shipped registry, because the gate that would have caught it could not see references of that shape (`#T1076`).** Prose, tests and one MCP field. **No op added, removed or renamed; no signature change; `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 12**, and **`describe()["tools"]["total"]` stays 556** — verified against a freshly rebuilt `.so`, not assumed.

It was still cited as LIVE in the `summary` AND `explanation` of `srmech.cascade.the_one` — `mcp_callable`, inside the wheel, and byte-mirrored into the compiled `srmech_tool_registry.c` — while `tests/test_mat_carrier_rc69.py::test_no_to_numpy_attribute` asserted in the same tree that the name was gone. `Mat.buffers` in `mat_solve`'s summary resolved nowhere at all; the attribute is `Mat.buffer`, which both same-shape siblings spell correctly.
