## [0.9.0rc397]

**CORRECTLY-ROUNDED, libm-free TOML float parse — the last gap to fully self-host float TOML in C (`#T1066`).** srmech's C `srmech_toml` parser decoded decimal floats two ways that both lost the last bit: `toml_str_to_f64` accumulated `mant*10 + d` then divided by `10^fracdigits` (TWO roundings), and `toml_apply_exponent` applied the exponent by a per-step `*=10.0` / `/=10.0` LOOP (one rounding PER exponent step, so `1e-300` compounded 300 divisions). Measured over a 3025-token battery+fuzz against Python's `float(str)`: **1941 tokens were bit-different — up to 24 ULP off** — and `5e-324` and other denormals were rejected outright by the old `exp > 308` guard. That is why `toml_loads_c` DECLINED every float-bearing document and rode the stdlib parser. rc397 replaces the accumulator with a **correctly-rounded** (IEEE round-to-nearest-even), libm-free parse; **now all 3025 battery+fuzz tokens are bit-identical to `float(str)` / `tomllib`, so float TOML self-hosts on the C parser and no longer declines.** Pure C-side fix — all new functions are `static`, so **`SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 11**, no codegen / registry / tool-count ripple, and `describe()["tools"]["total"]` is UNCHANGED.

- **Two paths, both in `c/src/srmech_toml.c`.** The token is parsed into a sign, an integer significand `D` (point removed, leading + trailing zeros trimmed) and a net base-10 exponent `E`, so value = ±D·10^E. **Clinger fast path** (Clinger, PLDI 1990, "How to Read Floating Point Numbers Accurately"): when `D ≤ 2^53` AND `|E| ≤ 22`, a SINGLE IEEE multiply/divide by an exact compile-time `10^0..10^22` is provably correctly rounded — return `(double)D * pow10[E]` (or `/ pow10[-E]`). **Exact tail** (everything else — many-digit significands, `|E| > 22`, denormals): the correctly-rounded double of the exact rational `D·10^E` is computed over **`srmech_bigint`** (rc256; num/den, one big divmod, round-to-nearest-EVEN on the halfway tie), assembling the IEEE bit pattern directly so normals, denormals, underflow (→ ±0) and overflow (→ ±inf, matching `float('1e400')`) all round exactly. No malloc (fixed caller-owned limb storage — JPL Rule 3), no libm, no goto, no recursion; JPL Power-of-Ten ratchet unchanged (each new helper carries ≥2 asserts, ≤60 lines).
- **The Python float-decline is REMOVED.** `_native.toml_loads_c` walked the parse tree and returned `None` on any FLOAT node (the `_toml_tree_has_float` guard) precisely because the C float was not bit-exact; that function and its call are DELETED. A float-bearing document now self-hosts through the C parser and is bit-identical to `tomllib`. `srmech._toml.loads` and `describe()` are unaffected; `tomllib` / `tomli` remains the pure / Pyodide floor.
- **Test boundaries flipped to full self-hosting.** `test_toml_selfhost_parity_rc391.py` (`test_c_path_parity` → a decline is now a regression; `test_declines_are_exactly_the_float_docs` → `test_no_corpus_doc_declines`; `test_float_doc_rides_stdlib` → `test_float_doc_self_hosts`) and `test_dsl_catalog_selfhost_rc392.py` (`best_rational_signed.toml`'s `dead_band = 1e-12` now self-hosts; `_EXPECTED_CASCADE_DECLINE` → `_FLOAT_BEARING_CASCADE`) drop the one documented float decline. `test_descriptor_hash_selfhost_rc393.py` / `test_profile_toolschema_selfhost_rc394.py` were float-free (their empty decline-sets already hold, unchanged).
- **`tests/test_toml_float_correct_round_rc397.py` (NEW).** The bit-exactness gate: a hand-picked battery (0.1/0.2/0.3, min normal, min/next denormal, DBL_MAX, `1e-300`, 2^53±1, all-fraction + 40-digit significands) plus 3000 deterministic fuzz tokens (fixed seed = computational provenance), each asserted `toml_loads_c('x = '+tok)['x']` == `float(tok)` BIT-FOR-BIT via `struct.pack('<d', …)` (the only comparison that separates -0.0 from 0.0 and a 1-ULP miss from a hit); plus the overflow→±inf / underflow→±0 boundary and the front-door `_toml.loads` parity. Native-guarded via `require_native("srmech_toml_parse")`; numpy-free. **`c/test/test_srmech_toml_float.c` (NEW)** is the bare-C-HOST peer — parser output vs the host compiler's own correctly-rounded double literals — wired into the CMake ctest matrix (`-Werror`/`/WX` on Linux/macOS/Windows).

## [0.9.0rc396]

**WEYL CLOCK + SHIFT — close the ring position/momentum loop with the fenced position `x̂` (`#T1031`, position-operator half).** srmech already ships the momentum GENERATOR `lattice_momentum` (`p̂ = -i∂_x`); this adds its two missing partners on a periodic lattice. Position on a ring is NOT a naive linear `x̂ = diag(k·dx)` — that is multi-valued (it jumps at the seam `n−1 → 0`) and physically wrong — so the topology-respecting position is the **Weyl clock** `clock_operator(n)` = `U = diag(ω^k)`, `ω = e^{2πi/n}` (single-valued: the phase wraps once and closes). Its partner **`shift_operator(n)`** = `V` (the cyclic one-site translation `V|k⟩ = |k+1 mod n⟩`) is the group-level momentum. They obey the **Weyl relation** `U V = ω V U` — the compact, finite-dimensional form of the canonical `[x̂, p̂] = iℏ` (which cannot literally hold on a finite ring). Both are pure-Python constructions returning a complex `Mat` (mirroring `lattice_momentum`), so **no new C symbol → `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 11**. Canonical SSoT: Schwinger, J. (1960) "Unitary Operator Bases", *Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA* **46**, 570–579; Weyl, H. (1931) *The Theory of Groups and Quantum Mechanics*. **`describe()["tools"]["total"]` 544 → 546** (+2). (The 3 stale cosmos-ref cleanup remains a SEPARATE task.)

- **BIT-EXACT roots of unity where the phase is a whole quarter-turn.** `clock_operator` builds each `ω^k` exactly (`{1, i, −1, −i}`) whenever `4k ≡ 0 (mod n)` — a pure Class-C reorientation with no transcendental part — and only a genuine sub-quarter angle hits the Class-N `cexp` Euler cascade at the float64 boundary (the same boundary `lattice_momentum`'s `sin(2πk/n)` spectrum sits on). So `n = 2` and `n = 4` are bit-exact (`U = diag(1,−1)`, `diag(1,i,−1,−i)`), while `n = 3, 5` and the odd `n = 8` entries are machine-ε. No `abs()`; the quarter-turn signs ARE the Class-K pin-slot baked into the constant table.
- **n = 2 IS Pauli, and `Y = iXZ` falls out for free.** `clock_operator(2) == σ_z`, `shift_operator(2) == σ_x`, and the chiral third `i·(shift·clock) == σ_y` — all bit-exact against `pauli_matrices()`. No separate `Y` op is added; the chirality third is DERIVED from the multiply already shipped. Pinned in `tests/test_weyl_clock_shift_rc396.py`: the Weyl relation to machine-ε for `n ∈ {2,3,4,5,8}` (EXACT at 2/4); a ω̄-convention non-vacuity guard (the mirror convention must FAIL for complex ω); unitarity; and `U**n = V**n = I` — with `V·Vᴴ = I` and `V**n = I` bit-exact for EVERY n since `V` is an integer permutation. numpy-free.
- **Disclosure-note repair.** `srmech/physics/qm/__init__.py` said "no position operator `x̂` ships … it needs its own fenced operator, not a naive diagonal." Updated: the fenced position now ships as the Weyl clock (single-valued phase on the ring) paired with the shift, and `[x̂, p̂]` IS expressible on this surface — in its correct compact form, the Weyl relation `U V = ω V U`.
- **Rosetta:** two new `composition_of_c` rows (the `lattice_momentum` bucket) — the clock composes the C-dispatched Class-N `cexp` + exact literals, the shift is an exact integer construction. Full ripple ×2: 2 ToolEntries, 2 curated worked-example families (real WSL2 captures, `n`-keyed), the 6 derived-order regenerations, the op-name-set manifest + digest, and every count-pin site bumped 544 → 546.

## [0.9.0rc395]

**GENERAL ZERO-DIVISOR WITNESS — REPLACE the hardwired dim-16 sedenion op with the dim-general `cd_zero_divisor_witness(dim)` / `cd_zero_divisor_witnesses(dim)` (`#T1000`).** The no-legacy discipline applies pre-1.0: keeping `sedenion_zero_divisor_witness()` beside a general op is cruft, so it is REMOVED, not kept additively. The two successors exhibit the whole Hurwitz wall at any power-of-two rung `16 ≤ dim ≤ CD_MAX_DIM` (256), not one point of it — `cd_zero_divisor_witness(dim)` returns the FIRST basis-pair zero divisor `(e_i + e_j)(e_k + s·e_l) = 0` (deterministic order), and `cd_zero_divisor_witnesses(dim)` returns the COMPLETE set (exactly **168** at dim 16). Both are **`composition_of_c`**: they solve the `i ⊕ j ⊕ k ⊕ l = 0` support system with the C-dispatched Class-I `gf_rref` and read the second-factor sign DETERMINED (never searched, never `abs()` — a Class-K pin re-applied by Class-C) off the C-dispatched `cd_basis_product` cocycle. Cost is O(dim³) — tractable to 256, NOT the exponential product sweep. Empty / `None` for every `dim ≤ 8` (ℝ / ℂ / ℍ / 𝕆 are division algebras). **`describe()["tools"]["total"]` 543 → 544** (−1 sedenion, +2 general).

- **CONTINUITY.** `cd_zero_divisor_witness(16)` returns the IDENTICAL payload the removed op returned — `x = e1 + e10`, `y = e4 − e15`, both norm 2, product exactly zero. The dim-16 answer is unchanged; only the name and the generality moved. Pinned in `tests/test_zero_divisor_general_rc395.py`.
- **ABI 10 → 11 (a REMOVED C export).** The dedicated dim-16 brute-force export `srmech_cd_zero_divisor_witness` (and its static helper `cd_pair_product_is_zero`) is REMOVED from `c/include/srmech.h` + `c/src/srmech_cayley_dickson.c` — it predated the GF(2) route and is subsumed by the `composition_of_c` successors (no dedicated C symbol). A removed export produces no symptom other than a version mismatch, so by standing policy it bumps `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` 10 → 11 in lockstep with `EXPECTED_ABI_VERSION` in `srmech/_native/__init__.py`. The paired ctypes binding + the `cd_zero_divisor_witness_c()` wrapper are dropped, and `has_native_cd_closure()` no longer gates on the removed symbol. `GENOME_FORMAT_VERSION` unchanged. Verified no other C caller (grep of the whole `c/` tree: only the prototype + its definition referenced it).
- **CO-EQUAL DUAL-CONSTRUCTION consistency oracle.** `tests/test_zero_divisor_general_rc395.py` asserts the shipped op's witness SET equals an INDEPENDENT recompute driven straight through the raw C symbols `srmech_gf_rref` + `srmech_cd_basis_product` at dim 16 AND dim 32 (native-guarded via `tests._native_gate.require_native`), plus pure-path == native-path; a set mismatch is the finding, never papered over. Also pinned: the 168-at-16 set equals rc350's independent GF(2) criterion; the pinned `(1, 10, 4, 15, -1)` first witness; empty at dim 4/8; a shape-check at dim 64; and a no-false-negative brute-force product oracle on a deterministic `(i, j)` subset.
- **SCOPE-PIN inverted, not deleted.** `test_algebra_inertia_rc349.py`'s "not a general isotropy surface" pin is rewritten: the op IS dim-general now (it takes a `dim` argument), but it enumerates only the DISCRETE basis-pair witnesses (168 at dim 16), not the rational isotropy cone of the norm form — generality over RUNGS is not generality over a rung's isotropy surface. The math content is preserved.
- **Rosetta:** the sedenion `c_dispatched` row is replaced by two `composition_of_c` rows (joining `gf_solve` / `left_mult_kernel`). Full ripple ×2: 2 ToolEntries, 2 curated worked-example families (real WSL2 captures, `dim`-keyed), the 6 derived-order regenerations, the op-name-set manifest + digest, and every count-pin site bumped 543 → 544.

**SELF-HOST THE C TOML PARSER — repoint `profile_loader` + `introspect/tool_schema` onto `srmech._toml`; the `#T907` migration is COMPLETE, slice 4 (final).** rc391 landed srmech's internal TOML front door (`srmech._toml.loads` / `load` — native `srmech_toml` parser first, `tomllib` / `tomli` floor); rc392 repointed the two DSL catalog loaders; rc393 repointed the two AMSC loaders + the descriptor-hash gate. - **`srmech.profile_loader._read_descriptor`** (reads a profile's `srmech_profile.toml`) AND **`srmech.profile_loader._read_smoke_cache`** (reads a smoke-test cache TOML) now parse via `srmech._toml.load`. The module-top `tomllib` alias is DELIBERATELY RETAINED: `_read_smoke_cache`'s `except (OSError, tomllib.TOMLDecodeError)` clause (a malformed cache → cache MISS) needs the exception type, and `srmech._toml.load` rides `tomllib` on a malformed doc and re-raises that exact type, so the error contract is unchanged.
- **`srmech.introspect.tool_schema.load_extension_file`** (reads a profile's tool-schema extension TOML — `[[tools]]` + `[[tools.parameters]]`) repointed identically. It has NO `TOMLDecodeError` catch, so its `tomllib` alias + the now-unused `import sys` (whose only use was the stdlib version-guard) are removed entirely.

## [0.9.0rc391]

**SELF-HOST THE C TOML PARSER — srmech's own internal TOML loader over a DIRECT `srmech_toml` binding, `#T907` slice 1.** srmech's C library has shipped its own malloc-free `srmech_toml` parser for a long time, but Python only ever reached it INDIRECTLY through the DSL chain-spec JSON bridge; every descriptor / catalog read still went through the external `tomllib` / `tomli`. This rc binds the raw parser DIRECTLY (Route A — the same self-hosting move `sha256_bytes` makes for hashing) and lands srmech's own internal TOML front door. **No new registered op, no ToolEntry, no introspect / MCP / Rosetta / worked-example surface — this is srmech PLUMBING, not one of the 14 A-N compute capabilities. `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 10 (additive symbol only); `describe()["tools"]["total"]` is UNCHANGED.** NO consumer repoint this rc — the six stdlib-only modules stay on stdlib; rc2–rc4 repoint them onto the loader once the corpus-wide parity oracle is proven green.

- **New C symbol `srmech_toml_parse_arena_bytes(size_t src_len) -> size_t`** (`c/src/srmech_toml.c` + `c/include/srmech.h`). Returns a SAFE upper bound for the `ws` parse arena, removing the guess-and-grow hazard a ctypes / C-only caller would otherwise carry (there was no arena sizer for the raw parser, unlike the DSL bridge). The bound is the same proven-safe parse-only budget `srmech_dsl_toml_chain_to_json` already carves internally (`256·len + 64 KiB`), which dwarfs the ~56 bytes/source-byte a densest-possible `a=1` corpus consumes. JPL-clean (≤60-line, ≥2 asserts, no malloc/goto/multi-line-macro); wired into `make test` via a new `c/test/test_srmech_toml_arena.c` (sizer shape + exact-arena round-trip + dense-keys headroom).
- **`srmech._native` binds `srmech_toml_parse` / `srmech_toml_table_get` / `srmech_toml_parse_arena_bytes` directly.** The tagged-union `srmech_toml_value_t` is mirrored as a ctypes `Structure`/`Union` (STRING/INT/FLOAT/BOOL/ARRAY/TABLE), a recursive walker `_toml_tree_to_dict` turns the parse tree into a Python dict, and `toml_loads_c(text)` sizes the arena, parses, doubles-and-retries on `SRMECH_ERR_OVERFLOW` (belt-and-suspenders), and returns `None` on `SRMECH_ERR_BAD_INPUT` (DECLINE → caller rides tomllib). String VALUES are read by `str.len` (not NUL-terminated truncation) so an embedded-NUL value survives. The arena is held alive across the whole walk — every returned pointer aliases into it.
- **The float-fidelity boundary — a real finding from the oracle.** The plan assumed the descriptor corpus was float-free; it is NOT — `cascade_catalog/best_rational_signed.toml` carries `dead_band = 1e-12`, and srmech_toml's libm-free decimal→double accumulator lands it 1 ULP off (`1.0000000000000002e-12`) tomllib's correctly-rounded value. A self-hosting loader that silently returned a DIFFERENT float would be worse than one that declines, so `toml_loads_c` DECLINES any float-bearing document (it rides the bit-exact stdlib parse) and self-hosts everything else. This is the same fidelity boundary the DSL bridge's `%.17g` float path already carries, and it keeps a future attested descriptor's `descriptor_hash` identical native-vs-pure. (A correctly-rounded libm-free `strtod` in C is a separate, later undertaking, not this slice.)
- **`srmech/_toml.py` (NEW) — the internal front door.** `loads(text) -> dict` / `load(fp) -> dict`, native-first (`toml_loads_c` when the lib exposes `srmech_toml_parse`), `tomllib` (3.11+) / `tomli` (3.10) fallback otherwise. The fallback is MANDATORY and never removed: the C library is absent on pure / Pyodide wheels, so stdlib stays the correctness floor there (the `tomli` conditional dep is retained).
- **The co-equal dual-construction consistency oracle — `tests/test_toml_selfhost_parity_rc391.py`.** For every `.toml` under `srmech/` (attested descriptors, cascade / class catalogs, alias catalogs, worked instances) it asserts `toml_loads_c(text) == tomllib.loads(text)` AND `_toml.loads(text) == tomllib.loads(text)`. Any C-parser DECLINE is an EXPLICIT skip with reason, and — because the corpus is NOT float-free — the coverage test pins the decline boundary EXACTLY: every declined doc contains a float, and NO float-free doc declines (so the only thing the native path gives up is float fidelity, never integer / string / table grammar). Native-guarded with `require_native("srmech_toml_parse")` (the `#T843` / `#T1004` contract — SKIPS pure-by-design in the no-native shard, FAILS if native is missing unexpectedly; never a bare `assert HAS_NATIVE`). Plus type-fidelity spot checks (int stays int not float / bool; bool stays bool), the explicit `1e-12` float-rides-stdlib case, and a no-corpus-int-exceeds-int64 pin. numpy-free.

## [0.9.0rc390]

**THE ORDER-CARRYING OCTONION ASSOCIATIVITY READ — `srmech.biology.genome.split_defect`, `#T961`.** The COMPLEMENT of the order-BLIND `genome_octonion_associator` (rc325): the associator compares the fully-LEFT and fully-RIGHT folds of the same ordered turns — a PERMUTATION-INVARIANT, bracketing-only read that is identically 0 at n=3,4. `split_defect` instead takes ONE word of octonion basis letters and RE-BRACKETS it at a single split `k`: `split_defect(word, k) = signbit(fold(word)) ^ signbit(fold(word[:k]) · fold(word[k:]))`, where `fold` is the LEFT-fold octonion product and `·` is `oct_mult`. Because the 𝕆 index lane is ⊕-associative, the two bracketings ALWAYS share the index and differ ONLY in the center sign bit — the returned 0/1. It ships **co-equal Python + C** (`srmech_split_defect`, `c_dispatched`) — the pure `oct_mult` fold and the C peer are byte-identical over all 196608 (n≤3, k) cases, which IS the acceptance oracle. Additive symbol → `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays **10**. No `abs()` (sign is the Class-K pin bit `b>>3`, re-applied by the Class-C XOR); no stdlib `fractions` (integer byte ops).

- **`srmech.biology.genome.split_defect(word, k)`** (Class M ∘ K ∘ C; `c_dispatched`) → the 0/1 order-carrying associator-defect bit. It CAN fire only when BOTH split sides have length ≥ 2 (a length-1 side folds trivially), so a middle split needs `n ≥ 4`. **The prefix `fold(word[:k])` is the same growing-prefix accumulation a reader already walking prefixes gets for free** (the shape of rc336 `best_rational(with_path=)` / `continued_fraction_convergents`); no such octonion prefix-walker exists in the tree today, so the op computes the two brackets directly — noted for a future prefix-carrying reader to reuse.
- **The census (the false-green catcher — this is the whole point).** `split_defect == 0` is AMBIGUOUS: EITHER associative OR too short at `k`. The ratchet pins BOTH the associative zeros AND the non-associative nonzeros, all reproduced EXACTLY through the shipped ops (`oct_mult` / `cd_basis_product` / `algebra_table`): **ℂ 0/1 · ℍ 0/81 · 𝕆 1008/2401 · 𝕊 18480/32760** (ℂ/ℍ/𝕆 = all length-4 words at k=2; 𝕊 = distinct-letter length-4 words, the non-division rung). It is **0 inside every Fano frame (0/567** — a purely CROSS-FRAME quantity, each frame a quaternion subalgebra) and **gauge-invariant under all 2⁷=128 per-generator sign re-gaugings** (the 1344 octonion basis automorphisms are the gauge's other half — cited).
- **The NON-DISCRIMINATOR pin (it reads associativity, NOT division).** **Split-octonions give the IDENTICAL 1008/2401** for every split-gamma configuration (`algebra_table` with a +1 at any doubling rung) — split-𝕆 is non-division but equally non-associative. And the associative **Cl(0,7) control** — 7 anticommuting generators (matching 𝕆 on alphabet size + anticommutativity) but ASSOCIATIVE — gives identically **0**. So the ONLY thing `split_defect` measures is associativity.
- **⚠️ Two spec gaps from the ephemeral brief, resolved honestly.** (1) The brief's "threshold is FIVE letters at a middle split" is **off-by-one against its OWN 1008/2401 count, which is n=4** — the honest firing threshold is "both split sides length ≥ 2" (a middle split fires from n=4). The ratchet still shows a ≥5-letter FIRING case and a `k`-too-short NON-firing case (the same non-associative triple `(e1,e2,e4)` fires at k=1 but is 0 at k=2). (2) The brief's Cl(0,7) total **0/595448** (= 248·2401) uses a larger enumeration **not reproducible through a clean 7-generator word count**; the control is delivered at the 𝕆-matched n=4-all enumeration (**0/2401**), which carries the control's whole MEANING (associative ⇒ 0). `split_defect` is also NOT associated with `inertia_signature` (permutation test p≈0.5893 — cited from the brief, not recomputed).
- **Complementary, not redundant, with `hypercomplex_perspectives`** (disjoint domains: perspectives raises at dim 8; `split_defect` is 0 at dims ≤ 4 and non-trivial from 8). The maintainer's ship-both decision stands.
- **Computational provenance.** `notes/split_defect_rc390.py` → `.ndjson` reproduces all eight findings THROUGH the shipped ops (census, split-𝕆 non-discriminator, Cl(0,7) control, Fano-frame zero, 128-gauge invariance, threshold visibility, the C-vs-pure byte-identity oracle, the inertia citation). No `abs()`; no stdlib `fractions`.
- **Registration + counts.** One `ToolEntry` (mirroring the octonion peers, with a `smoke_test_hint` real-arg example keyed by param names `{"word":…, "k":…}`); one `c_dispatched` row in `rosetta_classification.ndjson` (+ the `_c_claims.py` `srmech_split_defect` claim, auto-derived by `gen_c_claims`); one curated worked example in `_tool_docs_curated.py` (real WSL2 numpy-absent capture) + refreshed `tests/worked_examples_result.ndjson`; `describe()["tools"]["total"]` **542 → 543** (the op-total pins across the test suite bumped, plus the `registered_op_names.txt` witness manifest + its digest + `EXPECTED_N`). Generated artifacts (`_tool_docs.py`, the four C registries) regenerated via `tools/regen_all.py`.

## [0.9.0rc388]

**THE ℍ-TORSOR OF A SEAM COSET — `srmech.math.octonion.oct_torsor_act` + `oct_torsor_div`, `#T963`.** The octonion `oct_mult` (rc324) read as a GROUP ACTION. A quaternion subalgebra `H = {±e₀..±e₃}` of 𝕆 and its set-complement — the seam coset `T = H·e = {±e₄..±e₇}` (8 signed bytes) — form a PRINCIPAL right torsor: `T` has no distinguished identity, yet `H` acts on it **simply transitively**. The action is literally `oct_mult(t, g)`; the division is `oct_mult(t₁^8, t₂)`. Both are exact integer byte ops, no `abs()`, no stdlib `fractions`, `composition_of_c` — **no new C symbol** (both ride the c_dispatched `srmech_oct_mult`, div after one Class-C XOR) and `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays **10**.

- **`srmech.math.octonion.oct_torsor_act(t, g)`** (Class M ∘ I; `composition_of_c`) → the RIGHT action `t <| g = oct_mult(t, g)` (9 integer ops). Closure is structural: the index lane `(t&7)^(g&7)` keeps bit 2 set because `g`'s index is `< 4` and `t`'s is `≥ 4`, so a seam element acted on by a group element lands back in `T` — **1792/1792** over the 28 seams. The right action `R_g` equals the left action `L_{conj g}` on `T` (1792/1792). It IS `oct_mult` byte-for-byte on all **256** pairs; the torsor is the NAMED reading.
- **`srmech.math.octonion.oct_torsor_div(t1, t2)`** (Class C ∘ M; `composition_of_c`) → the UNIQUE `g ∈ H` with `t1 <| g == t2`, `= oct_mult(t1^8, t2)` (10 integer ops). By the Moufang left-inverse property that `g` is `conj(t1)·t2`; on `T` every element is an imaginary unit (`idx = t1&7 ∈ {4,5,6,7} ≠ 0`, verified **224/224**), so `conj(t1)` is the branch-free sign flip `t1^8` — which is exactly what makes div 10 ops, not the 11 of a branching `oct_conjugate`. The op asserts the precondition and refuses the real center `idx(t1)==0`. Simple transitivity: orbit histogram **{1: 1792}**.
- **The 4-point ratchet (`tests/test_oct_torsor_rc388.py`).** It pins BOTH the law AND the defect, which a closure-only test misses (the naive composition still lands in `T` 14336/14336 while being the WRONG element): (1) act closes into `T` and div lands in `H`, solves, and is unique — 1792/1792 each, histogram exactly `{1: 1792}`, denominated honestly as **448 × 4** (the 28 seams carry only 7 distinct `(H,T)` decompositions; `T` is always `H`'s set-complement); (2) the action law `(t<|g)<|h == t<|(h·g)` is **14336/14336** AND the naive `t<|(g·h)` is **8960/14336**; (3) `oct_conjugate(t) == t^8` on `T`, **224/224**; (4) act byte-exact vs `oct_mult` **256/256**, `R_g == L_{conj g}` 1792/1792, and `oct_mult`'s sign table recomputed from `cd_basis_product` (no drift). Convention: RIGHT action (`R_g`, not `L_g`); div solves `t1<|g==t2`.
- **Notebook correction (`srmech_research_notebook.md` §3.47).** The torsor is the **4-index coset H·e** (8 signed bytes, 1792/1792 H-stable), NOT the strict 3-index set (H-stable only **1008/1344**; first escape `L=(1,2,3), e=4, g=+e1, t=+e5 → byte 4 = +e4`, the seam unit itself — the shipped RIGHT action `oct_mult(t,g)=e5·e1` gives `+e4`; the ephemeral brief quoted `−e4/byte 12`, which is the REVERSED order `e1·e5`). **3+4 is the structure; 3+1+3 manufactures a seam artifact.** The action law is native to the 𝕆 rung (matching `#1514`: turns→ℍ, composition→𝕆): with the group an ASSOCIATIVE rung it holds **200/200** sampled at dim 8, and the "seam-independent W" phrasing is LABELLED as tautological (`pack_word` never reads a seam), true but not a finding.

## [0.9.0rc382]

**CLEAN-BREAK CORRECTION — `srmech.qm` REMOVED, no legacy path, `#T1056`.** rc381 (the ADR-0010 physics slice, `#T1052`) moved the whole `qm` subpackage to `srmech.physics.qm` but shipped `srmech/qm/__init__.py` as a `DeprecationWarning` deprecation alias "for one release." ## [0.9.0rc380]

**THE CAYLEY–DICKSON LOOP-DEFECT LADDER — the k=2 commutator + the general-dim k=3 3-cycle holonomy, `#T1055`.** The k=3 triangle-holonomy research read the Cayley–Dickson property-loss story as a **ladder of loop-defect operators of rising arity, each turning on one rung later** — and found two genuine op gaps beside the shipped `cascade.associator` (the k=3 bare-tuple defect, which turns on at 𝕆). Both new ops are exact-ℚ, numpy-free, no `abs()`, and — like the associator — a pure composition of the already-C-backed products, so **no new C symbol** and `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays **10**.

- **`srmech.cascade.cd_commutator(x, y, table=None)`** (Class C ∘ M ∘ K) → the k=2 **square-loop** defect `x·y − y·x`, the all-zero tuple iff the ordered pair commutes. It **turns on at ℍ** — 6/16 noncommuting ordered basis pairs, while the associator is still 0 there — one rung BELOW the associator, which is what makes the two a ladder and not a restatement. Closed form `(dim−1)(dim−2)`: 0 at ℝ, 0 at ℂ, 6 at ℍ, 42 at 𝕆, 210 at 𝕊. `table=` reaches any algebra a structure tensor names (the `algebra_table` split γ-twist negative control), exactly as the associator does. `composition_of_c`.
- **`srmech.cascade.cd_cycle_holonomy(x, y, z, table=None)`** (Class M ∘ C ∘ K) → the general-dim, any-rung **3-cycle edge-holonomy**: a directed triangle `0→ˣ1→ʸ2→ᶻ0` of CD edge-gains, walked BOTH ways — `holonomy_left=(x·y)·z`, `holonomy_right=x·(y·z)`, `defect=left−right`, `closed=(defect==0)`. It is the general peer of the ℍ-only `qm.quaternion.quaternion_cycle_holonomy` (which lives on an associative rung where the walk is bracketing-free and never has to choose). `closed` is a property of the RUNG, not the gains: every triangle closes on ℝ/ℂ/ℍ, and at 𝕆 the basis triangles fail to close on exactly the 168/512 non-associating triples (1848/4096 at 𝕊). Its `defect` **IS** `associator(x,y,z)` (512/512 at dim 8) — the same k=3 content carried as a loop. ⚠️ EPISTEMIC CEILING: it reads the FORM of the holonomy (the ordered walk + whether it closes), not the ℍ-only SU(2) conjugacy-class read. `composition_of_c`.

- **Notebook SSoT amendment — §3.29.3 gains a 4th, CARRIER-DISCRIMINATED k=3 sense.** The section enumerated three k=3 senses ({B,H,N} / {3D_s,7D_g,1D_t} / {8v,8s,8c}) and OMITTED the associator-triangle. It is now added and explicitly **separated from the Out(Q8)=S₃ automorphism relabeling** (triality τ, which lives at ℍ where the associator is 0): the **turn-on rung** is the discriminator (commutator@ℍ / associator@𝕆), and the **second axis is the Fix-dimension** on so(8)=28 (order-3 τ `Fix=14=g₂` / order-2 swap `Fix=21` / `14+7+7=28`, §3.45.2). Kept a FORM claim, not an identity — the k=3 content is *carried by* 𝕆 non-associativity, and the two axes are the evidence the four senses are DIFFERENT.

Differential gate: `tests/test_cd_loop_defect_ladder_rc380.py`.

## [0.9.0rc379]

**THE NEW `srmech.chemistry` DOMAIN — reaction networks as exact-integer linear algebra, `#T1050`.** A brand-new top-level domain namespace (the ADR-0010 domain taxonomy names domains by field: math / biology / music / … → chemistry), built on the rc378 `primitive_integer_vector` keystone. Four public ops, each reading a chemical reaction as exact cyclic-group / spectral structure over ℚ (no float tolerance, no `abs()`):

- **`srmech.chemistry.balance_reaction(species, *, all_balances=False)`** (Class L ∘ I/K/C) → signed primitive integer coefficients = the integer nullspace of the **element × species** matrix `A` (`A·v = 0`). Each exact-Q kernel column is reduced by `primitive_integer_vector`, first-nonzero pinned positive; the SIGN carries direction (a negative coefficient is a product). `["H2","O2","H2O"] → [2, 1, -2]`. Accepts formula strings, `{element: count}` dicts, or a raw element×species `QMat`, interchangeably. Raises on an UNBALANCEABLE reaction (trivial kernel); an UNDERDETERMINED one (kernel dim > 1) raises unless `all_balances=True`.
- **`srmech.chemistry.conservation_laws(N)`** (Class L ∘ I) → an integer basis of the conserved moieties = the LEFT-nullspace of the **species × reaction** stoichiometric matrix `N` (`γᵀN = 0`), via `N.T.nullspace()` + the keystone.
- **`srmech.chemistry.deficiency(reactions, *, with_components=False)`** (Class L ∘ J) → the Feinberg deficiency `δ = n − ℓ − s = rank(L_complex) − rank(N)`: `n` distinct complexes, `ℓ` linkage classes (components of the complex graph, read as `n − rank(L_complex)` from the Class-L `dense_laplacian`), `s = rank(N)` (Class-J `QMat.rank`). `A ⇌ B` has `δ=0`; `2A → A+B → 2B → 2A` has `δ=1`.
- **`srmech.chemistry.parse_formula(formula)`** (Class F/G) → an `{element: count}` dict, with multi-letter symbols and arbitrarily NESTED parenthesised groups (`"Ca3(PO4)2" → {Ca:3, P:2, O:8}`); defers (raises on) hydrate dots / charges / isotopes.

⚠️ **TWO DIFFERENT MATRICES** — the #1 correctness trap, tested in both directions: `balance_reaction` builds **element × species**; `conservation_laws` / `deficiency` build **species × reaction**. Correctness is pinned against TEXTBOOK oracles (H₂O synthesis, C₃H₈ combustion, C₂H₆ combustion needing a gcd reduction, Fe/O₂ redox, Michaelis–Menten's two conservation laws, the documented δ=0 and δ=1 networks).

- **C parity (ADR-0009).** The three math ops are `composition_of_c` — they compose the already-C-backed `QMat` nullspace/rank, the graph Laplacian, and `srmech_primitive_integer_vector` — so they need **no new kernel**. `parse_formula` is the one genuinely new capability and ships a dedicated JPL-clean caller-arena C twin **`srmech_parse_formula`** (a bounded non-recursive tokenizer with an explicit paren-multiplier stack; ≤60-line functions, ≥2 asserts each, no malloc/goto; `srmech_parse_formula_ws_bound` sizes the arena) in `c/src/srmech_chemistry.c` + prototype in `c/include/srmech.h` + ctypes binding & `has_native_parse_formula()` in `srmech/_native`, so it is `c_dispatched` with the pure-Python explicit-stack body as the byte-identical fallback and parity oracle. Additive symbol → `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays **10** (no callback typedef).
- **Citation (science is the SSoT).** The deficiency `δ = n − ℓ − s` is definitional and stated self-contained; the standard references are M. Feinberg, *Foundations of Chemical Reaction Network Theory* (Springer, Applied Mathematical Sciences 202, 2019) and the open-access *Lectures on Chemical Reaction Networks* (Univ. of Wisconsin MRC, 1979/1980). The paywalled Chem. Eng. Sci. **42** (1987) origin paper is NOT used as the attestation (paywalled-DOI discipline).
- **Registration + wiring + counts.** A `ToolEntry` per op (`_register_chemistry_tools()`); `srmech.chemistry` appended to the Rosetta walk roots (`tests/rosetta_roots.py` + the `_EXPECTED_ROOTS` mirror) — a NEW domain, not an ADR-0010 declustering destination, so it is deliberately absent from both ADR-0010 tuples; 4 rows in `rosetta_classification.ndjson` (3 `composition_of_c` + 1 `c_dispatched`); curated worked examples in `_tool_docs_curated.py`; `describe()["tools"]["total"]` **526 → 530** (the 61 op-total pins across 56 test files bumped, plus the `registered_op_names.txt` witness manifest + its digest + `EXPECTED_N`). ## [0.9.0rc378]

**THE `primitive_integer_vector` KEYSTONE — the smallest integer vector on an exact ℚ-vector's ray, `#T1049`.** New op `srmech.math.cyclic.primitive_integer_vector` (Class I ∘ K ∘ C): given a rational vector — a `QMat` row/column (what `QMat.nullspace` returns), a list of `Q` / `int` / `Fraction`, or a list of `(num, den)` pairs — it returns the `list[int]` pointing the SAME way with content 1, in the canonical convention that the **first nonzero entry is positive**. The all-zero vector maps to all zeros. This is the keystone the chemistry stoichiometry domain (`#T1050`, balancing a reaction = the integer nullspace of the stoichiometric matrix) consumes next: a ℚ kernel column becomes the integer reaction coefficients.

- **Algorithm (exact, integer-only, NO `abs()`):** clear denominators by their LCM (Class I, composing the arbitrary-precision `cyclic.gcd` — not the uint64-capped `cyclic.lcm`, since an exact-nullspace column grows bignum), strip the content = gcd of the entry magnitudes (Class I / Class K magnitude), then pin the first nonzero entry positive (Class K pin-slot ∘ Class C reorient, mirroring the `_ipoly_primitive` / `_primitive` convention in `srmech.cascade`). `with_content=True` returns `(content_signed, primitive)` so `content_signed * primitive` reconstructs the denominator-cleared vector `L·v` (the reduction is reversible), matching `_ipoly_primitive`'s shape.
- **1:1 C parity (ADR-0009):** new JPL-clean C peer `srmech_primitive_integer_vector` in `srmech_cyclic.c` (int64 signed fast path over caller-owned buffers, no malloc; `INT64_MIN` and any int64 intermediate overflow return `SRMECH_ERR_OVERFLOW` so the pure-Python bignum body — the complete, byte-identical alternative — takes over), prototype in `c/include/srmech.h`, ctypes binding + `has_native_primitive_integer_vector()` in `srmech/_native`. Additive symbol → `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays **10**; no callback typedef.
- **Registration + counts:** `ToolEntry` (Class I + K + C) in `tool_schema.py`; `c_dispatched` row in `rosetta_classification.ndjson`; `describe()["tools"]["total"]` **525 → 526** (the 61 op-total pins across 55 test files bumped, plus the `registered_op_names.txt` witness manifest + its digest + `EXPECTED_N`). Generated artifacts regenerated via `tools/regen_all.py`.

### The ``compose`` → ``composites`` rename (ADR B.1 rule-1's ONE sanctioned exception)

A `compose.py` already lived in `srmech/cascade/` — the ADR-0002 chain ENGINE (`run_chain` / `parse_chain_spec` / `parse_chain_spec`). The incoming `amsc/cascade/compose.py` is the DISJOINT lean-ISA COMPOSITES layer (`cyclic_gcd` / `best_rational_signed` / `kuramoto_step` / `autocorrelation`; its own docstring opens *"Cascade **composites** — iterative algorithms over the atoms"*). Two disjoint modules cannot share one leaf name, so the incoming one is `git mv`'d to `srmech/cascade/composites.py` (module `srmech.cascade.composites`). This is ADR-0010 B.1 rule-1's ("a slice relocates a PARENT; it does not rename the LEAF") ONE sanctioned exception, documented AS the exception in the merged package docstring; the leaf name is docstring-derived. The incumbent `compose.py` is LEFT untouched. The C dispatch strings use FLAT op names (`srmech.amsc.cascade.cyclic_gcd`, NOT `...compose.cyclic_gcd`), so they took the plain amsc-drop; only the class-descriptor / Rosetta / `_c_claims` `defined_at` fields carry the `compose`→`composites` module qualifier.

### The flat-API ``__init__`` merge (load-bearing)

The rc364 top-level `__init__` (catalogs-loader package, deliberately import-free) is UNIONED with the incoming subpackage `__init__` (the flat op re-exports). Every `from srmech.cascade import <op>` consumer AND the DSL flat resolver (`dsl/_catalog.py` does `getattr(srmech.cascade, op_name)`) rely on `srmech.cascade.<op>` resolving, so the full flat surface is preserved. ⚠️ ORDERING: the `atoms` re-exports (`chiral_flip` / `hypercomplex_couple` / `magnitude`) precede the `cd_register` / `sedenion_register` imports, which do `from . import chiral_flip` at import time. Verified: `from srmech.cascade import cyclic_gcd, quaternion_dft, the_one` works, `import srmech.cascade.composites` / `.one` / `.matrix_cascades` succeed, and `import srmech.amsc.cascade` raises `ModuleNotFoundError`.

The FLAT dotted form `srmech.amsc.cascade` → `srmech.cascade` (and `srmech.amsc.cascade.compose` → `srmech.cascade.composites`) swept every live source/tests/tools/C/`.github`/`.ndjson` reference. A rename preserves the bucket, so all four non-compute counts and the `_TOTAL_NON_COMPUTE` pin are unchanged; only the row's dotted name and the zero-reach pin moved.

### The census's rc365 mint conflated three quantities — the first move exposed it, and it is FIXED

The census two-edit procedure (drop the module from the manifest + update the digest) turned out **incomplete**: dropping `harmonics` from the manifest turned `test_the_move_map_matches_A2` red — not because harmonics was misfiled, but because the rc365 mint treated the **current amsc population** (the manifest, which must shrink so the down-only ceiling drops), **A.2's fixed plan** (`NAMED_DEPARTURES` / `ADR_A2_DESTINATION_COUNTS` — `harmonics → music` is correct forever), and **drain progress** as one quantity — true only in the snapshot where nothing has moved. Fixed by adding a `LANDED` record and a conservation invariant (`EXPECTED_N_MODULES + len(LANDED) == ORIGINAL_N_MODULES`), making "a named member is REAL when still in amsc OR landed", and stating the "73 of 75" gap against a fixed `ORIGINAL_N_MODULES`. The manifest still drops the leaver; A.2's record is preserved; a shrink can no longer be booked without saying where the module went. **census digest `c3c3d174…` → `52a34d12…`; 78 → 77 manifest lines, 75 → 74 modules.** See ADR-0010 Amendment C.

### What the prose op-ref gate did NOT catch — and why it matters for the next slices

The rc363 prose gate was expected to fire on the stale citation; it did not. Harmonics' only dotted `srmech.amsc.harmonics.*` strings were the ToolEntry `name=` fields (which the gate does not scan — it reads `summary` / `explanation` / params / returns), and its prose cites siblings in **slash-form** `srmech/amsc/harmonics.py:NN`, which the gate excludes as a filename. So a module whose cross-citations are file-path refs is invisible to the dotted-path gate; the slash-form citations were fixed anyway, below the gate's floor. The instrument that actually caught the move was the **rc361 op-name-set witness**. The bigger `math` / `apokatastasis` buckets are likelier to carry genuine dotted cross-citations that WILL trip the prose gate.

## [0.9.0rc365]

**THE `srmech/amsc/` MODULE-AND-SUBPACKAGE CENSUS — ADR-0010 A.5 item 5, the instrument that must land green BEFORE the first module-moving slice.** `#T1034`. Ships **alone and moves no module**, per the A.5 ordering rule: *an instrument built in the same arc as the change it detects has no green baseline, so a red is unattributable.* No op, no C surface, no registered callable — `describe()["tools"]["total"]` stays **525**, `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays **10**.

### Why it exists

rc364's Amendment B.5 measured it: `CEIL_AMSC_PREFIX` counts **dotted module PATHS**, so it is structurally blind to a directory/module MOVE — rc364 moved four directories out of `amsc` and both channels read FLAT. *"The quantity the arc actually drains, module by module, has no instrument."* `srmech/amsc/` is draining **75 modules → 4** (only `format` / `catalog` / `descriptor` / `gap_suggester` keep, per A.2); nothing in the tree measured that population. This rc is that instrument.

### What it is — a name-SET, not a name-COUNT

`tests/test_amsc_module_census_rc365.py` + the hand-committed manifest `tests/amsc_module_census.txt`. Mirrors the rc361 op-name-SET witness precedent: a count of 75 is blind to a rename-in-place, and this arc moves *named* modules out, so the SET is the right quantity. The manifest is the **75 module stems + 3 subpackage names** (subpackages marked with a trailing `/`), sorted, plus a `srmech.amsc.format.sha256_bytes` digest over the normalised body (`"\n".join(sorted) + "\n"`, so a CRLF checkout cannot split the Windows/Linux digest).

- **DOWN-ONLY.** The live module set must stay a **subset** of the committed manifest — a module may LEAVE, but one *appearing* in `amsc` is the regression this catches. The floor is the four keepers; when the live set equals them the arc is DONE (documented in the test).
- **Departures respect A.2.** The removed set (committed − live) must be ⊆ the departure allowlist (all 71 non-keepers, derived from A.2's authoritative "only 4 keep"), and the four keepers are asserted **never** to be in the removed set. A.2's per-destination counts (apokatastasis 31 / math 22 / introspect 10 / biology 4 / cascade 1 / music 1 / _native 1, keeps 4) are encoded as documentation data; only the destinations A.2 names per-module (biology / cascade / music / _native / the named introspect members) are checked member-by-member — the winding/math/introspect split is published only as an aggregate, so reproducing it per-module would fabricate authority A.2 does not carry. A.2's table sums to 74 against 75 modules; the residual 1 is A.2's own acknowledged "73 of 75" classification gap, and the census does not depend on resolving it.
- **⚠️ HAND-COMMITTED, NOT codegen-emitted.** `test_the_manifest_is_not_codegen_emitted` asserts nothing under `tools/` writes the manifest — a declustering slice runs `tools/regen_all.py` as routine work, and a generated census would be rewritten by the very change it must detect and go green unconditionally (A.5 item 1's rule). The two-edit procedure (rewrite the manifest AND update the digest in source, same commit) is copied from the rc361 witness.

### Non-vacuity — proved by injection on the real population

`test_the_census_can_actually_fail` runs four injections and proves exactly the intended assertion fires while the others stay green: (1) a module leaving for a mapped destination (`rational` → `srmech.math`) keeps down-only green and **changes the digest** — the move is detected; (2) a departure the map does not classify → the **move-map** assert goes red; (3) a NEW module appearing in `amsc` → the **down-only** assert goes red; (4) a keeper (`format`) leaving → the **keeper** assert goes red. A census that cannot be shown to fail is the EMPTY probe A.5 warns against.

### Selection predicate (rc364's lesson, confirmed not assumed)

Adding this test file changes **no** op-population pin, split, ceiling or allowlist — it adds a test, not a registered op, and registers no `ToolEntry`. Confirmed: the rc361 op-name-SET witness (which pins both the op-name set and `EXPECTED_N = 525`) stays green, as do the rc364 cascade-catalog-home test, the version pin, and the ref-notation guard. **A.5 item 5 is now DONE — the first module-moving slice (rc366) is unblocked.**

## [0.9.0rc364]

**ADR-0010'S FIRST EXECUTION SLICE — `srmech.cascade` is real, and a documented migration path that raised `FileNotFoundError` for 93 rcs now works.** `#T1034` (with `#T1039`). `describe()["tools"]["total"]` stays **525**; `carrier_schema()` stays 28; `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 10 (no C signature changed — one generated header comment regenerates).

### The move

ADR-0010's `make_class` re-homed clause, executed verbatim: the built-in `[class]` / `[cascade]` / worked-instance TOML catalogs left `srmech/amsc/_research/` for **`srmech/cascade/catalogs/`**, and `srmech/amsc/_research/` was deleted. `srmech.cascade` is the arc's **first new top-level namespace**, so it also sets the pattern — three rules, recorded as ADR-0010 Amendment B.1:

1. **A slice relocates a PARENT; it does not rename the LEAF.** `class_catalog` / `cascade_catalog` / `worked_instances` kept their names. One slice, one variable — a slice that moves AND renames makes every red ambiguous between the two, which is the unattributable-red hazard ADR-0010's own prerequisite section forbids one level up. (Also: `class` is a Python reserved word, so a "name it after the TOML section" rule breaks on its first member.)
2. **Declarative descriptors under `catalogs/`; imperative modules beside it.** When later slices move `compose` / `atoms` / `the_one` / `cd_register` in, they land at `srmech/cascade/*.py`.
3. **Every catalog directory carries an `__init__.py`.** Measured first: `worked_instances/` had no marker and shipped anyway, because both backends copy the package tree wholesale. The marker is the difference between inclusion by *declaration* and inclusion by *heuristic* — and this rc exists because an adjacent assumption of exactly that kind cost two descriptors their place in the wheel.

`srmech/cascade/__init__.py` imports nothing and exports nothing, so `import srmech.cascade` stays free; asserted, not merely intended.

### ⚠️ A LIVE WHEEL DEFECT, CLOSED — the loader shipped, the thing it loads did not

`tests/data/genome_type_aliases_legacy.toml` is the documented migration path for rc271's **BREAKING** `stick`→`plasmid` / `minted`→`nuclear` rename, and its own header prints the call to make: *"Opt in with ONE call: `genome.load_type_aliases_toml("genome_type_aliases_legacy.toml")`"* — a **bare filename**. `tests/**` is in `sdist.include` and **not** in the wheel (`wheel.packages = ["srmech"]`, no force-include, no `MANIFEST.in`). **Install the wheel, follow the header, get `FileNotFoundError`** — for **93 rcs** (rc271 → rc363). `load_type_aliases_toml` was in `genome.__all__` with an introspect entry the whole time.

rc362 then landed the tree's first-ever `[[alias]]` descriptor (`music_domain_aliases.toml`) in the same directory. **That was not a mistake, it was the absence of an alternative** — there was no `ALIAS_CATALOG_DIR` to land it in, so `tests/data/` was where a descriptor went *by default rather than by decision*. Both now ship at `srmech/cascade/catalogs/alias_catalog/`, and both documented one-liners are **executed** in `tests/test_cascade_catalog_home_rc364.py` rather than described. A rule — not a filename pair — forbids the next alias descriptor from landing in `tests/data/`.

### The alias layer gets the catalog shape the `[class]` layer has had since rc39

`srmech/dsl/_alias.py` exposed `load_aliases_toml(path)` and nothing else: no `ALIAS_CATALOG_DIR` peer to `CLASS_CATALOG_DIR`, no `register_alias_dir` peer to `register_class_dir`. Four public names close that (`#T1039`, ADR-0004's config-driven/plugin stance made concrete):

| class layer (rc39) | alias layer (rc364) |
|---|---|
| `CLASS_CATALOG_DIR` | **`ALIAS_CATALOG_DIR`** |
| `register_class_dir` · `SRMECH_CLASS_PATH` | **`register_alias_dir`** · **`SRMECH_ALIAS_PATH`** |
| `list_classes` | **`list_alias_descriptors`** |
| `load_class_catalog` | **`resolve_alias_descriptor`** (name **or** path) |

Resolution is **filesystem-first**, so no existing caller changes meaning; a bare name falls through to the catalog. Shipped descriptors are A-tier and a user directory may not shadow one, matching `load_class_catalog`. **What it enables: a domain can now SHIP its vocabulary** — an acoustic user `pip install`s srmech and gets `partials` / `bell_tuning` / `overtone_series` with no source edit and no recompile.

Three rosetta rows, and **the split is not the obvious one**: `resolve_alias_descriptor` is **host_glue** (descriptor FS *discovery* — a bare-C host must FIND the file before `srmech_toml` parses it), while `list_alias_descriptors` + `register_alias_dir` are **dev_tooling** (*browse* and *configure* — a C host resolves the one name it was handed; peers of `list_cascade_ops`/`list_classes` and `register_catalog_dir`/`register_class_dir`). host_glue **21 → 22**, dev_tooling **51 → 53**, total **210 → 213**; `composes_c` **UNMOVED at 138** — none of the three composes a C op. ⚠️ **The discriminator is not "does it touch the filesystem" — all three do.** It is **LOAD/GET vs BROWSE/CONFIGURE**, the split `srmech.dsl` already encodes over the *same* directory (`load_class_catalog` reads it = host_glue; `list_classes` browses it = dev_tooling). rc364 first shipped `list_alias_descriptors` as host_glue by reasoning from the mechanism (it calls `glob`) rather than the capability, making it the only host_glue `list_*` in `srmech.dsl` against five dev_tooling siblings; **the fix was the classification, not the pin**. No `ToolEntry`, so no op-count pin moves.

**Pin files touched** (see the selection predicate below): `test_non_compute_ratchet_rc170.py` (`_TOTAL_NON_COMPUTE`, `_EXPECTED_SPLIT`), `test_annex_ratchet_rc177.py` + `test_annex_ratchet_rc183.py` (`_TOTAL_NON_COMPUTE`, `_FULL_SPLIT`), `test_rosetta_completeness.py` (`NON_COMPUTE_DEV_TOOLING_EXEMPT`, +2), `rosetta_classification.ndjson` (+3 rows), `rosetta_roots.py` + `test_rosetta_roots_single_source_rc361.py` (the `srmech.cascade` root).

**⚠️ SELECTION PREDICATE, stated so the next slice inherits a rule rather than a list.** A slice that **adds or removes a public callable under a rosetta walk root** selects *every* file that pins a population, split, ceiling or allowlist derived from the ledger or the op registry — mechanically, every test that reads `rosetta_classification.ndjson`, calls `rosetta_live_objects()`, imports from `test_rosetta_completeness`, or reads `tool_schema_view()`. That is **51 files**, found by one grep. The *path*-edit count (28) predicts none of them. rc364's own cost finding already named this predicate — *"scope later slices by public callables and ledger rows disturbed, not by paths rewritten"* — and the first pass then selected by hand anyway and missed `test_non_compute_ratchet_rc170.py`, which carries its own `_TOTAL_NON_COMPUTE` / `_EXPECTED_SPLIT` pins **separate from** the two annex files. Six sequential targeted sweeps at ~1930 tests covered 8 of the 51.

ADR-0012 clause C6's **package-home half is closed; its `describe()` half stays open** — `"alias"` still occurs 0 times in `json.dumps(describe())`. The layer is now reachable by name and still not discoverable without knowing the name. Half the defect, precisely.

### ⚠️ THE RATCHET DID NOT MOVE, AND THE PLAN IS WHAT WAS WRONG

`CEIL_AMSC_PREFIX` was expected to fall. Measured after `tools/regen_all.py`: as-text **2957 → 2957**, decoded **577 → 577**, every per-artifact pair flat. The only regen delta in the tree was **one line of header comment** in `srmech_class_registry.c`.

The ratchet counts a **dotted** prefix — a *module-path* population. This slice moved **data files**, whose location is only ever written as a filesystem path with slashes, and the descriptor BODIES are untouched (a `[class]` descriptor's `op = "srmech.biology.genome.chromosome"` names an op whose module did not move), so all 40 decoded hits survive by construction. **The instrument is correct; ADR-0010 was wrong to fold "move the catalogs" and "move the modules" into one drain.** Recorded at the ratchet and as Amendment B.5, so a later slice does not read a flat rc as a failed one.

The quantity this slice *did* reduce — `srmech/amsc/` from **4 subpackages to 3** — has no instrument anywhere. That census is now **A.5 item 5**, and it must land in its own rc with a green baseline *before* the first module-moving slice; it was deliberately not minted here, because an instrument built in the same arc as the change it detects has no baseline to be attributed against.

### Two defects found in passing

- **`srmech.cascade` appended to the rosetta walk roots** (`tests/rosetta_roots.py`), moving from `_ADR0010_NEW_NAMESPACES` to `_ADR0010_EXISTING_DESTINATIONS` — the one route `test_rosetta_roots_single_source_rc361` accepts, and the rule rc362 set for `srmech.music`. It adds **zero rows**; the namespace holds descriptors, not callables. Still the right edit: a *non-existent* root is silently skipped, an *existing empty* root is a measured zero that goes red the moment a later slice moves ops in.
- **Two guards were unrunnable inside a git worktree.** `test_ref_notation_emitted_rc348.py` and `test_rosetta_roots_single_source_rc361.py` excluded paths by testing `"worktrees" in path.parts` on the **absolute** path. Run from a `.claude/worktrees/` checkout — where this project's build discipline says to work — that matched EVERY file, so the ref-notation scan derived an **empty** task-ID set and both strict-zero tests failed on *"derived no local task IDs at all - the scan is broken"*. The non-vacuity assert did its job (loud, not silent), but the gate could not go green in the sanctioned environment. Fixed by testing the parts of the path **relative to the scan root** — `.claude/worktrees/` sits above `docs/`, so nothing below `docs/srmech` can be a worktree.

### Cost, for planning the remaining slices

Amendment A.3 budgets 5,442 hand-edit lines / 751 files for the whole arc. This slice: **206 grep hits → 28 live path literals → 29 files hand-edited**, a **≈7:1** ratio; the residue is CHANGELOG (do-not-touch), test *filenames*, dated `notes/`, and `srmech.dsl._class_catalog.*` module refs the move does not touch. **The move was the cheap part.** Effort went, in order, to: the alias-home decision and its ADR write-ups, the wheel defect and its test, the new `_alias` surface, the rosetta ripple — and last, the paths. Scope later slices by *public callables and ledger rows disturbed*, not by paths rewritten.

### Also

- `python/README.md` cascade-catalog descriptor count **15 → 20** (stale since rc363 measured it; the README ships as the PyPI long-description).
- `docs/srmech/CLAUDE.md` package-layout diagram now shows `srmech/cascade/catalogs/` with all four catalogs and their counts.

## [0.9.0rc363]

**THE ADR-0012 INSTRUMENTS — three ungated clauses become gates, and building them proved the ADR wrong twice.** `#T1045`. Implement-before-accept by user direction; ADR-0012 stays 🟡 PROPOSED. `describe()["tools"]["total"]` stays **525**; `carrier_schema()` **26 → 28**; `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 10 (no C signature changed — two generated tables regenerate).

### Why implement a PROPOSED ADR

User direction 2026-07-30: *"adr12 implement as proposed tell us when to mark accepted. might seem backwards but I don't want follow up adr to fix it if we botch a design choice early."* So the clauses get instruments while the ADR is still a proposal, and the acceptance decision is made against measurements rather than against a reading. It was the right order: **two of the draft's own statements did not survive being implemented** (below).

ADR-0012 §3.2 is the governing line — *"a clause without an instrument that can return otherwise is not a clause, it is a preference"*. rc362 closed the C2 and C3 **exhibits** by hand, with no gate that selected them. An exhibit closed by hand is a preference that happened to be honoured once.

### The shared instrument — a SECOND channel, because one channel cannot disagree with itself

`tests/coercion_boundary.py` derives what an op actually accepts and produces **from its own source**: it tracks the op's declared parameters through assignment, iteration and helper calls (imported helpers included) and reads the `isinstance` guards on the way. ADR-0012 §2 states why this had to exist — both `describe()` and `carrier_schema()` derive their capability axes from the **declared type strings**, so the drift ratchet built to force a new carrier into the registry reads the same field it is supposed to police. §7.3 records the consequence: C parity was byte-green on the identical hole, *because* both projections read the same impoverished SSoT.

Dataflow tracking is not an optimisation. Attributing every `isinstance` in a defining module to every op in it reports `coupling.fold_spectrum` as accepting a `Poly` — the guarded value is rebuilt from recovered HDC tokens and has no path from any parameter. Tracking removes that row and keeps every genuine one.

### GATE 1 — C2 (TYPED HONESTLY): the clause as literally written is too noisy to ship

ADR-0012 §3.1 says *"the test is mechanical: does the type string name what the op's own coercion `raise` text names?"*. Implemented plainly — carrier tokens in any raise text in an op's defining module, against that module's declared types — it flags **16 of the 33 modules it selects** (measured on the rc362 tree, before this rc's fixes), and all 16 were inspected: `amsc.tripoly`'s *constructor* raises on `BiPoly`/`Poly`/`Q` while the registered op takes raw coefficients; `amsc.op_provenance` raises prose explaining what is NOT provenance-tracked; `amsc.genome` (68 ops) trips on one `Q` in one helper. A gate wrong roughly half the time trains the reader to override it, so **the noisy form is not shipped**.

`tests/test_declared_type_honesty_rc363.py` ships the **decidable subset**: a carrier is flagged only when the op BOTH accepts it (dataflow-tracked `isinstance`) AND names it in a raise text on that same path. Selection **27 of 525 ops**; on the rc362 tree it found **8 violations, every one genuine**, all **fixed rather than ceilinged**:

| op | withheld | was declared |
|---|---|---|
| `carrier_ladder.qpoly_promote` | `QBiPoly` | `QPoly` |
| `q_gosper.q_gosper` (both params) | `Poly` | `QPoly` |
| `elliptic_gosper` · `elliptic_recurrence_8w7` · `elliptic_zeilberger` · `elliptic_wz_certificate` · `carrier_spectrum` | `EllMonomial` + `Theta` | `EllRatio` |
| `harmonics.classify_chirality_harmonic` | `Q` | `float` |
| `coupling.fold_spectrum` (WIDE channel only) | `Q` | `number` |

**Five of the eight carried the union in their human-readable prose in the SAME TUPLE that withheld it from the machine-readable field** — each elliptic op's `description` already read *"an EllMonomial / Theta is lifted"*. That is C2's failure mode in one line of source, and it is why the clause is about a *field* and not about documentation quality.

Every widened type string maps to the **same** MCP coercer its one-carrier key already used — `_to_ellratio` has accepted `EllRatio` / `EllMonomial` / `Theta` since rc61. **The wire behaviour did not change; the declaration caught up.** `float | Q` and `number | Q` also get `_TYPE_LEXICON` entries so the published JSON-schema type stays `"number"` rather than degrading to `"string"` (ADR-0012 §4.2 row 4).

**Still open, and said out loud: the RETURN half of C2 is ungated.** `returns.type` has no second channel, and ADR-0012 §6.3 already declines `returns.shape` as a gate surface (403 unregistered capitalised-token occurrences over 154 distinct tokens — a wider regex floods). That verdict stands.

### GATE 2 — C3 (CONSTRUCTIBLE): the existing ratchet passed by not selecting

`tests/test_carrier_schema_rc205.py::test_every_tool_type_carrier_token_is_registered` is the C3 ratchet and it **stays** — it is the right instrument for what it measures. But it scans declared type strings, and at rc362 the string `"Qalg"` occurred in **0 of 525** of them, so it passed throughout the one event it exists for.

`tests/test_carrier_use_derivation_rc363.py` supplies the missing channel. **27 candidate operand classes** surface across 525 ops; two structural exclusions apply as RULES rather than lists — `BaseException` subclasses (6) and `_private` names (6, all lazy aliases of a registered carrier or an internal handle). The six infra/handle exemptions (`ChainSpec` / `Endpoint` / `MPRRecord` / `RecoverableFold` / `Run` / `SpectralHandle`) are now **single-sourced** in `tests/coercion_boundary.NON_CARRIER_CLASSES` and consumed by BOTH gates, so two channels asking the same question cannot grant different exemptions.

**This corrected ADR-0012's own baseline.** §3.1 records *"of the 25 genuine operand-carrier classes the other 516 ops surface, 24 have a registry row — the lone precedent is `CarrierSpectrum`"*. Measured on the USE channel the residual is **two, not one**:

- **`Theta`** — the exact modified-theta symbol θ(z; p), the ATOM of the elliptic row, accepted **directly by five ops**. The draft missed it for exactly the reason the clause exists: it was measuring the declared channel, where all five said `EllRatio`.
- **`CarrierSpectrum`** — built on `carrier_spectrum`'s return path and handed back under `'spectrum'`; its own docstring calls it *"a first-class carrier object (not a diagnostic dict)"*.

Both were **registered** (26 → 28), each with a real description, a `_CAPABILITY` row (`_CAP_NO_PRODUCT` for both — neither has a closed binary product, which is distinct from `"unclassified"`) and an executed construction example. So C3 ships strict-zero rather than with a CEIL of 2. **A baseline is a measurement, and a measurement inherits the blindness of its instrument.**

### GATE 3 — the prose op-ref resolution gate (`#T1045`)

`#T930` closed this question for the packaged `[class]` TOML descriptors — op-refs bound by string, nothing asserting they still resolve, a rename leaving the binding orphaned while every other test stayed green. The tool schema has the same shape and had none of the guard. Measured across the introspect surface: `example` carries 563 `srmech.amsc.*` citations and fails **loudly** (`test_worked_examples_execute_rc354` runs them), while `summary` + `explanation` carry **251** and fail **silently**.

`tests/test_prose_oprefs_resolve_rc363.py` takes the silent half. `example` is deliberately out of scope — execution is strictly stronger than resolution, and duplicating it adds cost with no detection.

**The rule, stated:** a dotted path resolves iff, taking the LONGEST importable module prefix and walking the rest with `getattr`, every segment exists. **A module path counts** — `srmech.amsc.laplacian` (135 occurrences, the largest single citation) is a real reference, and ADR-0010 moves modules, so a dead module citation is exactly as broken as a dead op citation. Deep chains resolve too (`srmech.amsc.qmat.QMat.rank`). Two extractions are excluded **by rule**: a filename (`srmech.h`, the C public header, 24 occurrences — not a Python path at all) and a wildcard tail (`srmech.qm.*`, truncated to its module prefix).

Measured: **462 occurrences of 199 distinct paths across 236 of 525 ops** — 438 attribute references, 24 module references, **0 unresolved**. Strict-zero, no CEIL. The gate also covers `parameters[].summary` and `returns.shape`/`.summary` (6 occurrences), where it found **one genuine stale citation**: `genome_register_attested`'s `source` example read `'srmech.genome.<name>'`, a module path that has never existed. Fixed.

After this gate, **a module move cannot leave a stale citation behind** — which is what makes ADR-0010's decluster safe from the prose side.

### Non-vacuity — demonstrated, not asserted

Each gate was proven by injecting a real defect into real content, watching it go red, then restoring **byte-identically** (sha256-verified). The C3 proof is a **differential**, and it is the load-bearing one:

> Restoring the rc362 pre-state exactly — `partials` declared bare `Sequence`, `Qalg` unregistered — leaves the existing declared-channel ratchet `test_every_tool_type_carrier_token_is_registered` **GREEN (1 passed)**, while the new use-derivation gate goes **RED, naming all three `srmech.music` ops**.

That is ADR-0012 §1.2's *"findings no gate selected"* converted into a finding a gate selects. The C2 injection (reverting `elliptic_gosper.r` to `EllRatio`) fires 3 assertions including the CEIL-is-not-slack pin; the prose injection (`srmech.amsc.laplacian.elementwise_sqrt` → `srmech.laplacian.…` in `rational.sqrt`'s SIBLINGS prose, i.e. an ADR-0010 move that forgot a citation) fires the named parametrised case plus the aggregate.

### One further defect the work surfaced — a generator whose preservation claim was false

`tools/gen_carrier_examples_probe.py` has claimed since rc241 that *"hand-curated construction examples may be added here and are preserved"*. They were not: `main()` rewrites the whole file from its two dicts, and regenerating for the two new carriers **silently dropped the rc362 `Qalg` row** — whose `yields` carries the zero-divisor / irrationality witness a bare `repr` cannot show. Fixed by giving the generator a `_CURATED` dict applied last, so the claim is structurally true rather than aspirational. This is ADR-0012 §6.1's pattern (a mechanism that declares a property it does not have) caught in a third place.

### ADR-0012 amendments — including a clause the draft did not have

- **§3.3 (new)** records the implement-before-accept measurement, both corrections, the injection proofs, and — plainly — **what is still ungated after this rc**.
- **§3.1 C6 (new) + §3.4 (new) — CONFIG-VISIBLE.** User direction: *"our TOML surface should even enter describe information. this is how users and LLM and srmech inference with siona will know what tools do what, with our siona project goal to actually be able to know what a cascade looks like from a word problem."* The structural argument: **introspection derived from Python source cannot see config-driven behaviour by construction** — so ADR-0004's config-driven preference and ADR-0012's introspect-as-contract standard are in direct tension, and the tension WIDENS with every descriptor added. Measured: `class_catalog/` 4 descriptors **are** visible (`describe()["classes"]["toml_total"] == 4`); `cascade_catalog/` ships **20** with **zero** visibility (`json.dumps(describe())` contains `"cascade_catalog"` 0 times); the `[[alias]]` layer has **no `describe()` axis and no package home** — `dsl.load_aliases_toml(path)` takes a path with no registered directory, which is why rc362's first-ever descriptor landed in `tests/data/`, outside every wheel. For Siona specifically, **domain-word → op is the alias layer and op → chain is the cascade catalog: both halves of the word-problem-to-cascade bridge, and neither is reachable.** The clause is **documented and deliberately NOT implemented** — the `describe()` axes are the user's own rc.
- **§8 / §9** — the *"this ADR closes nothing"* and *"carries no C-side or codegen change"* bullets are struck-through rather than deleted, because the DATE on the measurement they report is what makes the rc363 injection meaningful.

### An ADR-0009 parity break rc362 shipped, found by rebuilding the library before testing

`srmech.mcp._tools._TYPE_LEXICON` and `_ENCODING_HINT` have a **C mirror** (`c/src/srmech_tool_schema.c`, `MCP_TYPE_LEXICON` / `MCP_ENCODING_HINT`) that `test_mcp_defs_type_lexicon_and_hint_mapping` pins exactly. rc362 added `"Q"` and `"Sequence[int | Q | Qalg]"` to the Python maps and **did not mirror them**, so a C-emitted `inputSchema` advertised `"string"` for four params the Python emitter advertises as `"array"` — the row-4 silent-degradation shape ADR-0012 §4.2 names, on the C side. It was invisible on any host whose `libsrmech` predated the change; it surfaced here only because rc363 rebuilt the shared library before running the suite (`[[feedback_verify_the_artifact_under_test_is_the_one_you_think]]`). `CEIL_AMSC_PREFIX["c/src/srmech_carrier_registry.c"]` as-text **191 → 204** and `["c/src/srmech_tool_registry.c"]` **1224 → 1225**; `TOTAL_AS_TEXT` **2943 → 2957**. ### A measurement-instrument failure of my own, recorded because it is the rc's own theme

`tests/test_associator_control_gf_solve_rc360.py` was reported by a local sweep as *"timeout: the monitored command dumped core"*. It is neither a crash nor a regression. **Run alone it passes: 19 passed in 747.6 s** — comfortably inside the 900 s per-file budget that sweep used. So the budget was NOT too low; what killed it was **three of my own pytest processes running concurrently against one tree**, which pushed a 747 s suite past 900 s. Measured 2×2 on `test_one_named_sign_flip_is_the_flexibility_control`, each run alone:

| tree | library | result |
|---|---|---|
| rc362 baseline | pure | **149 s, passed** |
| rc362 baseline | native | **369 s, passed** |
| rc363 (this branch) | native | **363 s, passed** |

Baseline-native and rc363-native are identical within noise, so **rc363 changes nothing about this suite's runtime**; the ~2.5× is native-vs-pure on a call-dense workload and it is present at baseline. The whole file measures **747.6 s** against a 60-minute CI job budget.

⚠️ **A wrong explanation, corrected here rather than left standing.** While the file-level run was pending, this rc first reported the cause as WSL suspending long background processes between tool calls, inferred from an elapsed-time counter that appeared to stall. That inference was WRONG — the suite ran to completion normally, which it could not have done if it were being suspended. The counter looked stalled because separate `wsl` invocations were being read as one continuous observation. The real cause is self-inflicted contention, and it is the more useful lesson: **a test sweep that runs concurrently with other test sweeps measures the scheduler, not the tree.** Serial runs, or none.

Three instrument failures in one rc, all the same shape and all worth naming together, because the ADR this rc implements is about exactly this: a **stale `.so`** answering for a table that had changed; a **prose count** nothing recomputes; and a **timeout** reported as a core dump. In each case the instrument, not the subject, produced the reading — `[[feedback_verify_the_artifact_under_test_is_the_one_you_think]]` and `[[feedback_an_instrument_that_cannot_return_otherwise_is_not_a_measurement]]`.
