The conversion is whole here and nowhere else.

### (6) NOT FILED, FOUND WHILE BUILDING — two findings the work-list did not contain

**(6a) `gh #962` ×3 — an ARMED strict-zero violation that `gh #1542` would have detonated on merge.** Stated exactly, because the first version of this paragraph got it wrong and the correction is the point: this is **not** a pre-existing red on `main`. `_local_task_ids()` scans the working-tree FILESYSTEM, and the note that spells `#T962` — `docs/srmech/notes/t962_cwf_tw_is_not_absent.py` — **does not exist on `main`; `gh #1542` ADDS it.** So `962` is not decidable on `main` today and CI is green there. It went red in this session's tree only because that branch's file was checked out on disk at the time — a real failure, but of the *working tree*, not of `main`.

The consequence is the reason it is fixed here anyway: **the moment `gh #1542` merges, `962` becomes decidable and the three bare `#962` already sitting in the emitted registry become a strict-zero violation on `main`.** rc358 drains them first, so that merge cannot red the branch. (This is the same atomicity trap as item (1), approached from the other side: there, converting a ref armed the guard; here, another PR's *note file* arms it.)

`#T962` being spelled in that note makes the naive fix "convert to `#T962`" — **and that would have been wrong.** This is the `#943` collision the convention warns about, live: `gh #962` is a real CLOSED issue (*"srmech: genome storage perspective + native A-N binding — dev-session tracker (F708–F715)"*) and the three emitting sites cite exactly that (*"Part 2 of #962; validated as F711-F715"*), while the note's `#T962` is an unrelated local task about whether `Tw` is algebraically absent from `cwf_consistency_mod2`. **Topicality decided it: the fix is the `gh ` prefix, not the `T`.** Applied upstream in `tool_schema.py`, so the ratchet **drains** 3 rather than converting 3 (129 → 126).

**(6b) The ref-notation guard has a STRUCTURAL BLIND SPOT — reported, not fixed here.** `c/src/srmech_class_registry.c` embeds the packaged `[class]` TOML descriptors as **decimal byte arrays** (`35, 57, 54, 50` = `#962`). The guard's `_bare_refs` is a textual line scan, so it sees only integers and measures that artifact at **0 bare refs** — while the compiled binary demonstrably ships the decoded text: `strings -a libsrmech.so` recovers `"# Class catalog entry: Genome (the seed worked-instance; #962 Part 2 / #566)"` and a peer `#564` from `hurwitz.toml`. These are real GitHub refs wanting a `gh ` prefix, but the **guard blindness is the actual defect**, and closing it means teaching the ratchet to decode byte-array payloads plus editing the source TOMLs. That is a build, not a text fix, so it is **left for its own rc** rather than forced into this one. Recorded here because a silent blind spot is how the next 15 false links ship. Note that the `#T1022` ship gate is unaffected: `strings` decodes these payloads, so `grep -c '#914'` → 0 covers this route too.

### Verification

Pedantic C build (`-DSRMECH_PEDANTIC=ON`, `-Werror`) clean; `ctest` 10/10; `make test` 30/30; `regen_all.py` idempotent (second pass: **0 files changed**, byte-identical); ref-notation guard + numpy ratchet + JPL audit + C-test wiring + version-pin **62 passed**; edited-module tests (cayley-dickson ×2, genome fiber, hurwitz, matrix cascades, qm single-particle) **98 passed**.

## [0.9.0rc357]

**THE RELEASE TAX.** Two items sat in the tracker classified as *infrastructure* — "a flaky C test" and "some missing CI timeouts" — and were deprioritised on that basis. **That classification is the defect being fixed here.** Neither is a background condition. One is a live `abort()` in a shipped C source file that fires on **1.33% of its own input domain**; the other is a **5-of-42** timeout-coverage rate across the workflows that build and publish every release, including all four publish jobs. "Infrastructure" is what a release-blocking defect gets called when nobody has measured it. Both are measured here, and both are release tax: they are paid on every rc, by everyone, forever, until someone stops calling them background.

*One correction to this rc's own opening framing, because the measurement did not support it.* This rc was opened on the premise that each item had cost a full CI cycle in a single day. **It did not, and the record says so plainly.** rc354's publish failure was repaired with "Re-run failed jobs", not a rebuild: attempt 2's 17 build jobs carry **byte-identical start timestamps** to attempt 1, so they never re-ran — real cost **1:19 of compute and 6:44 of calendar, most of it human reaction time**. And rc356's red run (30419622648) was **not** `#T980`'s flake at all: its only failed job was `pedantic C build • windows-latest` — the genuine MSVC `C4456` shadowing defect that rc356's own commit message takes credit for finding. Re-checked directly for this rc: across the **three** most recent red `srmech-ci` runs (30419622648, 30385819304, 30324962867) there are **11 failed jobs, every one of them a real build or test failure and none transient**. The reclassification from *infrastructure* to *release tax* stands on its own evidence — a 1.33%-per-input abort and a ~12%-per-run flake need no inflated cost estimate — so the estimate is **retracted rather than repeated**. Per `[[feedback_every_doc_edit_faces_falsification]]`, a changelog is not exempt from the discipline it documents.

### (1) `#T980` — an assert that asserted the NEGATION of its own recoverable guard. FIXED AT ROOT.

Filed as *"flaky SIGABRT in the 512-term series test"*. It is not flaky, it is not about 512 terms, and it is not in the test. It is a **deterministic C defect** at `c/src/srmech_rational.c:121`, in `exp_series_accumulate`:

```c
assert(sum_num != NULL);
assert(term_abs <= (uint64_t)INT64_MAX || term_abs == 0);   /* <- line 121 */
if (term_abs > (uint64_t)INT64_MAX) {
    return SRMECH_ERR_OVERFLOW;                             /* <- the SUPPORTED outcome */
}
```

`SRMECH_ERR_OVERFLOW` is a **documented, in-contract result** of `srmech_exp_series_truncate`. `srmech/amsc/rational.py:505` says so in as many words — *"On overflow, fall through to bignum path"* — and does exactly that. So the assert stated the negation of a supported outcome, one line above the guard that returns it. For any input whose common-denominator term `|p|^k · q^(N−k) · (N!/k!)` lands in the band `(INT64_MAX, UINT64_MAX]` — fits u64, so every `exp_series_mul_u64` overflow check passes, but exceeds i64 — an **NDEBUG build returns the correct answer while an asserts-live build `abort()`s the host.**

This is the rc289 `genome_list_genomes` defect class recurring verbatim: **one projection correct, the other killing the host** — precisely what ADR-0009's co-equal-projections invariant exists to forbid. The `asserts-live-smoke` cell (#937) was doing exactly the job it was built for.

**The fix is positional, not logical.** An `assert` may only encode something impossible *by construction*; a condition that a recoverable guard exists to handle is by definition possible. The assert was right in content and wrong in **position** — below the guard it becomes a genuine by-construction invariant, and the JPL Rule-5 count is preserved (2 asserts, no ratchet movement):

```c
assert(sum_num != NULL);
if (term_abs > (uint64_t)INT64_MAX) {
    return SRMECH_ERR_OVERFLOW;
}
assert(term_abs <= (uint64_t)INT64_MAX);   /* invariant by construction here */
```

**Evidence — reproduced, then killed, then bounded exhaustively.**

| step | result |
|---|---|
| Direct ctypes, asserts-live build, `(p=-40, q=1, N=12)` | `srmech_rational.c:121: exp_series_accumulate: Assertion ... failed` — **SIGABRT, exit 134, 100% deterministic** |
| Same input, same build, after the fix | `rc=4` (`SRMECH_ERR_OVERFLOW`), wrapper completes on the bignum path |
| **Exhaustive** sweep of the entire int64 fast-path domain (`p∈[-40,40] × q∈[1,40] × N∈[0,20]` = **68,040** combos), asserts-live | **0 aborts.** 34,310 `OK`; 33,730 `ERR_OVERFLOW` |
| Independent Python replication of the same arithmetic | **902 combos (1.33%)** would have hit the old assert; its `OK` count of **34,310 matches the C library exactly**, validating the model |
| Affected test, **100 runs**, `PYTHONHASHSEED` 0–99, asserts-live | **100 passed, 0 failed, 0 SIGABRT** (19 tests/run) |

**The flake is dead at the root, not routed around.** The 100 runs span `PYTHONHASHSEED` 0–99 against an asserts-live library (`nm -D` confirms `__assert_fail` is present, so a green result is not a stripped-assert artifact), and they include **seed 21 — the seed that was 8/8 SIGABRT before this fix**. No retry decorator, no skip, no `-k` filter, no rerun was added: routing around a flake is the thing this rc exists to stop.

The 33,730 overflow returns decompose as **902** that reach the moved assert, **32,431** that overflow earlier in u64 and never get there, and **397** at the sum accumulation *after* it — so the assert-firing subset is the 1.33%, not the whole overflow class. **No shipped wheel was ever affected**: `pyproject.toml:163` pins `cmake.build-type = "Release"`, so every published artifact is NDEBUG and returns the correct value.

*Ruled out, with reasons.* **Not** stack overflow or 512-term recursion — there is no recursion on this path, and the crashing path is the int64 fast path gated to `num_terms <= 20` (`_SAFE_C_N`, `rational.py:485`); the "512" in the tracker title is the parametrize `max_terms`, the upper bound of a random draw, not the N at the crash (observed crashing N: 4–20). **Not** a C arena or memory error — line 496 is plain `c_int64` scalars, and the caller-arena bignum path at line 516 is never reached for these inputs. **Not** fork-plus-threads — the reproduction used no xdist, no `--forked`, one process, one thread; `--forked` is the *containment* that stopped the abort coring the whole CI run, not the cause.

**The same defect shape, found and fixed in three more places.** A scan of all 135 `c/src/*.c` for asserts whose condition is the logical negation of the recoverable guard immediately following (excluding the correct NULL-contract idiom) found three peers:

| site | before | status |
|---|---|---|
| `srmech_rational.c:121` | asserted `term_abs <= INT64_MAX` above the guard returning `ERR_OVERFLOW` | the live bug; **actively firing** |
| `srmech_platform.c` `srmech_plat_mkdir` | asserted `path[0] != '\0'` above the guard returning `ERR_BAD_INPUT` | latent only because no test drives an empty path |
| `srmech_platform.c` `srmech_plat_file_remove` | identical | latent, same reason |
| `srmech_platform.c` `srmech_plat_file_replace` | **strictly worse** — asserted non-empty `src`/`dst` while its guard checked **only NULL** | an empty string aborted with **no recoverable peer at all**; the empty-path case now returns `ERR_BAD_INPUT`, matching its two siblings |

**Honest bound on that scan:** it finds only the *"assert negates its own guard within 3 lines"* shape. rc289's `genome_list_genomes` was the **wider** kind — assert in the callee, recoverable contract in the caller — which this scan cannot see. That class is not claimed closed.

**(1b) A second, independent defect: the failure was not reproducible from its own report.** `tests/test_qalg_series_c_rc156.py:78` seeded its RNG as `random.Random(0xC156 ^ hash(name) & 0xFFFF)`. **`hash(str)` is `PYTHONHASHSEED`-salted and nothing pinned it** — CI runs `pytest tests/ -q -n auto --forked -p no:randomly` (`srmech-ci.yml:743`), and `-p no:randomly` disables the one plugin that would have set it. So the 120 draws were a **fresh random sample in every process**: this was never a fixed-seed test, and a red run could not be replayed from its own failure output. That is the entire *"same commit, red then green"* signature. Measured: `PYTHONHASHSEED=21` → 8/8 SIGABRT, `PYTHONHASHSEED=22` → 8/8 pass — fully deterministic per seed, a lottery across seeds. **Both defects are real and neither substitutes for the other:** fixing only the seed would have *hidden* a live C abort; fixing only the assert would have left a test whose failures cannot be reproduced. The seed is now a literal per op, and the four inputs that actually aborted — `(-40,1,12)`, `(-28,1,16)`, `(-32,25,14)`, `(34,32,9)` — ship as **explicit regression pins** that run in every process instead of ~6% of them.

### (2) `#T951` — 5 of 42 jobs had a timeout. Now 42 of 42.

Three premises in the tracker entry did not survive measurement, and correcting them changed the ranking. "No job timeouts" was **false for the hot path** — rc352 already put `timeout-minutes: 60` on all five `srmech-ci` jobs under this same task ID. But **37 of 42 jobs repo-wide had none**, including **all four publish jobs, which is where rc354 actually died**, and they ran to GitHub's 360-minute default.

**Timeouts are now derived, not felt.** One rule, applied uniformly and documented in the YAML at each site:

> `T = ⌈max_observed⌉ + max(⌈0.5 × max_observed⌉, 10 min)`

The 50% term covers growth across an rc sprint. The **10-minute floor** is load-bearing: measured p50→max spread is ≤2 min in *absolute* terms on every job regardless of length (a slow pip/apt/image fetch costs minutes whether a job runs 30s or 45min), so purely proportional headroom would make the **shortest** jobs the tightest and turn the guard itself into a flake source.

| workflow | job | max observed | timeout |
|---|---|---|---|
| `srmech-ci` | `build-and-test` | 15:17 | 60 → **26** |
| | `asserts-live-smoke` | 19:10 | 60 → **30** |
| | `pedantic-build` | 1:47 | 60 → **12** |
| | `pure-wheel-build` | 0:51 | 60 → **11** |
| | `fallback-no-native` | 45:34 | 60 → **70** *(raised)* |
| `srmech-publish` | `build-wheels` | 4:08 | none → **15** |
| | `build-sdist` / `build-pure-wheel` | 0:32 / 0:29 | none → **11** |
| | `publish` | 1:43 | none → **12** |
| `srmech-autotag` | `maybe-tag` | 0:20 | none → **11** |
| `codeql` | `analyze` | 1:37 | none → **20** |

Two of these are deliberate departures, flagged rather than silently fudged. **`fallback-no-native` goes UP.** Its uniform 60 gave **31.7% headroom — the tightest ratio in the repo** — over a job that has grown 44:01 (rc351) → 45:34 (rc356), ≈18.6 s/rc; at that rate 60:00 binds in ~47 rcs, about two weeks, and it binds as a *false* timeout on a healthy run. The asymmetry decides it: a false trip costs a full 45-minute cycle, while catching a genuine hang at 70 instead of 60 costs 10 extra minutes. Reverse it when the pure-suite split (`#T1007`) lands. **`codeql` gets 20, not the rule's 12**, because its runtime scales with tree growth rather than per-run variance and 24 samples of a growing repo is weak evidence for a ceiling. The **31 dormant** sister-subtree jobs (antikythera / chess / ephemerides, last run 5–7 weeks ago) get a uniform **60** labelled in the YAML as **explicitly UNDERIVED** — deriving real numbers would mean running dormant workflows just to time them, and 60 still reclaims 6× against the 360-minute default.

**One retry, on one leg, for one mechanically-defined failure class.** rc354 died in `publish` when the runner failed to pull `ghcr.io/pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish:release-v1` — the action's `action.yml` is a composite that generates a Docker trampoline — with `net/http: request canceled (Client.Timeout awaiting headers)` **19 seconds in, before the entrypoint ran, with zero bytes uploaded**. Retry coverage across all 15 workflows was **zero**. The TestPyPI leg now gets exactly one retry, gated on three **conjunctive** conditions satisfied by rc354 and by no other observed failure: **position** (failed during image resolution, before the entrypoint), **effect** (no bytes uploaded, so a retry resumes from identical state), and **signature** (a *transport* error, not an HTTP application error — a 400/403/409 from TestPyPI is not transient). It is a duplicate step keyed on `steps.tpypi_1.outcome`, **not** a third-party retry action, because such an action is itself an external fetch and would reintroduce the exact failure mode it is meant to remove.

The load-bearing property: **this cannot convert red→green for a deterministic failure.** A bad token, bad metadata or a duplicate filename fails attempt 2 identically and the job goes red, costing one extra ~1:23 attempt. A partial upload also stays red. The **production PyPI leg is deliberately left single-shot** — clean releases are rare and human-gated, and a failure there should reach a human.

**What was deliberately NOT shipped, and why.** A **blanket retry on test steps** would be *worse than the status quo*: all 11 failed jobs across the three most recent red `srmech-ci` runs were real failures and none were transient, so a blanket retry would have masked eleven true reds and doubled the cost of each. **`-x` / `--maxfail=N`** on the pure suite — the obvious "make red runs cheap" move — destroys the full failure inventory that cell exists to produce, and is the same family as the `-k` narrowing the job's own comment already rejects on record. **`fail-fast: true`** is deliberately `false` in 13 places; under ADR-0009 every projection must report. **Pre-pulling the ghcr.io image** was rejected on mechanics: `docker pull` always resolves tag→digest against the registry, so it removes no network dependency — it would look like hardening while doing nothing, i.e. a dead instrumentation seam. **`skip-existing: true`** changes semantics and masks a genuine already-published signal for a case never observed.

**Finally, the pure cell's evidence is preserved.** One pytest step is **42:56 of a 43:32 job (98.6%)**, structurally all-or-nothing: a failure at any point discarded all of it *and* skipped the downstream skip-audit, so a red run lost that signal too. `pytest-pure.log` was `tee`'d and **never uploaded** (`grep -c upload-artifact srmech-ci.yml` → 0), surviving only in the web log. It now uploads with `if: always()` — the failing run being exactly the one whose log is worth having. This does not make the run faster; it makes a red run **informative** instead of merely expensive.

## [0.9.0rc356]

**THE SAME SWEEP AS rc355, ONE LAYER DOWN.** rc355 closed four places where the *Python* verification layer could not detect a defect. This rc is the C-side and cross-projection instance of the identical shape: **a C ratchet that never runs, a test that lost its own contract, and two projections that disagree about what an error IS.** ADR-0003 says the C host stands alone; ADR-0009 says the projections are co-equal. Neither was verifiable while these held. Every guard ships with its red-then-green recorded, and — per rc355's own lesson — with evidence that the guard is REACHED.

**(1) 0 of 30 C tests were executed by any automation, local or CI (`#T953`).** The finding was filed as "`test_srmech_genome.c` is wired into no CI gate". That is true and it is not one file. `docs/srmech/CMakeLists.txt` wired **nine** of the thirty `c/test/*.c` binaries, and there was no `enable_testing()`, no `add_test()`, and **no `ctest` step in any workflow** — the `pedantic-build` job (`srmech-ci.yml:556`) was Configure + Build, so CI compiled nine test binaries on three OSes and threw them away. The other twenty-one were referenced nowhere. The `make test` target — which `c/README.md` documents as *the* local flow — looked for `test/test_srmech.c`, **a file that has never existed in this tree**, printed `(Phase B1: no test_srmech.c yet — skipping)` and exited 0. Both supposedly-independent enforcement paths were compile-only or no-op green.

*The cost, measured.* `test_srmech_progress_tick.c` — the smoke for the §101 cancel channel — **has been RED since rc307, roughly 48 rcs.** rc307 reinterpreted `ws_len` on the three fiedler symbols from a COUNT OF DOUBLES to BYTES (a breaking wire-contract change that bumped `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` 9 → 10, documented at `c/include/srmech.h:180-196`) and migrated two of the three test callers. The third kept passing `36u`, the doubles count; `srmech_laplacian_fiedler_sparse_arena_bytes(4)` is 256 bytes, so the call was declined by the arena guard at `srmech_laplacian.c:2165` **before the tick loop was ever entered** and returned `SRMECH_ERR_BAD_INPUT` where it asserted `SRMECH_CANCELLED`. CI built it every time. The two migrated siblings even ship the regression assertion *"old doubles-count ws_len (8*n) -> BAD_INPUT"* — the tests that encode the migration and the caller that missed it were in the same commit.

**What ships.** `enable_testing()` + `add_test()` for the nine already in the matrix **plus `test_srmech_genome`**, and a real `ctest --test-dir build --build-config Release --output-on-failure` step in `pedantic-build`. Not `|| true`: a test run that cannot fail the build is the compile-only gate wearing a run step's name. `make test` now builds and runs **all thirty** (`-I$(SRCDIR)` so `test_srmech_config.c` / `test_srmech_text_fold.c` find their private headers; each binary runs with `$(BUILD)` as cwd, because several write scratch files relative to it and running from `c/` drops that litter into the source tree). Measured: **30 passed, 0 failed, 0 warnings, 551 ms for the whole set** — there was never a runtime argument against running them.

*Why ten and not thirty, stated plainly.* The residual twenty are green under gcc on WSL2 and have **never been built by MSVC**, and this matrix compiles `/WX`. Wiring twenty unverifiable files at once is how a wiring rc lands red, which is the one outcome worse than the gap it closes: a permanently-red gate everyone learns to ignore. They land in batches, each verified on the 3-OS matrix. `tests/test_c_test_wiring_rc356.py` holds a **DOWN-ONLY CEIL of 20** so the residual drains and cannot grow, and asserts the structure around it: `enable_testing()` present, every `add_executable` also `add_test`-registered (the compile-only shape itself), no stale registration, the workflow actually invokes `ctest`, and `make test` is not back to the Phase-B1 stub.

*The wiring paid for itself on day one: the first MSVC compile of a newly-wired test FAILED (`#T953`).* `test_srmech_genome.c` had never been compiled by MSVC before this rc, because it was in no build at all. Its first entry into the pedantic matrix immediately surfaced **two latent C4456 `declaration hides previous local declaration` defects** — fatal under `/WX`, and invisible on a file that had been green under gcc and clang on every prior run, because **gcc does not warn on shadowing without an explicit `-Wshadow`**. Linux and macOS had nothing to say about a defect that was there the whole time. That is the gate doing precisely the job it was wired to do, on day one, and it is not an argument for backing the wiring out.

| site | shadowed | what the inner variable actually is | renamed to |
|------|----------|--------------------------------------|------------|
| `:291` | `unsigned char body[24]` at `:172` (the §44 in-memory body) | the on-disk byte length of `turns.bin`, `ftell`-ed for the arena-scaling comparison | `turns_bin_len` |
| `:1639` | `srmech_status_t st` at `:184` (the `genome_save` status) | the verdict of the rc280 `srmech_genome_section_counts` calls, and nothing else | `counts_st` |

Scoped renames only — no logic change, no restructuring, no scope widened, and the neighbouring `body_scaled` (a distinct identifier a mechanical replace would have corrupted) left alone. **A tree-wide sweep establishes these were the only two:** `gcc -std=gnu11 -Wshadow` over all 31 `c/test/*.c` **and** every `c/src/*.c`, at the real build's standard and include paths, reports exactly those 2 before and **0 after**. That sweep is strictly BROADER than C4456 — `-Wshadow` also flags locals shadowing parameters and globals (C4457 / C4459, likewise `/W4` and likewise fatal here) — and it found none of those either, so **the twenty tests still behind `CEIL_UNWIRED_C_TESTS` carry no shadowing defect waiting to fire when they are drained.** It also restates the batching argument as measurement rather than caution: ONE file entering the matrix produced two real errors; twenty entering together would have produced their sum at once, in a gate nobody could bisect. Verified after the rename on the paths reachable locally — `make test` **30 passed, 0 failed**; `ctest` **10/10** against a `-DSRMECH_PEDANTIC=ON` (`-Werror`) build; `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` still 10 in both `c/include/srmech.h` and `_native.py`, a test file exporting nothing. **The MSVC path itself cannot be verified locally: CI is the only MSVC verification available, and it gates.**

*The blocker that made `#T953`'s named file unwireable, fixed rather than routed around.* `test_srmech_genome.c`'s `ensure_dir()` was a **NO-OP under `_WIN32`** — `return system(NULL) ? 0 : 0;`, with the comment *"the parity harness runs on Linux"* — so the temp dir was never created and every save would have failed on `windows-latest`. It now does a real `_mkdir` / `mkdir`, drops the shell-out entirely (removing a `system()` escape from the test tree), removes the two files a genome dir can hold to preserve the freshness the old `rm -rf` provided, and **probes that the directory is genuinely writable**, reporting through the file's own `check_true` channel. That last part matters: all 26 call sites ignore the return value, so a status code alone would have been a guard nobody reads.

**(2) The cancel channel was RIGHT. The TEST was wrong (`#T977`).** Filed as "the cancel channel is not returning its own status". It is not: `status=2` is `SRMECH_ERR_BAD_INPUT` and the `SRMECH_CANCELLED` 7 was never set, swallowed or overwritten — the arena guard returns before the power-iteration loop, so the tick never fires and `fiedler_file_iterate`'s `return SRMECH_CANCELLED` (`srmech_laplacian.c:2121`) is never reached. Instrumented over the same graph and the same buffer, varying only `ws_len`: `36` → `st=2, ticks=0`; `arena_bytes(4)` = `256` → `st=7, ticks=3, out_vec` zeroed. **`ticks=0` is the decisive evidence** — the callback is never invoked, so no cancel is ever requested. **No library code was changed and the contract was not touched**; the fixture now sizes its arena through the canonical helper, matching its two migrated siblings. Fixing correct code to satisfy a wrong assertion would have broken the ABI-10 contract to preserve a stale caller.

**(3) Two projections that disagree about what an error IS (`#T954`).** §44 defines a cap label as UTF-8 bytes up to the first NUL, and **both writer halves enforce it** (`_pack_cap` encodes UTF-8; the C `genome_pack_cap` documents its input as bytes "already UTF-8"), so no genome srmech wrote can carry a label that fails to decode. One that does is *ungrammatical* — the same class as `_stream_body_blocks`' "unrecognised block kind byte", which has raised `GenomeBoundingError` from three branches away in the same generator all along.

Measured on the rc355 tree, manifest present, one CHROM label byte set to `0xFF`: **five reads SPLIT** (`catalog` / `census` / `content` / `registry` / `gene_express_plan` → `GenomeBoundingError` compiled, `UnicodeDecodeError` scripting) and the six that appeared to AGREE agreed on the **wrong type** — a raw codec exception leaked through the `GenomeBoundingError` normalisation boundary it was raised inside. `UnicodeDecodeError` names a codec, not a genome: no path, no genome identity, nothing to distinguish it from a locale bug in the caller's own code. A caller could not write one `except` clause that held on both hosts.

**The C half is the serious one, and it is the opposite of what the finding assumed.** The compiled projection's `GenomeBoundingError` above was the rc342 digest bound firing on a byte flip that happened to break the digest too — the right answer for an unrelated reason. Asked where no committed digest can answer for it (§44 rebuild-by-scan, manifest absent, coupling supplied), **the C returned `SRMECH_OK` and copied the raw `0xFF` into its own canonical JSON output**, which RFC 8259 §8.1 then makes invalid JSON: measured status 0, `0xFF` at output byte 825, inside `"label": "g\xffography"`. The `UnicodeDecodeError` seen there was not C rejecting anything — it was the ctypes shim choking on C's success. A bare-C host got success plus a mangled label and no signal at all. `srmech_genome.c` says *"labels are UTF-8"* four times and checked it nowhere; labels were `memcpy`'d as opaque bytes.

**Both halves fixed, because fixing only Python leaves the bare-C host silently accepting.** C: a new file-local `genome_label_is_utf8` (same acceptance set as `txt_utf8_next` in `srmech_text.c` and as Python's `bytes.decode("utf-8")` — stray continuation bytes, overlong forms, truncated sequences, surrogates and > U+10FFFF all rejected), wired into **both** cap-label readers. That second one is the point: `genome_decode_label` serves catalog/census/registry, but the GENE surface reads through `genome_gene_label`, so validating only the first left `srmech_genome_genes` still emitting a raw undecodable label. All twelve `genome_gene_label` call sites already treat `NULL` as `SRMECH_ERR_BAD_INPUT`, so no site silently skips a gene it cannot name. Python: the five bare `.decode("utf-8")` strand sites (`_unpack_fiber_cap`, `_unpack_oct_fiber_cap`, `_unpack_cap`, `_active_telomere_label`, `_ScanState.fold`) route through `genome._decode_label`, which chains the original exception so the byte offset is not lost — as rc294 chained its `OSError`. **After: every row of the matrix reads `GenomeBoundingError` in both projections**, and both cap kinds are covered.

*Two corrections to the filed analysis, recorded because a wrong reason survives longer than a wrong answer.* The report described a manifest-less row where `genome_content` returns a successful read; **it does not reproduce, and a CLEAN control shows why the row was uninformative** — with the manifest removed and no `coupling` passed, a clean untouched genome raises `GenomeBoundingError` on the same reads, so that row was measuring "no rebuild width supplied", not the label. The decisive cell is manifest-absent **with** coupling, which is the one quoted above. Second: an attempt to isolate the C by repairing the manifest's digests was **discarded as inconclusive** — a control that made the *same byte position* a VALID UTF-8 change still returned status 2, proving the repair was incomplete and that cell proved nothing about UTF-8 either way.

*Also recorded, not fixed here.* `tests/test_genome_read_bound_global_rc342.py:259` forces three `has_native_genome*` gates off to build its "scripting" projection, but `genes()` gates on `has_native_genome_genes()`, a different symbol — **there are 44 such gates**, so that helper's pure runs partly dispatched into C. The new test flips all 44 and asserts the count stays ≥ 40, so a partial flip cannot quietly weaken it.

**Red-then-green, recorded.** (1) HEAD's `progress_tick` fixture restored under the new wiring → **`ctest` exits 8, `test_srmech_progress_tick (Failed)`**; rc356's fixture → exit 0, 10/10 in 0.06 s — i.e. the new run step would have caught the actual rc307 regression. `make test` with the same planted fixture → `29 passed, 1 failed`, exit 2; restored → `30 passed, 0 failed`, exit 0. All six assertions in `test_c_test_wiring_rc356.py` planted individually (`enable_testing()` commented out; an `add_executable` without its `add_test`; a registration with no source; three names dropped to raise the unwired count; `|| true` appended to the ctest step; the Phase-B1 stub restored) → each fails exactly its own assertion, `6 passed` restored. `ensure_dir`'s probe with the old `_WIN32` no-op planted and an unwritable base → `FAIL ensure_dir` + the stderr diagnosis; unplanted → `231 passed, 0 failed`. (3) the C guard measured before and after on the identical store: `RAW C status=0` with `0xFF` at output byte 825 → `RAW C status=2`, while the clean and valid-UTF-8 controls stay `status=0` and read back unchanged.

*Three false-positive traps hit while writing these guards, kept as comments where they bit.* A whole-file substring search for the Phase-B1 stub matched the **new recipe's own comment quoting it**; a commented-out `enable_testing()` **satisfied** its own presence check (the red-team run PASSED until comments were exempted); and the "no bare label decode remains" check matched `_decode_label`'s **own docstring**. Same class as the ref-notation guard's code-span exemption: a mechanical check that cannot tell a description of the defect from the defect reports the fix as the bug.

**Version SSOT bumped in all five locations** (`pyproject.toml`, `pyproject-pure.toml`, `srmech/version.py`, `c/include/srmech.h`, and the pinned string in `tests/test_signal_processing_scaffolding.py`). **`SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` STAYS 10.** No exported signature changed shape, no struct grew, no callback typedef was added and no symbol was removed: `genome_label_is_utf8`, `genome_decode_label` and `genome_gene_label` are all `static`, and what changed is the VERDICT the genome read symbols return on malformed input, not the wire format any caller marshals. This is the deliberate contrast with rc307 — that bump was required because the *unit* of an existing parameter was reinterpreted, so every external caller had to change what it passes; here a caller passes exactly what it passed before. No public callable was added or renamed (`_decode_label` is private), so `tools.total` is unchanged and the four-generated-file public-callable ripple gate is not triggered.

## [0.9.0rc355]

**THE VERIFICATION LAYER IS THE SUBJECT. Every item here is a place where a gate certified SHAPE and could not certify TRUTH** — a test that could only fail in one direction, two schemas shipped side by side that nobody compared to each other, prose that stated two true things without saying they were the same thing, and an invariant with no guard at all. This session measured that shape repeatedly; these are the instances that were found but not yet closed. **Every guard below ships with its red-then-green demonstration recorded**, because a guard shipped without evidence that it fires is exactly the defect class this rc exists to close.

**(1) A ℍ-choice-invariance guard that could only ever fail DOWNWARD (`#T996`).** `tests/test_quaternion_subalgebra_stabilizer.py:255` reduced the worst spectral deviation as `_scalar(max(reference[i] - spectrum[i] for i in range(6)))` — the Class-K magnitude applied OUTSIDE the fold, so `max` ran over **signed** differences and the magnitude only rectified the single already-selected extremum. The Killing spectrum is `sorted()` and every eigenvalue is negative, so any UPWARD corruption re-sorts to the top, leaves the leading signed differences at ~0, and parks the outlier at a large NEGATIVE value that `max` discards. **Measured on the shipped form: `+1e6`, `+1e-6` and `+1e-9` injected on `killing_spectrum[0]` for every non-reference ℍ all reported deviation `1.776e-15` and PASSED.** The magnitude now folds per element — max-of-magnitudes, which is what "worst deviation" means — and the same three corruptions fail at `9.99999e+05` / `9.99999e-07` / `9.99998e-10`, i.e. the guard now fires at the tolerance boundary and not only on sledgehammers. Class-K discipline is unchanged: still `cascade.magnitude`, never `abs()`; only the fold order moved.

*Two things deliberately NOT done.* The assertion was **not** tightened to `== 0.0` to match the test's name: measured across ℍ = 2..7 the honest residual is `1.776e-15` and **0 of 36 entries satisfy `reference[i] == spectrum[i]`**, so the invariant is tolerance-exact at `_BIT_EXACT` (1e-10) and "bit-identical" is the NAME over-claiming, not the tolerance being slack — tightening it would turn the test red on honest input. The docstring now says so. And the sibling reductions at `:230-231` were **not** batch-converted: `_scalar(max(low) - min(low))` takes max-minus-min of one list, non-negative by construction, so magnitude-outside is harmless there. A repo-wide sweep for `magnitude(max(` / `_scalar(max(` / `_scalar(min(` / `_scalar(sum(` over `tests/`, `srmech/` and `tools/` returns those two sound lines and no second instance of the defect.

**(2) Two schemas ship in every wheel and nothing compared them to each other (`#T993`).** `ToolEntry.parameters` becomes `inputSchema.properties` / `.required` via `srmech/mcp/_tools.py:289`; `ToolEntry.example["input"]` is the dict a reader copies to make that call. `srmech/amsc/tool_schema.py:28` declares the contract in one line — `"input": {"data": "b'abc'"}`, a kwargs map whose keys are parameter names — and **nothing enforced it**. The existing guards are each sound and each structurally blind to this: `test_mcp.py:128` checks property KEYS against Anthropic's grammar and never reads `example`; `test_mcp.py:155` checks `required ⊆ properties`, both sides derived from `parameters`; the rc353 strict-zero gate stringifies the example and greps it; and `tools/run_worked_examples.py` selects on `worked` and never reads `input` at all.

**Measured on the rc354 tree: 189 of 386 input-bearing entries publish an example that is INVALID under their own live `inputSchema` — 36.8% of all 513 srmech tools.** It ships: 383 `"input":` literals are compiled into `docs/srmech/c/src/srmech_tool_registry.c` and the same dicts sit in `srmech/amsc/_tool_docs.py` inside the wheel, reaching users through `describe()`, the MCP tool list and the compiled-in C registry — the same three surfaces the ref-notation arc measured. Worst single row: `frame_carrier_compare` publishes three keys against eight parameters for **0 hits and 6 required missing**. `jacobi_sncndn_series_truncate` publishes the MATH names `u` and `m` against `numerator` / `denominator` / `m_numerator` / `m_denominator`, so a reader who follows it gets a `TypeError`. `best_rational` publishes `'numerator/denominator'` as one slash-joined key — the example that exists to prevent the int-pair misuse is itself unpassable.

**What ships is `tests/test_tool_example_input_schema_rc355.py`: two STRICT ZEROS and a per-class DOWN-ONLY CEIL.** Strict zero 1 — an `input` dict may not mix numeric call indices with parameter names (measured 0, held at 0); that ambiguous blend is the one shape from which no consumer can recover the author's intent. Strict zero 2 — when `input` and `output` are BOTH dicts they are two halves of one indexed transcript and their keysets must be equal (measured **95 pairs, 95 agree, 0 disagree**); this is what makes the 87-row numeric-index ceiling safe to hold rather than drain in a rush. The ceiling is **per class, never one global number**, per the rc354 rule that a regression must not hide behind an unrelated fix: `mixed_param_and_prose` 15, `missing_required` 6, `zero_param_with_keys` 11, `all_prose_labels` 70, `numeric_call_index` 87. It also fails when a ceiling sits ABOVE the true count, so drain-then-lower must happen in one commit.

*The structural finding under the count, recorded because a ceiling alone will never drain it.* `example["input"]` carries **three incompatible conventions** and the docstring blesses only one. **157 of the 189** (87 numeric call indices + 70 free-prose labels) are not sloppy kwargs — they are a DIFFERENT FIELD wearing the `input` name, and the numeric one is internally disciplined (the 95/95 keyset agreement above). The landable fix is to move those two forms to a separate `scenarios` key so `input` is strictly a kwargs map, taking 189 → 21 by rename alone; the residual 21 (`mixed_param_and_prose` + `missing_required`) are unambiguous defects under the tree's own documented contract and are the drain-first target for a third strict zero. That rename is **deliberately not in this rc**: it touches every consumer plus 383 generated C literals, and this rc ships the missing GUARD, not a mechanical batch-convert.

**(3) `one.py` stated `2+4+8` and `1+3+7+3` and never said they were the same fourteen (`#T982`).** Both numbers are TRUE, both equal 14, both appear within 130 lines of each other, and no sentence named them apart — so a reader shown one meets the other as a contradiction. The code was never wrong: `BLOCK_DIMS` is `(2,4,8)` at `one.py`, `One.partition` returns `(1,3,7,3)`, and the module-docstring table already carries both an `ℝ·1` column and an `Im 𝔸ₙ` column. What was missing is the naming hinge, and `BLOCK_DIMS` is in fact never CONSUMED inside `one.py` (only `IMAG_DIMS` drives `to_matrix` / `_blocks_from_flat` / `_adjoint_blocks_pure`), which is precisely why the two were never forced to be named apart. They now are, in both directions: the **CARRIER partition** `(1+1)+(1+3)+(1+7) = 2+4+8` groups the 14 by WHICH ALGEBRA a direction lives in (read across the rows); the **OPERATOR partition** `1+3+7+3` groups the SAME 14 by WHAT ROLE a direction plays (read down the columns). Neither refines the other and neither is "the" partition.

*Ripple, because this prose SHIPS.* The `One.dim` wording is duplicated verbatim in the packaged class descriptor `_research/class_catalog/one.toml` (surfaced through `make_class("One").dim`) and in the declared bit-exact Rosetta peer `srmech/qm/hurwitz.py`, which carried the carrier-only reading with no hinge at all — both corrected. And the generated `hurwitz_planes` worked example literally rendered the conflation to MCP users as `imag dims 1,3,7 -> 2+4+8 = 14`, which reads as "1,3,7 sums to 2+4+8"; fixed at its CURATED source and regenerated, never hand-edited in `_tool_docs.py`.

**(4) The A–N slot tables had no shape guard at all (`#T1017`).** `AN_IMAG_SLOTS` and `GRAMMAR_SLOTS` are the tables that assign the 14 A–N classes to the substrate's axes, and nothing validated them. Falsified by construction on the rc354 tree: an **8-label heptad for 7 axes**, an all-empty table, a duplicate-label table and a garbage-label table were **ALL ACCEPTED** by `the_one`; a 2-block table raised a bare `IndexError` from tuple indexing, which is an accident, not a guard. `Block` was a bare frozen dataclass, so `Block(algebra="O", n=3, imag=<7 axes>, an_imag_slots=<8 labels>)` constructed cleanly. The only thing standing between the tree and a wrong shipped value was a **literal value pin** in `tests/test_one_rc49.py` — which cannot survive a refactor that edits constant and literal in lockstep, says nothing about `Block` construction, and pins ORDER, the one thing the framework has not derived.

`_validate_slot_shape()` now runs at import and `Block.__post_init__` guards direct construction. It also **mechanises the hinge from (3)**: `1 + len(Im block)` must equal `BLOCK_DIMS`, which is the one place the two partitions of the same 14 are forced to agree — before rc355 that was asserted in prose and checked nowhere.

⛔ **SHAPE ONLY, and the constraint is itself a test.** The guard checks how many labels sit where and that the label SET is exactly A–N. It never checks WHICH label sits at WHICH axis: the heptad ordering `D,E,F,G,K,L,M` is ALPHABETICAL and was never derived, so pinning it would mint a claim the framework has not made. The bijection check is `sorted(...)` precisely so it is order-blind, and `test_slot_shape_guard_is_order_blind` asserts that order-blindness directly — replacing the SET check with a positional pin turns it RED, so a future "tightening" into an ordering claim cannot land quietly.

*Writing those tests reproduced this rc's own theme, so the fix is recorded here rather than smoothed over.* With `_validate_slot_shape()`'s **call site** commented out and the function left intact, all four of the new guard tests still PASSED — they call the function directly, so they verify its logic and say nothing about whether anything invokes it. A guard nobody calls is prose. `test_slot_shape_guard_actually_RUNS_at_import` closes it by mutating the shipped heptad literal in the module's real source, exec'ing it, and requiring `ValueError`, with the unmutated source exec'd as the control. The guard's honest LIMIT is stated in both the docstring and the test: it runs ONCE at import over the constants as WRITTEN IN THE FILE — which is the actual failure mode, a wrong table committed to source — and cannot see a post-import rebinding, where only `Block`'s per-axis length check fires.

**Red-then-green, recorded for every guard.** (1) shipped form + `{+1e6, +1e-6, +1e-9}` → `1 passed` three times; fixed form, same three → `1 failed` three times with the true deviation reported; clean → `12 passed`. (2) four planted defects — a prose key on a clean entry, a numeric/named blend, a mismatched input/output keyset, and a DRAINED row — fire the ceiling, strict zero 1, strict zero 2 and the stale-ceiling assertion respectively; unplanted → `4 passed`. (4) guards stripped → all four corrupted tables accepted; call site alone removed → the wiring test alone fails; SET check replaced by an ORDER claim → the order-blind test alone fails; restored → `44 passed`.

**Version SSOT bumped in all five locations** (`pyproject.toml`, `pyproject-pure.toml`, `srmech/version.py`, `c/include/srmech.h`, and the pinned string in `tests/test_signal_processing_scaffolding.py`). No public callable added or renamed — `_validate_slot_shape` is private and `__post_init__` is a dunder — so `tools.total` is unchanged and the four-generated-file public-callable ripple gate is not triggered. No ABI change; `AN_IMAG_SLOTS` has no C peer.

## [0.9.0rc354]

**FOUR REPAIRS, ALL OF THE SAME KIND: a surface that told a reader something the code did not deliver.** The chirality classifier claimed exact Class-N ratios and computed floats; the granularity note separated three senses of "the cube" and was missing a fourth; a four-word carrier vocabulary was proposed for data that does not determine it; and 427 worked examples were checked for shape but never executed.

**(1) `classify_chirality_harmonic` goes EXACT — Class-N `Q`, not `float` (F1336).** `harmonics.py` has carried, since rc154, a comment stating the op composes "**Class-N** exact ratios". Through rc353 it read the vector as `float`, so the claim was false of the code. Every element is now promoted through `q.to_q` (a float's `as_integer_ratio` is EXACT, so nothing is approximated on the way in), the whole probe runs on ONE common denominator in bignum integers — Class-I `cyclic.gcd` supplies the lcm — and each score is an exact `Q` formed once. `_spectral_scores` **returns `Q`** now; call `float(score)` for a rendering. `dc_threshold` accepts `int` / `float` / `Q` and its declared type stays `"float"`, so no MCP coercer and no C-registry type change was needed.

*Three reachable defect families, each reproduced against the shipped rc353 op and each now a test:* **(i) entries past 2^53** — `[3*(2**53-1), -(2**53-1)]` has exact DC score 1/2 → harmonic 1 and returned 2 on every interpreter, because the loss is in `float(v)` BEFORE any summing; **(ii) INTERPRETER-DEPENDENT verdicts** — CPython >= 3.12 made built-in `sum()` Neumaier-compensated, so an all-double vector with exact DC 1/2 classified 2 on 3.10/3.11 and 1 on 3.12+, while `requires-python` is `>=3.10`; a C projection folds naively and so tracked 3.11, which under ADR-0009 is a live multi-implementation parity break, not a hypothetical; **(iii) UNDERFLOW** — `[1e-200] * 3`, a CONSTANT vector (exact DC 1), squared to `energy == 0.0` and returned harmonic 2 at no boundary at all.

**THE HONEST NULL, stated so it is not overclaimed: the documented ±1-hypervector domain was NEVER at risk, and that is provable rather than unobserved.** `Sum(x)` and `Sum(|x|)` are exact small integers for n < 2^53 and IEEE division is correctly rounded, so an exact 1/2 renders as exactly `0.5`. `test_pm1_domain_was_never_at_risk` re-derives it exhaustively over every ±1 vector, n = 2..14. **Do not read this as "the classifier was returning wrong harmonics"** — it was wrong at three edges. All six worked-example verdicts are unchanged, pinned by a test.

*Also fixed in the same op:* the docstring advertised a `Mat` input and a `Mat` **raised** `TypeError` (`Mat` iterates ROW-WISE, so `float(v)` met a `list`); `harmonics._flat_scalars` makes the claim true. And the double float conversion at the old `:99` / `:145` is collapsed — the classifier now coerces exactly once.

**(2) The `describe()` granularity note gains its FOURTH sense of "the cube" (F1336).** rc353's `collision_note` was TRUE and INCOMPLETE, and accurate-but-incomplete is as serious as false the moment a planner acts on the gap. **An algebra of real dim `n` does not have `n` units — it has `2n` SIGNED units, needing `log2(n)+1` bits** (`log2(n)` for the index, one more for the sign). So H (dim 4) has 8 signed units = a **3-CUBE**, and O (dim 8) has 16 = a **4-CUBE**. The 16-vertex tesseract is therefore ALSO O's **unit-label** cube, not only S's grading cube — **two different 16s** (S: 16 basis DIRECTIONS; O: 16 signed UNITS). That is why 8 is the middle ground: O addresses 16 units in 4 bits AND contains H seven times (the Fano lines, verified closed under `cd_basis_product`, not asserted).

*The shadow result, DERIVED then MEASURED:* under a flat `(log2(n)+1)`-bit XOR label the low `log2(n)` bits XOR **exactly** (0 violations at every rung), but the TOP sign bit does **not** — violating ordered pairs number exactly **`2*dim*(dim-1)`** (4 / 24 / 112 / 480 at dims 2/4/8/16), a fraction `(dim-1)/(2*dim)` = 1/4, 3/8, 7/16, 15/32 -> **1/2**. **THE FLAT HYPERCUBE IS WRONG EXACTLY WHERE THE ALGEBRA ANTICOMMUTES**, and it worsens up the ladder. **BOUNDS, shipped inside the payload and asserted by a test so they cannot be dropped:** the closed form is DERIVED and CHECKED at six rungs (2/4/8/16/32/64), **NOT proved for all n**; "O is THE right carrier" is a **DESIGN argument, not a measurement**; and `(dim-1)/(2*dim)` is about **BASIS-PAIR PRODUCTS**, not a strand-misread rate — it must not enter an error budget. Generating code `docs/srmech/notes/unit_label_cube_rc354.py`; folded into notebook §2.5.1.

**(3) The DOMAIN-MATCHING vocabulary is a NULL, and ships as one.** A four-word MAGNITUDE / PHASE / ORIENTATION / PATH vocabulary was proposed for picking a carrier by what a domain needs. **Measured against the shipped registry: the published capability row determines the word for 3 of 25 carriers.** `float` (MAGNITUDE) and `complex` (PHASE) differ in EXACTLY ONE published field — `max_dim`, a dimension, not an order predicate; `address` is `"exact"` for all 25 (zero entropy); and `turn` is constant `"abelian_only"` across all 14 commutative carriers, i.e. no discriminating power in exactly the half where the two words must be told apart. **The missing field is an ORDER predicate**, missing for a structural reason: of the ladder's four loss steps the block measures three and never the first (R->C loses TOTAL ORDER; C->H `commutative`; H->O `turn`; O->S `compose`, which the four words have no name for at all). Two further blockers: the verdict space is a **LATTICE, not a chain** (`Mat` = (zero_divisors, non_commuting) and `octonion` = (full, abelian_only) — neither dominates, so `Mat` sits at no rung), and `Vec` **fits zero buckets** derivably.

**MAGNITUDE and PHASE are therefore NOT attached to any carrier row** — asserting a word beside data that does not determine it is the rc339 defect one level up. What ships is `carrier_schema._domain_word` / `_domain_word_gap()` (module-private, matching that file’s `__all__ = ["carrier_schema"]` convention — these are introspection derivations, not ops in the 14-class vocabulary, so they mint no ToolEntry), surfaced at `describe()["carriers"]["domain_word_gap"]`, DERIVED live from the rows so it cannot drift: the two words the row CAN decide are returned, the two it cannot are refused as `"undecidable"`, and the `order` field that would close it is specified with a falsifiable witness (formally real iff -1 is not a sum of squares) meeting the rc343 admission rule.

**(4) The worked examples are EXECUTED (gh #1530 §K).** `tests/test_worked_examples_strict_zero_rc353.py` says in its own docstring that it "cannot distinguish a captured output from a typed one — only re-execution can". `tools/run_worked_examples.py` is that re-execution; rc353's gate is unchanged and stays green.

*The explicit key was already in the tree.* §K asked explicit-key vs both-field scan. **Explicit key** — the inline `# -> <ExcType>` marker, promoted to normative and matched EXACTLY against the STATEMENT it binds to (trailing comment, or its own line immediately after; zero orphans measured). The both-field scan is rejected on measurement: 9 snippets carry a raise annotation but die EARLIER from an unrelated cause, and a "documents a raise, therefore a raise is a pass" scan marks all 9 GREEN — a false green in the very test built to stop one, strictly worse than the two false-RED traps §K records. A `# -> X` whose `X` is not an exception type is a VALUE annotation (`# -> True` occurs 141 times) and is ignored.

*Snippets made SELF-CONTAINED, never deleted.* **`hdc.polar_similarity`** read `open('srmech/amsc/attested/...')` — a cwd-relative read that resolves only from the package root; it now uses the public `catalog.iter_attested_dataset`, which is install-location and cwd independent and hands back the MPR envelope instead of bypassing attestation (re-run from a neutral cwd: 19 TE bands, `max(sg)` 9.121, similarity 1, the five negative controls identical — nothing re-captured). **The genome preamble** (`G`, `ONE`, `KMAP`, `FAM`, `codon`, `leaf`) was derived in-session and never written down, so 68 genome examples opened on an undefined name; it is now one shared `setup` block that **DERIVES** the 21 synonymous families with `genome.codon_read` against the attested `transl_table=1` rather than typing a table. **Seven snippets held an English sentence where code goes** (`max component drift`, `all int, no float in spectrum`, `max |LA - RA|`, ...) — each is now the statement that actually computes the value the `output` field already records, with the import it needs, and every magnitude written as an explicit Class-K sign branch rather than `abs()`.

**`hdc.loop_bind_hd` is NOT broken and was NOT "fixed".** It raises `AssertionError` at line 22 of 23 and line 23 is its own annotation: a documented guard, which the executor now positively VERIFIES instead of misreading as a failure. The §K table's "3 genuinely broken — certain" is honestly **2 certain, 1 misfiled by trap 1**, and that misfiling is the best argument for the explicit key.

*Architecture, forced by measurement:* ONE long-lived worker subprocess (`import srmech` costs ~0.5 s; 427 cold starts would be ~200 s of pure overhead), the timeout is the PARENT KILLING THE CHILD (no in-process interrupt is reliable, `SIGALRM` does not exist on Windows, and the CI matrix has a Windows cell), the worker runs from a **neutral temp directory** so a cwd-relative read cannot be certified as working, snippet `print()` is redirected away from the record channel, and cwd / `sys.path` are restored per snippet with periodic recycling. Per-snippet `src_sha256` makes the ledger's freshness assertion decidable, and the ceiling is keyed per CI cell because native dispatch changes outcomes.

**Version SSOT bumped in all five locations** (`pyproject.toml`, `pyproject-pure.toml`, `srmech/version.py`, `c/include/srmech.h`, and the pinned string in `tests/test_signal_processing_scaffolding.py`). No ABI change.

## [0.9.0rc353]

**THE INTROSPECT SURFACE STOPS BEING A STENCIL — all 513 tools get an EXECUTED, domain-grounded worked example and a three-perspective explanation, behind a strict-zero gate with no CEIL and no allowlist (`#T1010`).**

**The defect, measured.** Every one of the 513 `ToolEntry` examples was a SIGNATURE ECHO: 356 carried a literal `=<` type stencil (`algebra_table(dim=<int>, gammas=<Sequence[int] | None>) -> list`), the rest were zero-argument echoes, and **zero** carried executed output. `tool_schema.py` states the design as *"EXAMPLE (executed I/O where safe, else …)"* — the executed-I/O half had never been delivered, and the fallback shipped universally. It went unnoticed because the coverage ratchet asserted only that `summary` is NON-EMPTY; a stencil is non-empty, so the gate was green while the field said nothing.

**Why it is a show-stopper and not polish.** In one session an Opus 5 agent queued TWO phantom gaps against already-delivered code and nearly rebuilt both: `mat_rank` (while `QMat.rank(*, method=)` ships at `qmat.py:446` with C peer `srmech_qmat_rank`) and an ordered-enumeration primitive (which exists 7× in C, with `itertools.combinations` the correct Python projection — measured tuple-identical). The stencils did not stop it. Every example is now written so a reader cannot fail to see the op already does the job, and each names the sibling ops most likely to be re-derived by accident.

**What ships.** Worked examples of a FEW COHERENT CALLS with real captured output, grounded in real research subjects rather than random values — the attested CMB catalogs, the Antikythera gear arithmetic (Metonic 235/19, Saros 223, Callippic 940), the attested genetic code, Gell-Mann SU(3) and the CKM matrix, the 12-EDO circle of fifths and the nucleosome's 147 bp. Explanation length across all 513 now runs min 510 / median 1341 / max 2476 characters.

**The gate** (`tests/test_worked_examples_strict_zero_rc353.py`) is strict-zero on three conditions — no `=<`, non-empty captured output, and an explanation carrying all three perspectives — with **no `CEIL_`, no allowlist and no `-k` filter**. `=<` is a zero-false-positive marker: it is a syntax error in Python everywhere (the operator is `<=`), so it can only ever be a rendered type annotation standing where an argument value belongs.

**Fabrication check.** The gate certifies SHAPE, not truth, so every shipped example was re-executed in a FRESH interpreter on a numpy-absent host and diffed byte-for-byte against the shipped output: **0 mismatches**.

**Three real defects surfaced by the authoring, each fixed upstream:**

- **A local task ID shipping BARE in the compiled-in C registry.** `qm.quaternion.quaternion_cycle_holonomy`'s summary read `(#944 follow-on)` while the tree spells the same number `#T944` — a false link by construction, reaching users via `describe()`, the MCP tool list and `srmech_tool_registry.c`. HEAD carried three copies across two shipped artifacts. Adjudicated by reading both sides (same local task, no GitHub object), fixed at one character in `tool_schema.py`.
- **A registration literal permanently shadowing curation.** `sha256_bytes` and `sha256_batch` each carried a one-call `example=` stub on the REGISTRATION, and a registration literal always wins the `_apply_docs` merge — so the stub silently outranked `_tool_docs_curated.py`, the file the project designates for hand-curation. Same class as the rc291 finding. Both stubs removed, with the reason recorded in place.
- **A false docstring on `cascade.lstsq`.** It claimed to delegate to `mat_lstsq` unconditionally; that predated rc140's QR routing and was stale. Real input takes the QR path (`srmech_qr_f64`, which does not square the condition number); complex input, a rank-deficient `R`, or a native-absent host falls back to the normal equations. The `ToolEntry` summary had the QR shape right all along.

**The new worked-example prose tripped the numpy ratchet, and was REWORDED — not exempted.** The authoring put five numpy tokens into `_tool_docs_curated.py`, mirrored by regeneration into `_tool_docs.py`: `1 linalg/fft  3 matmul  1 ufunc` per file against `CEIL_LINALG_FFT = 2` (already fully spent by `laplacian.py`) / `CEIL_MATMUL = 0` / `CEIL_UFUNC = 0`. Every hit was legitimate prose — naming what the op does NOT fall back to (`not numpy's linalg.eigvalsh`), what it REPLACES (numpy's `exp(1j*θ)`), what it MATCHES (NumPy's matmul on two 1-D arrays), or what you would otherwise wrongly hand-roll (`V · V.conj().T - I`). The fix follows the **rc57 reword precedent — name the op, or write `·`** — with **no allowlist, no raised ceiling, no narrowed scan root and no touched regex**; weakening a guard to fit our own output is the failure this ratchet exists to catch, and deleting the entries would have thrown away the highest-value half of each one (a reader learns what to stop reaching for). The one EXECUTED site — `qr`'s `max(magnitude((Q @ R)[r, a] - A[r, a]) …)` — became `mat_matmul(Q, R)`, which names the shipped op instead of leaning on operator sugar and is the better documentation; the example was re-executed in a fresh numpy-absent interpreter and its captured output is byte-identical. Post-fix the ledger reads `2 linalg/fft  0 matmul  0 ufunc`, exactly the ceilings, with `laplacian.py`'s two pre-existing docstring mentions untouched.

**Also in this rc.** `describe()`'s granularity `collision_note` gains a second axis: `index_bits` is an EXPONENT (log2 of `slots`), never a dimension — so the 4-cube (tesseract) grades the SEDENIONS at dim 16, while ℍ's grading cube is the SQUARE (ℤ/2)². The tesseract that lives IN ℍ is a third object, 16 unit POINTS of ℝ⁴, and **128 of their 256 products leave the set** (measured), so no sign-bit XOR grades them.

**Notebook.** `srmech_research_notebook.md` gains §3.45, a USAGE EXAMPLES section organised by domain subject rather than by module, and §2.5.1, a notation entry for the `ℍ ⊗ ℍℓ` Cayley–Dickson doubling recording why the two imaginary triples are not interchangeable.

## [0.9.0rc352]

_**The `−` in `cd_mult`'s cross term IS the Cayley–Dickson γ, hardcoded to −1 — and the moment it becomes a parameter, `cd_norm_sq` is silently wrong on every algebra newly reachable. Two coupled tasks, shipped together because the second is only reachable once the first lands (`#T997`, `#T1001`). `tools.total` 511 → 513; `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 10 (three additive symbols; no exported signature changed).**_

- **`#T997` — `cascade.algebra_table(dim, gammas)` + `cascade.table_product(table, x, y)`, CONTROL-grade.** The generalised doubling is `(a1,a2)(b1,b2) = (a1·b1 + γ·conj(b2)·a2, b2·a1 + a2·conj(b1))` with one γ ∈ {+1, −1} **per rung**, in LADDER order (`gammas[0]` = ℝ→ℂ). `cayley_dickson._mult`'s hardcoded minus is that γ pinned to −1, and `cd_basis_product`'s `(ph, qh) == (1, 1)` branch is the single place it acts: γ = −1 flips the sign exactly when `ql == 0`, γ = +1 flips it exactly when it does not. **So there is ONE cocycle engine, not two** — `srmech_cd_basis_product` is now literally `cd_gamma_basis(dim, NULL, …)`, in C and in Python alike.

- **THE DEFAULT IS THE SHIPPED ALGEBRA, BIT-IDENTICALLY — pinned, not asserted.** `gammas=None` reproduces `cd_basis_product` at **every `(dim, i, j)` up to dim 64** (4096 pairs at 64, 0 disagreements); `algebra_table(8)` **IS** `qm.octonion_mult_table()` and `algebra_table(4)` **IS** `qm.quaternion_mult_table()`, element-for-element; and `table_product(algebra_table(dim), x, y) == cd_mult(x, y)` **300/300** on random dim-8 integer pairs and **200/200** on random exact-ℚ pairs. Those two counts are reproduced by a test, run as written — a quoted measurement no test reproduces is prose.

- **WHAT A `+1` BUYS, MEASURED — and it is narrower than it sounds.** All eight γ-triples at dim 8 give exactly **TWO** answers: `(−1,−1,−1)` → trace `(1,7,0)` / norm `(8,0,0)` = 𝕆, and **every other triple** → `(5,3,0)` / `(4,4,0)` = split-𝕆. The family is not eight algebras; it is 𝕆 and split-𝕆 seven ways. The split answer independently reproduces rc349's `inertia_signature` differential, which reached `(5,3,0)` through a third construction — three implementations, one number.

- **THE JUSTIFICATION IS CONTROLS, AND THE CAPABILITY ARGUMENT IS DEAD.** `[[feedback_negative_controls_for_carrier_claims_split_octonion_and_random_anticommutative]]` makes split-𝕆 / random-table controls mandatory, and every one this arc has needed — split-𝕆, split-ℂ, split-ℍ, 100+ random tables — was hand-rolled in a test file **because no constructor existed**.
