## [0.9.0rc351]

_**A pure / Pyodide / WASM install could SAVE a fiber-bearing genome and never load it back — and no CI cell could see it, because no cell had ever run the suite with `HAS_NATIVE=False` (`#T1004`). The marker set that keyed the block walk was spelled in six places; four had drifted. It is now spelled once, an AST ratchet fails the build on a seventh spelling, and `srmech-ci.yml` gains the `fallback (pure-Python, no native)` job. `tools.total` unchanged at 511; `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 10 (no signature changed).**_

- **THE DEFECT, VERBATIM.** `python -m pytest tests/test_genome_fiber_channel_rc322.py` on a clean tree with no native library: `GenomeBoundingError: genome body: unrecognised block kind byte 70 at offset 37`. Byte 70 is `0x46`, `FIBER_CAP_MARKER`. `genome.py` defines fourteen leaf-wide block markers and one tuple naming them, `_LEAF_WIDE_BLOCK_MARKERS`, whose own comment said it existed *"so the two can never drift on which markers are leaf-wide"*. Four walkers need that set. Three read the tuple. **The fourth — the no-native streaming reader INSIDE `genome_load`, the decoder a pure install actually runs — carried an inline hand-copy that stopped at `CHROMATIN_MARKER`**, omitting `FIBER_CAP_MARKER` (`0x46`) and `OCT_FIBER_CAP_MARKER` (`0x4F`). The C classifier `genome_cap_kind` knew both. Under **ADR-0009** that is a parity break with the polarity **inverted** — the *scripting* projection was the one missing the capability, which is the direction a native-first CI shape is structurally unable to observe.

- **THE WRONG DESCRIPTION AND THE MISSING GATE WERE THE SAME ROOT — that is the transferable half.** `.github/workflows/srmech-ci.yml:3-4` opened with *"srmech is pure-Python (no native binary, no cibuildwheel matrix)"*. Measured against the tree it describes: **135 C sources, 507 exported symbols, `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` 10, and cibuildwheel used in that very file and in `srmech-publish.yml`**. Not merely stale — self-contradicting inside its own file. A maintainer who reads "srmech is pure-Python" concludes there is no *second* path to test and therefore no fallback cell to add, and for the entire life of the C library none was added: `pure-wheel-build` builds the `py3-none-any` wheel and smoke-imports it, but **never runs pytest against it**. So every pure-only code path in srmech was CI-invisible, and this defect sat red on a clean tree with every job green. Header corrected; the job list is now enumerated in it; the `paths:` filter — which covered `docs/srmech/python/**` but **not `docs/srmech/c/**`**, so a C-only change ran neither the pedantic matrix nor the parity suite — is corrected in the same pass, same root.

- **FIXED BY REMOVING THE SPELLING, NOT BY EXTENDING THE COPY.** Adding two markers to the drifted list would have reproduced the drift once more. Every site now asks the ONE classifier: `_cap_kind` (HV form) and `_block_is_cap` (bytes form) are the only two readers of `_LEAF_WIDE_BLOCK_MARKERS`, which moved up beside the marker constants it names, and every walk asks one of them. Two more named sets remain, both reviewed declarations: `_CHROM_BOUNDARY_MARKERS` (the four chromosome-opening caps) and `_GENE_MARKERS` (the five gene delimiters), plus `_ACCESS_RESET_MARKERS`, **derived** from the first so a future boundary cap joins it for free. `_REGION_OPEN_MARKERS` is **gone** — it was a byte-identical duplicate of `_CHROM_BOUNDARY_MARKERS` declared 2 600 lines away.

- **THREE MORE SITES HAD DRIFTED THE SAME WAY. Grepping the marker names rather than trusting the reported count is what found them, and each is measured, not inferred.**
  - **`_hv_from_block`** — the same truncated 12-of-14 copy. A fiber cap came back from disk as `sectors=QUAD` while `_pack_fiber_cap` mints it at `sectors=256`. The bytes round-tripped and the **carrier** did not, silently, because `HV.__eq__` compares buffers only.
  - **`_ScanState.fold`** (and its C peer `genome_scan_fold_block`) — an eight-term `!=` chain. A fiber cap was counted as a **data turn**, so the rebuilt-by-scan `leaf_count` came back **one higher** than the `leaf_count` `genome_save` had written into the manifest: measured 4 vs 3 on a three-turn fiber chromosome. The manifest is documented as a *derived cache*; the derivation disagreed with the cache.
  - **`_gene_express_plan_strand`** — an unrecognised cap fell to the data branch and strode at the **packed-turn** width (9 bytes) instead of the leaf width (32). Measured: the trailing gene's span ended at byte **141**, which is *inside* a block. This is the identical failure the `rc340` comment three lines above it describes for the octonion turn rung, one marker family over.
  - Two further sites — `genes` / `gene_express` and their C peers — treated the §95b diploid telomere, the §95a centromere, the §98 chromatin cap and both fiber caps as **gene leaf data**, decoupling a cap through `sc_uncouple` as if it were content.

- **THE GUARD CATCHES THE CLASS, AND IT WAS PROVEN RED BEFORE IT WAS TRUSTED.** `tests/test_genome_marker_set_drift_rc351.py` parses `genome.py` and enforces three rules over **both** syntactic forms the drifted code used (a collection literal `kind in (A, B, C)` and a comparison chain `x != A and x != B`): **R1** no inline spelling equal to a named set; **R2** no inline *near*-copy — a proper subset covering more than half of a named set, which is the drift signature (12-of-14, 12-of-14, 8-of-10) while a deliberate two-element pair sits well under the line; **R3** named sets are pairwise distinct. The escape hatch is deliberate: declare your subset at module level with a name and a docstring, and the ratchet reads it as reviewed. **Demonstration: with the source fix reverted, 10 of the 12 rows in the file go red; restored, 12/12 green.** The two that pass either way are forward-looking completeness invariants (the canonical tuple already held all fourteen; so did the C classifier) and are labelled as such.

- **THE CI CELL WAS PROVEN RED BEFORE IT WAS TRUSTED, TOO.** `fallback (pure-Python, no native)` installs through the `pyproject-pure.toml` hatchling backend so **no CMake runs and no `srmech/_native/` is ever created**, then **asserts `HAS_NATIVE is False` and that `_find_library()` resolves nothing** — without that assertion a leaked library turns the cell into a silent duplicate of `build-and-test`, which is the exact failure mode that let this ship. Reproduced locally with the cell's own steps: **pre-fix tree, no library → 11 failed; post-fix → 709 passed, 347 skipped**. **Scope: the whole `tests/` tree, no `-k`, no file list** — a filter is how a green gate lies, and the pure paths worth defending are spread across genome / carriers / cascade / qm / hashing. The same anti-narrowing collection guard the `asserts-live-smoke` job uses (#937: *"coverage == COLLECTION"*) is applied here; that job already runs the full suite per-PR under `--forked`, which is heavier than this plain run. **What this cell does NOT cover, stated in the job comment: the C implementations themselves (by construction — that is the matrix's job) and the ~275 `skipif(not …native…)` differential rows, which skip here. `-rs` prints the skip count on every run so the size of the blind spot stays a number in the log.**

- **Two native-differential rows stopped asserting their own library into existence.** `test_f4_native_equals_pure_random_strands` in the rc322 and rc325 fiber suites opened with `assert _native.has_native_genome_*()`, so the no-native run was red on two rows for a reason unrelated to the code under test — part of why nobody ran it. They now `skipif`.

- **THE CELL'S FIRST RUN FOUND A SECOND, UNRELATED DEFECT — a degenerate eigenbasis that the native peer had been masking.** `symmetric_eigendecompose` projected the Hermitian solver's complex eigenvectors with a bare `.real`, on the docstring's premise that *"the Hermitian path returns them with imaginary part ~0"*. **That premise is false on a degenerate spectrum**, where every unitary basis of the eigenspace is equally correct and the cascade is free to return one carrying a phase. Measured, on the 3×3 IDENTITY: `V = [[1,0,0],[0,0,1j],[0,1,0]]` — a valid basis whose middle column is `i·e₂`. `.real` annihilated it, returning a matrix with a **zero row** that neither reconstructed (`V·diag(w)·Vᵀ` came back **0** where `L` was **1**) nor was orthonormal. Each column is now rotated onto the real axis first (`_pin_eigenvector_phases`: pick the largest-magnitude entry via `re²+im²` — no `abs()` — and multiply the column by `conj(pivot)/|pivot|`), which also **subsumes** the Class-K `Z₂` pivot-sign pin. **Measured over 804 real-symmetric matrices** (5 hand-built degenerate fixtures + 400 random-symmetric + 400 exactly-degenerate diagonals, n ≤ 6) the residual imaginary part after pinning is **identically `0.0`** — the columns are real up to a GLOBAL phase, never a genuine mixture — so the projection is exact, not an approximation. The pinning test (`test_symmetric_eigh_canon_routing_rc67.py`) had existed since rc67 and had been **silently red on the pure path ever since**; nothing could see it.

- **THE MAGNITUDE IS A CASCADE OP TOO — the A-N ratchet caught the first cut reaching for the FPU.** That phase pin was first written with `|pivot|` as `best ** 0.5`, and `tests/test_an_cascade_ratchet.py` failed on **every** CI cell simultaneously with `A-N cascade ledger drift float_pow: live=1 ceiling=0`. Deterministic, identical on Linux 3.10 / 3.12, macOS, Windows and asserts-live — it is an AST ledger, not a platform effect. **`CEIL_FLOAT_POW = 0` is a hard-won zero and the repair is to route the site through the cascade, never to raise the ceiling.** `|pivot|` is a *complex modulus*, which is precisely what `laplacian._fhypot` (`float(rational.hypot(re, im))`, **Class M** sum-of-squares ∘ **Class N∘K** sqrt) already exists for — it was imported in that same file, three lines from `_fsqrt`, labelled *"Class-N |z| magnitude, not libm"*. The lesson generalises past this diff: **sign-handling and MAGNITUDE are both cascade ops.** Doing the Class-K half correctly and then reaching for the FPU for the magnitude is half the discipline, and it is the half that is easy to miss because the sign rule is the one that gets quoted.
  - **A root here is genuinely unavoidable, and that was checked rather than assumed.** Producing a UNIT column from a non-unit one is a normalisation; the phase pin, the `Re`/`Im`-selection route and the `Re(zᵣ·conj(z_k))` route all land on the same `√(re²+im²)`. What IS avoidable is paying for it when there is no phase to remove — a pivot already on the real axis needs only the `±1` Class-K flip. **Measured over the same corpus (3214 columns pinned): the native path needs the root for 0 columns (0.00% — the C Jacobi always returns real columns) and the pure path for 150 (4.67%).** The cascade call is confined to exactly the degenerate columns that motivate the function.
  - Reconstruction / orthonormality are unchanged by the reroute: worst `rec_err` **4.168e-13** and worst `orth_err` **9.992e-16** on the pure path, identical to the `** 0.5` measurement.

- **`SRMECH_EXPECT_PURE=1` — an intent declaration, because `HAS_NATIVE == False` is ambiguous and the ambiguity is load-bearing.** Twenty tests are written to **FAIL, not skip**, when the library is absent (tasks `#T843` / `#918` / `#939`): *"the claim and the code must agree. If this fails, `mat_eigvals` is classified `c_dispatched` while no C entry point backs it — the exact false-claim shape this rc exists to end."* A silent skip is precisely what they exist to prevent, so a broken C build cannot pass quietly. In the new cell, though, the library is absent **on purpose** — and *"the build broke"* and *"we removed it deliberately"* produce the identical observation. The discriminator cannot be read off the library; it has to be **stated**. `tests/_native_gate.py` holds the ONE definition (`require_native`), the cell is the only thing in the repo that sets the variable, and **nothing changes anywhere else**: without it, every gate still fails exactly as before, now with the `#T843` reason attached instead of a bare `assert` or an `AttributeError` on a `None` library. It also cannot excuse a pure-path DEFECT — a gate is evaluated before its test body and cannot convert a failure into a skip. **Proven:** with the rc351 source fix reverted *and the variable set*, the cell still reports the same **11** genome-marker failures.

- **The excuse is AUDITED, because an unaudited excuse is a mute button.** `tools/audit_pure_by_design_skips.py` compares the gates that actually FIRED (from the run's `-rs` output) against the `require_native()` call sites **read out of the tree** — derived, never a frozen number. Both directions are red: a skip with no call site behind it, and — the one that matters — a **declared gate that stopped firing**, which means a test was deleted, renamed or filtered out. It runs *after* a green suite, which is exactly when a mute button would be invisible. **Demonstrated:** 20 declared / 20 observed → pass; delete one gate's skip line from the log → `::error::` + exit 1. An eleventh gated test is therefore a deliberate, visible act.

- **The cell's report flags were wrong in the first cut, and the CI log proved it.** `-rs` **replaces** pytest's default report characters rather than adding to them, so the first run's 26 failures had no `FAILED …` summary lines at all and had to be reconstructed from tracebacks. Now `-rsfE`: skips listed, failures summarised.

- **C moved in lockstep, and one hoist was needed.** `genome_scan_fold_block`, `genome_genes_split`, the append-region leaf counter and the `gene_express` region filter all now ask `genome_cap_kind` instead of re-spelling it; `genome_is_boundary_cap` (which already existed) supplies the boundary half. The rationale comments pushed `genome_genes_express_region` to 65 lines and tripped the down-only **JPL Rule 4** ratchet — the access-gate branch was extracted to `genome_express_fold_cap` rather than exempted. Pedantic `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic` clean; `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays **10** (no exported signature changed — derived manifest *content* is corrected for fiber-bearing bodies, which is a bug fix, not a wire-format change).

## [0.9.0rc350]

_**`gf_rref` accepts GF(2). The lower bound `2 < p` was never a scope decision about fields — it was the shadow of a Fermat pivot inverse that rc49 deleted, and srmech's only finite-field elimination had been refusing the grading field of its own Cayley–Dickson ladder ever since (`#T1003`). Widened in Python AND C; `tools.total` unchanged at 511; `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 10 (no signature changed — the accepted input set grew).**_

- **THE GUARD HAD A STATED REASON, AND IT WAS STALE — that is why this widens rather than adding a parallel GF(2) surface.** The rc44 C guard's own comment read *"p must be an odd prime in (2, 2\*\*31) so a\*b fits uint64 **and Fermat inversion is valid**"*, and rc44's `gf_inv` was indeed a private `a**(p-2) mod p`. **rc49 replaced that power with the extended-Euclidean `srmech_mod_inv`** (its own comment says so: *"rc49: supersedes the prior private Fermat power"*), which dissolved the Fermat half of the rationale. The surviving half — `a*b` inside one uint64 — justifies the **ceiling only**. So the refusal of `p = 2` had no live reason behind it, and a second surface would have been a duplicate of a kernel that was already correct.

- **THE ALGORITHM NEVER CARRIED THE ASSUMPTION; ONLY THE GUARD DID — measured before anything was edited.** Calling the untouched `_gf_rref_pure` at `p = 2` with the public guard bypassed matched an independent XOR-only oracle on **2100 random matrices across 7 shapes, 0 mismatches**. Char 2 is the *easy* end of the field range: the pivot inverse is `1⁻¹ = 1` (no division at all) and the row op is XOR. The odd-`p` hazards were probed individually rather than read for, and each is now a named test — `a == -a` (duplicate rows must collapse, not double), pivot division (`mod_inv(1, 2) == 1`), and the `(p+1)//2`-as-`2⁻¹` idiom (`gf_rref([[2]], 2)` must be **rank 0**, while `gf_rref([[2]], 3)` is rank 1 — the discriminator that keeps the char-2 answer from being a stub).

- **THE C PEER MOVED IN LOCKSTEP, AND WIDENING ONLY THE `if` WOULD HAVE SHIPPED AN NDEBUG-ONLY-GREEN CRACK.** `srmech_gf_rref`'s helpers `gf_add` / `gf_mul` / `gf_inv` / `gf_canonicalize` each carried `assert(p > 2u)`. Those asserts were unreachable while the top-level guard rejected `p = 2` first; the moment the guard widened they became live. **Measured by restoring them:** a debug build **aborts** at `gf_canonicalize` (`Assertion 'p > 2u' failed`) while a `-DNDEBUG` build passes silently. All four now read `assert(p >= 2u)`. The C smoke test's prime list gains `2u` (so char 2 is cross-checked against the same independent in-test oracle as every odd prime), its `"gf_rref rejects p=2"` case becomes `p=1` / `p=0` rejections plus an explicit `[[1,1],[1,0]] → I₂` char-2 case; **367 checks green under both `-O0 -g` and `-O2 -DNDEBUG`, pedantic `-Werror`**. The rationale comment then pushed `srmech_gf_rref` to 64 lines and tripped the down-only **JPL Rule 4** ratchet — hoisted above the function rather than exempted.

- **WHAT IT UNLOCKS — the CD index lane IS `(ℤ/2)^d`, and srmech's finite-field elimination had been excluded from it.** `cascade.cayley_dickson.cd_basis_product` sends `e_i · e_j` to index `i ⊕ j` at every rung in `CD_DIMS` (asserted exhaustively for dim ≤ 16). So the sedenion zero-divisor **support** condition is one GF(2) affine system: `(e_i + e_j)·(e_k + s·e_l)` expands to four terms at indices `i⊕k, i⊕l, j⊕k, j⊕l`, and with `i ≠ j`, `k ≠ l` the only pairing that can cancel is `i ⊕ j ⊕ k ⊕ l = 0`. Solving `[I | I | d]` through `gf_rref(…, 2)` and reading the affine solution set back out of the returned RREF gives the candidate supports; the sign is then **determined** (`s = −σ(i,k)·σ(j,l)`), not searched.

- **MEASURED: 735 candidates → 168 witnesses, set-identical to brute force, ~30× fewer products and ~449× faster.** Exhaustive brute force over all `(i,j,k,l,s)` — 22050 `cd_mult` products, 26.93 s — returns the **same 168** witnesses the GF(2) criterion finds in 0.06 s from 735 sign-free candidates. Every witness is verified to annihilate under the shipped `cd_mult` (no false positives); the set equality is the no-false-negatives half. The hardwired `sedenion_zero_divisor_witness()` (`e1 + e10`, `e4 − e15`; supports `1⊕10 = 4⊕15 = 11`) falls out of the construction. **Negative control:** the identical criterion over ℍ (3 candidates) and 𝕆 (63 candidates) returns the EMPTY set — the support system is satisfiable at every rung, and it is the sign condition that never closes below dim 16, so the dim-16 result is not an artifact of the method. **Why a solve and not a sample:** zero divisors are measure-zero in 𝕊 — 300 random dim-16 elements come back **300/300** left-multiplication-invertible, which is exactly why that witness is hardwired.

- **Additive by construction.** Every `p` accepted before is accepted now with identical output (regression-pinned at `p ∈ {3, 5, 7, 101, 65537, 2147483647}`); `p < 2` and `p ≥ 2**31` still raise. `QMat.rref_crt`'s prime walk stays odd **by design, not by domain** — it descends from just under the ceiling to keep each per-prime residue as wide as possible, so 2 is never a candidate. New: `tests/test_gf2_modular_linalg_rc350.py` (26 tests).

## [0.9.0rc349]

_**The inertia of the trace form `q(x) = Re(x·x)` separates the Hurwitz ladder from its split forms and from random tables — table-sensitive, exact, float-free (`#T987`, consolidating `#T968`). `srmech.amsc.cascade.inertia_signature` reads a rank-3 structure-constant TABLE, never a declared dimension and never a coordinate shortcut, and returns the Sylvester signature `(n₊, n₋, n₀)` in both the trace and norm forms with the negative pivot direction attached. `tools.total` 510 → 511; `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 10 (additive symbols); no existing behaviour changes.**_

- **GRADING FIRST, AND THE HEADLINE IS DELIBERATELY NARROW.** The loss ladder — ℝ→ℂ ordering, ℂ→ℍ commutativity, ℍ→𝕆 associativity, 𝕆→𝕊 composition — is the **classical Hurwitz result: definitional, textbook, forced**. Worse for any claim built on it: on the shipped ladder `n₋` is exactly **`dim − 1`** (measured 0/1/3/7/15 at dim 1/2/4/8/16), so **reading the shipped ladder is reading the dimension**. Grade those rows DEFINITIONAL. The claim that survives measurement is the one in the header, and nothing broader.

- **THREE THINGS AN INDEPENDENT DIFFERENTIAL BROKE IN THE FIRST CUT OF THIS RC, ALL CORRECTED HERE.** Each is now a named regression test, because each was a claim that read as sound and measured as false.

  1. **`n₋ == 0` DOES NOT MEAN "ORDERABLE"** — a false negative one rung above ℝ. **split-ℂ answers `(2, 0, 0)` with no negative direction, yet `(1+j)(1−j) = 0`** with both factors nonzero. A ring with zero divisors carries no compatible total order (each of `a>0,b>0` / `a>0,b<0` / `a<0,b<0` forces `ab ≠ 0`), so the observable would have certified as ORDERED something provably not orderable. The output is also uncorrelated with being a division algebra — it flags 𝕊 `(1, 15, 0)` and misses split-ℂ. **The `ordered` key is GONE**, replaced by `has_negative_direction` (`n₋ > 0`), whose honest reading is *"there is a negative-square direction in the trace form"* and nothing more. `test_the_op_never_claims_an_algebra_is_ORDERED` fails if any orderability key comes back.
  2. **THE COORDINATE FORM `a² − |v|²` IS INPUT-BLIND AND IS NEVER USED.** Measured over 4000 probes on `[−4, 4]⁸`: it agrees with the true `Re(x·x)` **4000/4000 on 𝕆 and 0/4000 on split-𝕆**. Both sides are exact integers, so this is a **substitution error that stays wrong at infinite precision, not a precision failure**. `Re(x·x)` is summed from the structure constants throughout. **This also re-diagnoses `#T968`:** its "the float read gets split-𝕆 demonstrably wrong" is almost certainly this substitution rather than floating point — and the shipped `cd_norm_sq` (`cayley_dickson.py`) is exactly that shape, `N(x) = Σ xᵢ²` in coordinates with a docstring asserting "positive-definite at every rung". It is **not a live bug today** only because no split constructor exists anywhere in the subtree; it is silently wrong the moment one arrives. Recorded here rather than changed, since fixing it means taking conjugation from a table and is a breaking change to a shipped op.
  3. **THE WITNESS ELEMENTS FIRST PROPOSED WERE NOT WITNESSES.** `[3,−5]² = −16 − 30i` and `[3,1,−3,4]² = (−17, 6, −18, 24)` — **neither is a negative real, so neither contradicts orderability.** Only a square that is a negative real *multiple of the identity* runs the classical argument (`eᵢ² = −1` ⇒ `−1` is a square ⇒ not orderable). The op returns the **negative pivot direction** from the congruence, and now reports the two facts separately: `witness_real_square` (`Re(w·w) < 0`, always) and `witness_certifies_nonorderable` (the full `w·w` is a negative real multiple of `e₀`). True on every ladder rung; a merely-negative trace direction is flagged as the weaker thing it is.

- **"ORDERED" DOES THREE JOBS AND THIS OP READS ONE — measured on srmech's OWN ops, and named in the payload.** ℂ is orderable as a *set* (trivially) and as an *additive group*: lexicographic order is compatible with the shipped `cd_add` **945/945**, and `cd_norm_sq` is multiplicative **2000/2000** (though not a *total* order — every magnitude class has ties and the ties are chirality orbits). What fails is compatibility with the *product*: **382/505**, because `(0,1)·(0,1) = (−1,0)`. So a negative-square direction denies an order **in the FIELD sense only**. Reporting "not ordered" unqualified would repeat the split-ℂ error in a subtler form — about an object that *is* ordered in two of three senses — so the result carries **`order_sense: "field"`** and the docstring spells out all three.

- **AN OPEN GAP, STATED RATHER THAN CLOSED — the prescribed repair does not work, and neither shipped op can be reused.** The natural fix for the split-ℂ false negative is "test isotropy of the norm to separate split-ℂ from ℚ(√2)". Measured, at this resolution it separates nothing: **split-ℂ and ℚ(√2) return IDENTICAL answers in BOTH forms** — trace `(2, 0, 0)`, norm `(1, 1, 0)` — because a signature is a **real-place** statement and `a² − 2b²` is isotropic over ℝ while anisotropic over ℚ. The two reuse candidates were checked before writing anything new, and both were rejected on measurement: **`cd_norm_sq` is the coordinate form** and returns `N([1,−1]) = 2` for a genuine null vector of the split norm (reusing it would have reproduced correction 2 exactly), and **`sedenion_zero_divisor_witness` takes no dimension argument** — it is sedenion-only, not a general isotropy surface. Separating them needs a **rational** zero of the norm form, which this op does not compute and this rc does not ship. Pinned by `test_the_norm_signature_does_NOT_separate_split_complex_from_Q_sqrt2` so a later reader cannot assume it was closed.

- **BOTH FORMS SHIP, NAMED — because the literature's `(4,4)` for split-𝕆 is the NORM form.** `q(x) = Re(x·x)` and `N(x) = Re(x·x̄)` are different reads with complementary signatures, and anyone checking `(5, 3, 0)` against a reference would conclude it had failed. Measured:

  | algebra | dim | trace `q` | norm `N` | `n₋ = dim−1` | witness |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | ℝ | 1 | `(1, 0, 0)` | `(1, 0, 0)` | yes | **none exists** |
  | ℂ | 2 | `(1, 1, 0)` | `(2, 0, 0)` | yes | `[0, 1]` |
  | ℍ | 4 | `(1, 3, 0)` | `(4, 0, 0)` | yes | `[0, 1, 0, 0]` |
  | 𝕆 | 8 | `(1, 7, 0)` | `(8, 0, 0)` | yes | `[0, 1, 0, …]` |
  | 𝕊 (sedenion) | 16 | `(1, 15, 0)` | `(16, 0, 0)` | yes | `[0, 1, 0, …]` |
  | **split-𝕆** | 8 | **`(5, 3, 0)`** | **`(4, 4, 0)`** | no | `[0, 0, 1, 0, …]` |
  | split-ℍ | 4 | `(3, 1, 0)` | `(2, 2, 0)` | no | `[0, 0, 1, 0]` |
  | split-ℂ | 2 | `(2, 0, 0)` | `(1, 1, 0)` | no | **none exists** |
  | dual numbers ℝ[ε]/(ε²) | 2 | `(1, 0, 1)` | `(1, 0, 1)` | no | **none exists** |
  | a random monomial dim-8 table | 8 | `(3, 3, 2)` | — | no | — |

  The norm column reproduces Springer & Veldkamp §1.7 exactly — `(1,1)`, `(2,2)`, `(4,4)` for the split composition algebras, definite for the others. The `n₋ = dim−1` column is the DEFINITIONAL grading made machine-checkable: **true for every shipped-ladder row and false for every split or degenerate one.**

- **THE MEASURED CEILING, which is hard and bounds every claim above.** `Re(x·x) = Σᵢ εᵢxᵢ²` **exactly** whenever the off-diagonal real parts vanish, with `εᵢ = Re(eᵢ·eᵢ)`. So pin the diagonal to 𝕆's and scramble the off-diagonal among the imaginary directions: **200/200 such tables return `(1, 7, 0)` — bit-identical to 𝕆 — while being 200/200 non-associative** (exhaustive lazy scan over all 343 imaginary basis triples; a five-triple probe was *not* decisive — 1 of 200 scrambled tables associated on all five, which is why the sweep is exhaustive). **The op reads the inertia of one quadratic form and nothing else. It cannot certify composition, alternativity, associativity or division** — `hdc.loop_associator` / `g2_three_form`, `genome_octonion_associator` and `left_mult_is_invertible` are the complementary instruments, and the docstring names them. A test pins this at 200/200 and a second test asserts the ceiling is stated in the docstring, so it cannot be refactored out of the surface a user reads.

  The scope is sharper than "blind to the off-diagonal", and that came out of getting the first version wrong: letting the scramble reach `e₀` puts real mass off the diagonal, and then the op **does** separate part of the family — **130/200 still identical, 70/200 separated**. The precise statement is that it reads **exactly the symmetric part of the real slice `c_ij0 + c_ji0`**, and nothing beyond it.

- **C1 — THE SPLIT OCTONIONS ARE THE PASS CONDITION, AND THE OP CLEARS IT.** An audit found a *different* mechanism holding 200/200 on shipped 𝕆, split-𝕆 **and** a random non-associative non-composition table alike, because it took no algebra input at all. **An instrument that cannot separate those three is not reading the algebra.** This one returns **three distinct answers** — `(1,7,0)` / `(5,3,0)` / `(3,3,2)`. Split-𝕆 lands `(5, 3, 0)` because 4 imaginary units square to `+1` and 3 to `−1`, so `n₊ = 1 + 4`. The split fixtures come from an **independent** generalized Cayley–Dickson doubling with per-level `γ ∈ {−1, +1}`, and the builder is cross-validated three ways: `γ = (−1,−1,−1)` reproduces the shipped `octonion_mult_table()` **byte-for-byte**, split-𝕆 is confirmed to carry a zero divisor by deterministic sweep, and 𝕆 is confirmed to carry none.

- **C2 — 240 RANDOM STRUCTURE-CONSTANT TABLES, EVERY WITNESS RE-VERIFIED.** 120 random **monomial** tables at dim 8 → **13 distinct signatures**; 120 **general** tables at dim 6 (arbitrary constants in `{−1, 0, +1}` — not monomial, not associative, not composition algebras) → **9 distinct signatures**. **0 witness-verification failures**, where "verified" means `w·w` is recomputed from the **full product over the table the witness came from**, not from the op's own Gram. Neither `(1, 7, 0)` nor `(5, 3, 0)` occurs **once** across the 240. An input-blind mechanism cannot produce that spread — this is the evidence the audit bar is cleared.

- **C3 — THE INSTRUMENT CAN RETURN "NONE", AND NOT BY READING THE DIMENSION.** A witness-finder that never returns "none" is not measuring anything, so ℝ returning no witness is a required control. It is not a `dim == 1` special case either: **split-ℂ and ℂ share dimension 2 and answer oppositely.** Both fall out of the same table read — and, per correction 1, neither answer is reported as "ordered".

- **`n₀` DOES REAL WORK, which required adding an input where it can.** On the whole ladder `n₀` is forced to 0, so it was doing nothing. **Dual numbers ℝ[ε]/(ε²)** — `ε² = 0`, a genuinely degenerate trace form — answer `(1, 0, 1)`, and the random monomial family fires `n₀ > 0` on its own (40/120 land `(3,3,2)`). Both are now tests.

- **AN INDEPENDENT EXACT ORACLE, SHARING NO CODE WITH THE THING UNDER TEST.** The Gram is real symmetric, so every eigenvalue is real and **Descartes' rule of signs is exact rather than an upper bound**. The oracle takes the integer characteristic polynomial by Faddeev–LeVerrier and counts sign changes in `p(x)` and `p(−x)`, with `n₀` the trailing-zero multiplicity. **249/249 agreement** across the named algebras and the 240 random tables. Two unrelated routes, one number.

- **EXACT AND FLOAT-FREE END TO END; NO FLOAT FAST PATH; SIGN IS THE CLASS-K PIN-SLOT.** The verdict is a comparison of two integer sums — no epsilon, no tolerance, no `float`, and **no `abs()` anywhere on the cascade path**, which matters more than usual because this op is *entirely* about sign. Magnitude is the named `_pin_magnitude` = `pin_slot_at_zero` (Class K) ∘ `reorient` (Class C), type-preserving on Python `int` so the elimination stays arbitrary-precision; gcd is the Class-I `srmech.amsc.cyclic.gcd`, not `math.gcd`. Tests grep the de-docstringed source of every helper for `abs(` / `float(` / `math.` / epsilon literals, and the C source for `abs(` / `llabs(` / `double` / `float`. Class K ∘ C ∘ L ∘ I — **no new primitive class**.

- **THE METHOD, so every number above is re-derivable.** `Re(x·x) = Σᵢⱼ xᵢxⱼ c_ij0`, whose symmetric integer Gram is `G_ij = c_ij0 + c_ji0` for the trace form and `G_ij = σⱼc_ij0 + σᵢc_ji0` (`σ₀ = +1`, else `−1`) for the norm form under the **named** conjugation `x̄ = x₀e₀ − Σ_{i>0} xᵢeᵢ` — a convention, not something a bare tensor determines. In both cases `xᵀGx = 2·f(x)`; the factor 2 is positive and moves no sign. Symmetric Gaussian elimination over ℤ then carries the invariant `A_ij = c·(Pᵢ)ᵀG(Pⱼ)` for one scalar `c` shared by the live block, of tracked sign `s`. The pivot-scaled Schur step `A_ij ← p·A_ij − A_ik·A_jk` keeps every entry an exact integer and multiplies `c` by `1/p` — which is precisely **why `s` flips exactly when the pivot is negative**, and the true sign at pivot `k` is `s·sign(p)`. When that is negative, **column `k` of `P` is the witness**, genuine by the same invariant. A zero-diagonal live block escapes through a determinant-1 hyperbolic fold; an all-zero one is `n₀`. The only division is an inertia-invariant positive-gcd strip, which holds the returned witness entries to **2 bits at every dimension probed**. Sylvester's law of inertia is what makes the answer independent of every pivot choice taken along the way.

- **C PARITY: a real symbol, differential-tested where the answer is NOT forced.** `srmech_algebra_inertia_signature` (+ `srmech_algebra_inertia_ws_bound`) ships in the new `c/src/srmech_algebra_inertia.c`, **caller-arena backed** (no malloc, no static scratch, no compiled-in memory cap) and JPL-clean: no goto, no recursion, every loop bounded by `dim ≤ SRMECH_ALGEBRA_INERTIA_MAX_DIM` (256), every function ≤ 60 lines with ≥ 2 asserts, warning-clean under `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -std=c99`. Per **ADR-0009** the capability is the invariant across projections, so agreement on the shipped ladder proves little and the differential deliberately covers the split algebras, the degenerate algebra and the diagonal-pinned ceiling family, **in both forms**: **618 checks, 0 mismatches** on signature AND primitive witness, `native_declined = 0`.

- **THE int64 CEILING IS REPORTED, NOT HIDDEN.** Exact intermediates grow (measured worst `|entry|`: 6 bits at dim 4, 13 at dim 8, 22 at dim 16, **62 at dim 32**), so **every multiply in C is overflow-guarded** and a genuinely large one returns `SRMECH_ERR_OVERFLOW` — never a silent wrap. Python then routes to its ceiling-free bignum path; a regression test drives a table with `10³⁰` entries through it and gets `(1, 1, 0)` with a verified witness. Same contract as `srmech_qmat`. A short arena and an unknown `form` are both **refused**, and both are tested.

- **THE TESTS EXERCISE THE SHIPPED OPS, AND THE ORACLE IS LABELLED AS ONE.** Per user direction 2026-07-27 (*"we like to use our own tooling when possible also for testing"*) and ADR-0009 — a test that computes its own `mult`/`add`/`norm` in bare Python tests the hand-rolled arithmetic, exercises **neither** projection, and lets the shipped op rot under a permanently green suite. So the ladder algebra here runs through **`cd_mult` / `cd_add` / `cd_conjugate` / `cd_norm_sq`**, including `x·x̄ = N(x)·1` end-to-end on the shipped surface. The split and random tables have no shipped product op, so a table-driven one is unavoidable — it is named **`_oracle_product`**, documented as an oracle, and **anchored to `cd_mult` at every rung in `DIVISION_ALGEBRA_DIMS`** (0 mismatches, 4 rungs × 40 random pairs) so it cannot drift. The independent Faddeev–LeVerrier signature oracle is likewise named `..._vs_independent_oracle`. The fences are read from the framework rather than hard-coded: the ladder test parametrizes over **`DIVISION_ALGEBRA_DIMS`**, the parity tests over **`INERTIA_FORMS`**, and `ASSOCIATIVE_ALGEBRA_DIMS` / `CD_DIMS` carry the associativity and past-the-wall fences.

- **Verification.** `regen_all.py` ran the full derived order and its second-pass idempotence proof passed; the delta is exactly the four files a `+1 public callable` moves — `_tool_docs.py`, `_c_claims.py`, `srmech_tool_registry.c`, `srmech_carrier_registry.c` — with the responsion and class tables unmoved. `gen_c_claims` harvested **both** C symbols against `srmech.h` (an undeclared symbol would have dropped silently into `UNVERIFIABLE_CLAIMS` and raised its down-only ceiling). The hardcoded `tools.total` moved 510 → 511 at **60 assertion sites across 54 test files**. Generating code for every number above: `docs/srmech/notes/algebra_inertia_controls_rc349.py`, NDJSON output beside it.

- **Canonical SSoT.** Sylvester, J.J. (1852), *Philos. Mag.* **4**:138–142 — the law of inertia. Hurwitz, A. (1898), *Über die Composition der quadratischen Formen von beliebig vielen Variablen* — 1, 2, 4, 8. Springer, T.A. & Veldkamp, F.D. (2000), *Octonions, Jordan Algebras and Exceptional Groups*, §1.7 — the split composition algebras and their quadratic-form signatures (the `(4,4)` is the NORM form).

## [0.9.0rc348]

_**A local task ID written as bare `#NNN` is a live link to someone else's issue — and four of them had reached SHIPPED artifacts (`#T986`). Reference-notation repair across the generator sources AND the prose they emit. No op added or removed (`tools.total` stays 510); `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 10; no behavior change. `tool_schema_sha256` DOES move — the C table is regenerated in lockstep and the byte-identity + hash ratchets recompute clean.**_

- **The measurement came first, and it did not match the precedent.** Task #T974 audited a 49-site set and found, after measuring, that nothing false had reached a wheel — every site was a docstring, comment or test. That conclusion was **not** assumed to extend here, and it did not. Regenerating and grepping the GENERATED artifacts found bare local-task refs baked into files that **ship in both wheels**: `srmech/amsc/_tool_docs.py` (module header + four `TOOL_DOCS` explanation values), `srmech/amsc/_c_claims.py` (module header), and the compiled-in C const table `c/src/srmech_tool_registry.c` (a table comment plus **eight** `ToolEntry` summary/explanation strings). So a consumer reading `describe()`, the MCP tool list, or the C registry was being handed `#938` — which GitHub renders as a link to *"srmech v0.7.5rc13: numpy-math ratchet + lmmse → cascade"*, an unrelated merged PR.

- **Every ref was adjudicated individually against BOTH the tracker and GitHub. A sweep would have broken a working link.** Each candidate was checked with `gh issue view` / `gh pr view` and against the owning rc's CHANGELOG entry. All six numbers resolve to real GitHub objects, so existence proves nothing — **topicality decides**:

  | ref | the prose describes | the real `#NNN` on GitHub | verdict |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `#943` | rc305 `ToolEntry.composes`/`.preserves` | v0.7.5rc18 matmul-kernel batch 3 | LOCAL → `#T943` |
  | `#838` | rc240 introspection docs floor | v0.7.0rc15 DSL surface audit | LOCAL → `#T838` |
  | `#916` | rc291 un-rederivable-prose guard | v0.7.3rc1 Cayley–Dickson demonstrator | LOCAL → `#T916` |
  | `#924` | rc294 stale executed-I/O examples | ephemerides-spectral v0.30.0rc10 | LOCAL → `#T924` |
  | `#938` | rc300 `c_claims` manifest / rc301 CD register | v0.7.5rc13 numpy-math ratchet | LOCAL → `#T938` |
  | `#1293` | the `carrier_schema()` CARRIER registry | **issue #1293: "expose CARRIER TYPES (a `carrier_schema()` peer to `tool_schema`)"** | **REAL — LEFT BARE** |

  `#1293` is an exact topical match and is written `gh #1293` at all nine of its sites — an authorial marker this tree already uses for genuine GitHub refs. It is a working link and was **not** touched. `#916` was independently confirmed already: `#T916` was in the tree at `codegen_manifest.py` and in this file, so the bare spellings were simply the unconverted remainder — one of which sat two lines from an existing `#T916` in the same file.

- **The generator sources and the prose they emit are one surface, so both moved.** Converting the comment that documents a defect while leaving the shipped string that exhibits it would have been incoherent. `gen_tool_registry.py`, `gen_tool_docs.py`, `gen_c_claims.py`, `gen_curated_probe.py` and `codegen_manifest.py` were repaired alongside `tool_schema.py`, `cd_register.py`, `cascade/__init__.py`, `introspect/__init__.py`, `_native.py` and `_tool_docs_curated.py`.

- **The un-rederivable-prose guard (`#T916`) did its job on this very change, and was not routed around.** Editing four `cd_register.py` docstrings made the committed `_tool_docs.py` explanations non-re-derivable, and `regen-all` **refused to write**, naming exactly four fields across four tools — `cd_carry`, `cd_correct`, `cd_couple_working`, `cd_uncouple_working`. That set was verified to be precisely the four docstrings edited and nothing else **before** `--accept-seed-drift` was passed, which is the documented response to a legitimate docstring change. The resulting diff was then re-checked line-by-line: the generated delta is `#838`×1, `#943`×1 and `#938`×13 replaced by their `#T` forms, plus the header lines below — no other byte moved, and no `#1293` moved.

- **Part 2 — an emitted header advertised a command that now REFUSES.** `_c_claims.py` told the reader to regenerate with `python3 tools/gen_c_claims.py`, but since rc346 a direct run of that script exits non-zero unless `--standalone` is passed. It now names the real entry point, `python3 tools/regen_all.py`, matching the four `.c` registry headers (already correct — the rc346 deferral had been closed for those, and **only** the Python-side header was still stale). `_tool_docs.py`, which named no entry point at all, gains the same pointer.

- **THE RATCHET — cleaning the instances without a guard would have been the same false green again.** A bare `#NNN` is valid text nothing computes over, which is exactly why it survived every existing gate for many rcs. `tests/test_ref_notation_emitted_rc348.py` now guards the **emitted artifacts** — the `regen-all` output set, derived from `codegen_manifest` so a seventh generator cannot ship an unguarded file (`test_every_emitted_artifact_is_pinned` goes red until a new output is classified). Deliberately scoped to what physically ships: the convention itself is now documented in the root `CLAUDE.md` ("Issue-reference notation"), and rc348 established that its **absence from every readable doc — not indiscipline — was the root cause**, since it lived only in one agent's memory and subagents never received it. Documentation is the primary control; this test is the last line of defence, and a bad ref authored upstream is caught here at the next regen, strictly before it can reach a wheel.

  Two pins, split by what is decidable without reading prose:

  - **STRICT ZERO — a known local task ID written bare.** If the tree spells a number `#TNNN` anywhere, that number IS a local task ID, so the same number spelled bare in a shipping file is a false link *by construction*. No adjudication needed. Zero today, and zero is the contract. The task-ID set is **derived** by scanning the tree (including `CHANGELOG.md`, which is excluded as a checked *surface* but is the most reliable *source* of the vocabulary) rather than hand-listed.
  - **DOWN-ONLY CEIL — every other bare ref** (`_tool_docs.py` 75, `srmech_tool_registry.c` 199, `srmech_carrier_registry.c` 2, the other three 0). These are pre-convention real GitHub refs still owed their `gh ` prefix. They are **not** batch-convertible — topicality decides, and a wrongly-converted working link is worse than an unconverted one because it looks deliberate — so the count is pinned and may only fall. A NEW bare ref fails the build and the author writes `gh #NNNN`, which is how the residual drains.

- **The guard exempts code spans, and that is load-bearing rather than lenient.** GitHub does not autolink inside a code span, so `` `#938` `` is the CORRECT way to quote a bad ref while documenting it — as the entry you are reading does throughout. A first-cut check that merely looked for `#\d+` would have gone red on the very changelog entry describing the fix, and a guard that cries wolf gets suppressed. Both backtick styles this tree uses are handled: immediate wrap (which a naive backtick *count* gets wrong for RST's ``` ``#938`` ```) and mid-span. Fenced code blocks are **not** handled, and that is measured rather than assumed: all six covered artifacts contain **zero** fence markers. Refs are bounded to **3–4 digits**, the range where "task or issue?" is a real question — which structurally removes `UAX #29`, `MS #20`, `Spike #24` and `F292 graft #1` instead of relying on a hand-maintained exemption list (an earlier draft had one, and it silently failed to match `UAX #29` anyway). The exemptions carry an in-file comment naming each and why, because **three separate bad ref-greps were written during this session** — wrong symbol prefix, wrong file path, and a version missing the code-span case.

- **The guard was PROVEN to fail, not assumed to.** Three injections into `_c_claims.py` (ceiling 0), each reverted after: a bare `#986` → **RED on both** checks (it is a known task ID *and* it grows the population); the same ref backticked as `` `#986` `` → **GREEN**, confirming the code-span exemption is real; a bare `#1500` → **RED on the CEIL only**, with strict-zero correctly silent because 1500 is not a task ID. Tree restored, 8 passed. (The first attempt at the backtick case was a **false green** — the shell ate the backticks via command substitution, so nothing was actually injected. It was redone through Python with the backticks verified present in the file before the run. An unproven exemption is exactly the false green this rc exists to remove.)

- **`CHANGELOG.md` is deliberately NOT covered, and the exclusion is commented in the test.** It holds ~360 bare refs across ~113 distinct numbers inside the region the `pypi-readme-changelog` markers slice into the PyPI long-description. Every one needs individual topicality adjudication before conversion, so it is tracked separately as **task T991** rather than swept.

- **Verification.** `regen-all` ran the full derived order (`gen_tool_docs → gen_c_claims → gen_tool_registry → gen_carrier_registry → gen_responsion_registry → gen_class_registry`) and its built-in second-pass idempotence proof passed: all 6 outputs byte-identical across two passes, 3 files changed. `regen_all.py --check` reports all 6 up to date. Targeted suite green — `test_regen_all_rc346`, `test_tool_registry_c_rc184` (byte-identity + `tool_schema_sha256` hash ratchet), `test_c_claim_resolution_rc300`, `test_tool_docs_coverage_rc240`, `test_cd_register_ops_rc301`, `test_composes_preserves_rc305`, `test_carrier_schema_rc205`, `test_class_registry_codegen_rc202`, `test_signal_processing_scaffolding`, plus the `tool_schema` consumers `test_mcp`, `test_mcpb_emit`, `test_introspect`, `test_rc15_describe_resolve`, `test_rosetta_completeness`, `test_mcp_marshal_c_rc187`. The two hash ratchets failed on first run against a **stale `.so`** — the rc347 build still held the old const table — and passed once `libsrmech.so` was rebuilt from the regenerated sources (134 `.c` files, gcc-13 `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic`, clean), which is the artifact-under-test discipline working as intended rather than a defect in the change.

## [0.9.0rc347]

_**The LANE axis: `describe()` now reports what each op READS (`#T985`). rc339 published what each CARRIER can DO; this is the complement over the VERBS, and a DIFFERENT axis rather than a finer grain of the same one. `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 10; `tools.total` stays 510.**_

- **THE CAYLEY–DICKSON PRODUCT FACTORS, AND EVERY OP CONSUMES ONE HALF, THE OTHER, OR BOTH.**

  | lane | what it is | character |
  |---|---|---|
  | **INDEX** | `e_i·e_j → e_{i XOR j}` | **abelian, order-blind**, exact at every rung, unbounded |
  | **SIGN** | the cocycle over it | **order-carrying**; every ceiling srmech publishes lives here (rc343) |

  **Lane is orthogonal to GRANULARITY** — `index == i XOR j` measured with **0 violations** at dims 2/4/8/16 (4/4, 16/16, 64/64, 256/256) and on the shipped `q8_mult` (64/64), i.e. the same statement at every addressing width — **and both are orthogonal to rc339's capability axis.** **Chirality is a SIGN-lane operation**, measured three independent ways over the basis products and moving **zero indices** in all of them: order reversal (the opposite algebra) moves 6/16 signs at ℍ, **42/64 at 𝕆**, 210/256 at 𝕊; `cd_conjugate` 14/64; `q8_conjugate` 24/64. Order reversal is the sharpest form of the claim — the index lane is order-BLIND and the sign lane order-CARRYING, which is the split stated as one measurement.

- **THE FIELD IS NOT AN ASSERTION — IT IS VERIFIED EXECUTABLY.** A declared lane that nothing can contradict is rc339's `bounded_by: "associativity"` in a new place, so `ToolEntry.reads_lane` carries the same shape of admission rule that `bounded_by` gained in rc343. Because chirality is sign-only, the two lanes can be perturbed **separately**, and that is what makes the declaration falsifiable:

  | | SIGN-lane perturbation | INDEX-lane perturbation |
  |---|---|---|
  | **algebra** | XOR the Q₈ center bit (`q ^ 4`); index untouched | relabel the V4 coset by ρ ∈ `Aut(V4) = S3`; sign bit untouched |
  | **geometry** | reverse orientation (reflect one axis); magnitudes untouched | positive-rational rescale; no orientation determinant changes sign |

  `tests/test_op_lane_rc347.py` drives **every** declaring op through both and asserts the response matches: `sign` must move under σ and **not** under a pure index relabel, `index` the mirror, `both` under both. An op declaring "sign only" that moves under an index relabel is **mis-declared and the build goes red**. A declaration with no driver also fails, because a field only *some* rows are checked against is the same false green one row at a time.

- **APPLICABILITY IS HALF THE RULE, AND IT IS WHY ONLY 9 OF 510 OPS DECLARE.** An op may declare only when **both** perturbations can be built for its input. `cascade.net_chirality` takes bare orientations (no index to move) and `cascade.cd_basis_product` takes bare indices (no sign to move) — **neither may declare**, not because the answer is unknown but because no measurement could contradict it. 501 ops correctly declare nothing; silence where nothing could be falsified is the honest report, and is the defect being *removed* rather than relocated.

- **Tw AND Wr ARE NOT ONE QUANTITY AT TWO RESOLUTIONS.** `genome.cwf_consistency_mod2` is the one shipped op that computes all three, so its **per-field** response IS the adjudication (3000 trials):

  | read | field | cascade | sign(algebra) | index(algebra) | sign(geometry) | verdict |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | **Tw** | `tw_mod2` | K ∘ I | **3000/3000** | **0/3000** | 0/3000 | SIGN, **ALGEBRA** |
  | **Wr** | `wr` | K ∘ C over E ∘ D | 0/3000 | 0/3000 | **3000/3000** | SIGN, **GEOMETRY** |
  | **Lk** | `lk_mod2` | M ∘ L ∘ C thru I | 735/3000 | **182/3000** | 0/3000 | **BOTH**, ALGEBRA |

  They read **different inputs** — a coset-sign count over the algebra vs the sign of orientation determinants over the geometry — and what they share is the **lane**. **Lk is the only mixer**: the only one of the three whose output answers to a pure index relabel. Wr's magnitude-blindness is the geometry-side proof it reads the sign and discards the magnitude it computed — `discrete_writhe` is **identical** under positive rational rescale ×1, ×3, ×100, ×1/7, ×999/4 (**5/5**) while **negating** under a reflection (−1 → +1). The fixture is asserted to have non-zero writhe: a writhe-0 embedding is reflection-invariant for the trivial reason, and the first one chosen was exactly that.

- **THE 2:4:8 CONFLATION GUARD SHIPS IN THE PAYLOAD, NOT IN A COMMENT.** `lanes["granularity"]` reports 𝕆 re-addressed at three widths — over ℝ (8 slots × 1 real dim, 3 index bits), over ℂ (4 × 2, 2 bits), over ℍ (2 × 4, 1 bit) — with **1 anchor + (n−1) torsors** at each: the identity sits in exactly one slot and **only that slot closes**. Measured through the index lane (closure under XOR, which is itself why lane is orthogonal to granularity): `H_L {0,1,2,3}` closes / `H_R {4,5,6,7}` does not; `C_LL {0,1}` closes / `C_LR`, `C_RL`, `C_RR` do not. **Those slot counts (8, 4, 2) are ONE algebra at three widths; `BLOCK_DIMS` (2, 4, 8) are the real dims of THREE algebras (ℂ, ℍ, 𝕆). Same three numbers, different objects** — so `granularity["reading"]` and `granularity["not_this_reading"]` name which is which, and a test asserts they do. A reader of `describe()` never sees a source comment; an unlabelled report *teaches* the confusion instead of removing it. (11D = 1+3+7 has no such collision.)

- **PROVEN AGAINST CLEAN `origin/main`.** `tests/test_op_lane_rc347.py` cannot itself run there — it imports `LANES` and reads `ToolEntry.reads_lane`, so it would **error on import**, and an import error proves nothing about whether the rule detects anything. The rule is therefore factored into `notes/op_lane_rc347_falsification.py` against nothing but surfaces main already publishes (`describe` / `get_tool_schema` / `q8` / `genome` / `qm.quaternion` / `cd_basis_product`) and run on both trees: **clean `origin/main` (`ea71fcbc3`, srmech 0.9.0rc346) exits 1 with 9 VIOLATIONS** — every one of the 9 ops has a *measurable* lane and `describe()` reports none of them, its top-level keys carrying no `lanes` at all — while rc347 exits 0. `--selftest` additionally injects two deliberately **wrong** declarations (`discrete_writhe` as `index`, `q8_project_v4` as `sign`) and requires the rule to catch both; it catches **2/2** on both trees, because a rule that has only ever seen correct data has not been shown to discriminate. Return codes read through `subprocess`, never `echo $?` — measured at rc346 that `wsl bash -lc '…; echo $?'` reports 0 for a control raising `SystemExit(2)`, which makes a guard look like it passed when it never ran.

- **SWEPT, NEVER SAMPLED — and the sweep changed two verdicts.** A single input can miss a real response: an even number of sign flips **cancels** inside an ordered product, and roughly one gain vector in fifteen exposes the Lk index response. The first draw of the probe reported `cwf_consistency_mod2` as index-blind and `discrete_writhe` as reflection-blind; **both were artifacts**, and both would have been shipped as declarations this ratchet then blessed. Every "did not respond" verdict in this rc is the verdict over the whole sweep.

- **rc346's `regen_all.py`, first real consumer.** One `python3 tools/regen_all.py` — derived order (`gen_tool_docs → gen_c_claims → gen_tool_registry → gen_carrier_registry → gen_responsion_registry → gen_class_registry`), 4 files written, **idempotence verified on the second pass**, 31.2 s. No generator was hand-sequenced and no reasoning was done about whether the carrier registry needed regenerating — the reasoning that sank rc345. `tools.total` did **not** move (510 → 510), so the carrier registry's real input (the sorted tool-name back-index) was unchanged and its delta is **its header comment only** — predicted, then **verified by reading the diff** rather than assumed.

- **The emitted `.c` header comments now name `tools/regen_all.py`.** All four C registry generators had been printing the old `python3 c/tools/gen_x.py > c/src/…` invocation — trap 2 preserved in the artifact, telling every future reader to use the form that silently changes nothing when the redirect is forgotten. rc346 left them stale deliberately to keep its own zero-delta signal clean; rc347 already moves those bytes, so it fixes them. The two `gen_unicode_*` generators are untouched (excluded from the pass as non-hermetic).

- **ABI stays 10.** `reads_lane` / `reads_input` are **data**, not an exported signature. Appending them to `srmech_tool_entry_t` is ABI-additive by the **rc305 precedent** — `composes` / `preserves` went onto this same struct without a bump — because callers receive a *pointer* from `srmech_tool_registry_get` and never allocate the struct, so every existing field offset is unchanged. Both JSON keys sort between `"preserves"` and `"returns"`, the C serialiser emits them there, and the `tool_schema_sha256` byte-identity contract is verified green. `GENOME_FORMAT_VERSION` unchanged.

- **The two lane keys tripped JPL Rule 4, and the fix went to the root.** They took `ts_emit_entry` to **67 lines** against the 60-line cap, so `ts_emit_lane` was extracted (13 lines, 3 asserts, Rule 5 clear) and `ts_emit_entry` is back to **59** — violations only go DOWN. Two independent files pin `describe()`'s exact top-level key set (`test_mcp.py::test_describe_shape`, `test_domain_classes_rc298.py`), and both were updated for `"lanes"`: a new `describe()` key is meant to be a reviewed act rather than something that lands unnoticed.

Targeted: the rc347 ratchet (21 passed), introspect / tool-schema / registry / MCP / Rosetta / `c_claims` / rc339 / rc343 / rc305, `regen_all --check`, and the version pin. ## [0.9.0rc346]

_**`regen-all`: the generated-file chain's run order is now DERIVED from declared dependencies, not remembered (`#T975`). Zero delta in every generated file — this rc changes how they are produced, not what. `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 10; no C source moved.**_

- **THE SET HAD BEEN MISCOUNTED THREE TIMES RUNNING.** The filed task said three generators. rc345 found a fourth the expensive way — it asked "did a carrier move?", answered *no* correctly, skipped `gen_carrier_registry`, and shipped a stale table, because that generator bakes the **sorted tool-name back-index** and goes stale on any change to `tools.total` whether or not a carrier moved. The rc346 survey found **six generators in the pass and two more that must be excluded**. A hard-coded call order encodes whichever count was current when it was typed; that is the whole argument for declaring the dependency instead.

- **THE EDGES WERE MEASURED, NOT READ OFF THE IMPORTS.** Each input was perturbed one at a time and all six generators re-rendered to see whose bytes moved:

  | perturbation | `_tool_docs.py` | `_c_claims.py` | `tool_registry.c` | `carrier_registry.c` | `responsion_registry.c` | `class_registry.c` |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | **new public callable** (`tools.total` +1) | 149084 → 149183 | — | moved | **180889 → 181113** | — | — |
  | **edited tool summary** (count-neutral) | — | — | moved | — | — | — |
  | **edited `_tool_docs.py`** (+14 bytes) | — | — | **827380 → 827394** | — | — | — |
  | **renamed a registered op** | — | — | — | — | **raises** | — |

  The third row is trap 1 measured at the mechanism: the injected bytes propagate **exactly**, because `tool_schema` merges `TOOL_DOCS` into every `ToolEntry.explanation` and `gen_tool_registry` bakes that prose into a C const table. Run the registry first and it is stale against the very docs it contains. The fourth row is why the responsion table joins the pass despite never moving on an addition — its dependency is a **validation** edge (`_validate_refs` requires every responsion `operator` to be a live schema key), so renames and removals break it outright.

- **THE ORDER IS DERIVED.** `tools/codegen_manifest.py` declares, per generator, the logical resources it `consumes` and `produces`, plus a `DERIVES` map recording which resource is built from which (`tool_schema ← tool_docs`; `carrier_schema ← tool_schema, carrier_examples`; `responsion_schema ← tool_schema, carrier_schema`). Edges are computed as "`a` precedes `b` when something `a` produces is in the transitive closure of what `b` consumes", and a topological sort with a declaration-order tiebreak yields the run order. Nothing names a sequence. Declaring a seventh generator's two fields places it automatically — **including behind `gen_tool_docs`**, which is the edge that has been forgotten every time.

- **FORGETTING TO DECLARE ONE IS NOW A RED TEST.** `discover_generator_scripts()` globs every `*/tools/gen_*.py` in the tree and `test_every_generator_is_classified` requires each to be either declared in `GENERATORS` or listed in `EXCLUDED` **with a stated reason**. Verified by dropping an undeclared `gen_seventh_probe.py` into `c/tools/` — the test names the file and fails. The two `gen_unicode_*` generators are excluded as **non-hermetic vendored upstream data** (they fetch UCD / UAX #29 over the network, import no srmech module, and are re-verified by their own attested tests); the two `gen_*_probe.py` are excluded as **human-in-the-loop curation** ("NOT the SSoT — the human reviews the emitted file"), since running them unattended would let a probe overwrite reviewed prose — the `#T916` defect aimed at the file that exists to survive regeneration.

- **TRAPS 2 AND 3 ARE NO LONGER REACHABLE BY THE CALLER.** The four C generators wrote to **stdout**, so a bare run with no redirect changed nothing while exiting 0 — success-shaped and inert. The runner now drives every generator through a render entry point and owns the write itself, so there is no stdout channel to lose output down. On line endings there is **no single on-disk convention to match**: measured at rc346 this tree carries `_tool_docs.py`, `srmech_responsion_registry.c` and `srmech_class_registry.c` as **CRLF** and the other three as **LF**, with no `.gitattributes` and `core.autocrlf=true` — so git normalises everything to LF in the object store and a wrong-convention write rewrites every line on disk while `git diff` stays clean. Writes therefore **preserve each file's existing convention** (unchanged content moves zero bytes) and comparisons **normalise** (never false-fire on the convention).

- **THE DEMONSTRATION FOUND A DEFECT IN THE RUNNER ITSELF, AND IT WAS THE SAME DEFECT.** The first version ran all six generators in one process, which *looked* ordered and was not: `srmech.amsc.tool_schema` merges `TOOL_DOCS` at **import** time, so writing `_tool_docs.py` part-way through a run never reaches a module already imported. `gen_tool_docs` wrote correct new docs and `gen_tool_registry`, microseconds later in the same interpreter, still rendered from the pre-write schema and emitted a table **20 bytes stale** — the exact failure `regen-all` exists to prevent, reproduced inside it. Caught because `--check`, run in a fresh process, reported `srmech_tool_registry.c` STALE immediately after a "successful" regeneration. **In-process ordering is not ordering.** Write mode now runs **one subprocess per generator** in derived order, which is the only version of "runs after" that survives an arbitrary future generator's import-time caching. `--check` stays in-process and is faithful there precisely because it writes nothing: every generator reads the state a fresh interpreter would read.

- **PROVEN AGAINST THE DEFECT IT TARGETS.** On a scratch copy, one op's docstring was edited and the generators run in the **wrong order** (`gen_tool_registry` then `gen_tool_docs`, exactly what the old per-script instructions said): the tree ended with correct docs and a tool registry **20 bytes stale**, carrying the superseded prose, and `--check` named the file. From the **same starting state**, `regen-all` produced the corrected 827400-byte table, `--check` came back clean, and the diff between the two results was **2 lines, localized** — the diff-shape test that distinguishes a real change from a wrong-EOL whole-file rewrite. The staleness guard, the curation guard and the anti-miscount guard were each additionally shown to **fail** on a tree carrying their defect.

- **DEV LOOP vs CI, measured.** `regen_all.py` (write + a built-in idempotence second pass, 12 subprocesses) is **31.9 s** — the dev loop. `regen_all.py --check` (content equality, one process, no writes) is **4.9 s**, cheap enough to always run, so it rides the existing `pytest tests/` suite as `test_no_generated_file_is_stale` rather than costing a new CI job. That also closes a real gap: `_tool_docs.py` is the **root** of the dependency order and was the one generated file in the chain with **no staleness check at all** — the four C registries and `_c_claims.py` each had one; the file they all descend from did not. **No mtime check was built**, deliberately: mtime is not a dependency signal in a git checkout (clone, rebase and `git checkout` set it in arbitrary order), so such a guard false-fires on CI and gets suppressed, and a suppressed guard is worse than none.

- **THE DEFAULT PATH IS THE CORRECT ONE.** Each of the six generators now refuses a bare `python3 tools/gen_x.py` — exit **2**, **zero bytes** written — and points at `regen_all.py`; the escape hatches are `--standalone` (raw: you own the redirect and the line endings) and `regen_all.py --only NAME --force-partial`, which names what is being accepted. Module **import** is unaffected, so every existing codegen test that drives a generator via `spec_from_file_location` is untouched. The stale `Regenerate:: python3 c/tools/gen_x.py > ...` instruction was corrected in all six module docstrings — it was the thing actively teaching the wrong order.

- **Zero delta, verified.** All six generated files were byte-identical fixed points before and after; `git diff --stat` over `_tool_docs.py`, `_c_claims.py` and `c/src/` is **empty**. Version bump touched 5 literals across 4 files with a **7-insertion / 7-deletion** localized diff. Pedantic build (`-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror`, cmake) clean, **0 warnings**; JPL Power-of-Ten ratchet unmoved (no C source changed). Targeted: 98 passed (rc346 + the six generators' own suites), 119 passed (JPL audit / MCP / tool schema), 24 passed (Rosetta), version pin green.

## [0.9.0rc345]

_**The genome's CONTENT count — `n_turns - n_chromosomes` — is what survives repartitioning, and it is DERIVED, never stored (`#T964`). `genome_save`'s returned catalog gains the scalars `n_chromosomes` + `n_content`; the on-disk head is byte-identical, `GENOME_FORMAT_VERSION` stays 19, `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 10.**_

- **GROUND TRUTH — the return and the head disagreed about SHAPE, not about the count.** `genome_save(...).get("n_chromosomes")` read `None` in 8/8 runs while the manifest head carried `n_chromosomes: 1`. Neither side was wrong. `_build_manifest_data_from_hexes` assembles the FULL catalog with a `chromosomes` **array** and no scalar; `_build_head_data` assembles the v12 HEAD with the **scalar** and no array; only the head reaches disk. So the count was never missing — it was `len(data["chromosomes"])`. The scalar name was already the house convention (`_read_head` has always back-filled it from the array in the other direction), so rc345 makes the full catalog honour it too, in both projections, with `n_chromosomes == len(data["chromosomes"])` always.

- **THE INVARIANT.** Each chromosome opens with exactly ONE boundary cap, and a cap is a `leaf_dim`-wide block — i.e. a turn — like any other strand element. So the boundary caps are IN `n_turns`, and subtracting the chromosome count removes the container overhead with **no residual**. Generating code: `scratchpad/fusion_test.py` (24 leaves, DIM 64, klein4 coupling seed 7, re-derived on every run of the new test module).

  | partitioning | `n_turns` | `n_chromosomes` | `n_content` | `body_sha256` |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 × 24 leaves | 25 | 1 | **24** | distinct |
  | 2 × 12 leaves | 26 | 2 | **24** | distinct |
  | 3 × 8 leaves | 27 | 3 | **24** | distinct |
  | 4 × 6 leaves | 28 | 4 | **24** | distinct |
  | 6 × 4 leaves | 30 | 6 | **24** | distinct |
  | 8 × 3 leaves | 32 | 8 | **24** | distinct |
  | 12 × 2 leaves | 36 | 12 | **24** | distinct |
  | 24 × 1 leaf | 48 | 24 | **24** | distinct |

  Neither the container count nor the raw turn count nor the digest is invariant; `n_content` is. **This is DEFINITIONAL to the format, not a discovery** — it restates "each chromosome emits a cap and a cap is a turn". What it buys is that the decomposition is EXACT, so two partitionings of the same content are comparable at all; an approximate relation would be useless for the one job it has.

- **THE SCOPE, STATED HONESTLY.** `n_content` counts every **non-boundary** block, which **includes inline caps** — §44 GENE caps, §95a centromeres. It equals `genome_census`'s `total_leaves` (which excludes *all* caps) only for a genome whose chromosomes have no inline structure. MEASURED: the same 24 leaves written as 4 genes of one chromosome give `n_turns` 29, `n_content` 28, `total_leaves` 24. The general law is `n_content == total_leaves + n_inline_caps`. Read it as "not a container", not as "leaves"; `genome_census` remains the leaf surface. `tests/…::test_content_counts_non_boundary_blocks_not_leaves` pins the inequality so the claim cannot drift back into the stronger form.

- **DERIVED, NEVER STORED — one encoding per datum.** `n_content` is exactly recoverable from the strand, so it gets no field in `manifest.json`: a stored copy of a derivable value is a second encoding that can go stale. The on-disk head is unchanged (same 7 keys, `format_version` 19), so there is no migration and no back-compat shim. Both scalars are computed at assembly time from counts the builder already holds — one `len()` and one subtraction, no extra read, parse, or hash.

- **NEW: `genome_content(path, *, coupling=None)`** → `{path, n_turns, n_chromosomes, n_content}`. It derives from the **strand** (the §44 body scan), not from the head's cached scalars — which is why it inherits the rc342 READ-SIDE INTEGRITY BOUND for free: the scan re-derives the region chain anyway, so holding it against the committed `body_sha256` costs no extra open, parse, or hash. A `turns.bin` modified out of band raises `GenomeBoundingError` here exactly as in `genome_catalog` / `genome_census`; a head-only fast path would have answered cheerfully. Manifest-less genomes pass through unbound and need `coupling=`.

- **CO-EQUAL C (ADR-0009).** New `srmech_genome_content` + `srmech_genome_content_arena_bytes`, so a bare-C host derives the three counts through its own entry point rather than reconstructing them from a catalog call. `genome_build_data`'s FULL branch emits the two new scalars too — without that the native catalog and the pure catalog would have disagreed on key set, which is an ADR-0009 split rather than a cosmetic gap. Verified native == pure for `genome_content` AND `genome_catalog` across 1/3/8/24 chromosomes. Additive symbols only, so **ABI stays 10**; a pre-rc345 library reports `has_native_genome_content()` False and takes the pure projection.

- **`genome_save` DOES NOT AUTO-PARTITION** — now stated in the docstring so the question stops recurring. "Splits" means it DERIVES boundaries from caps the **caller** already placed; it never invents one, and chooses no chromosome count, no split points, no size threshold. If it could re-partition, the bytes it wrote would not be the bytes it was handed and the manifest would stop being a pure derivation of the body. Pinned three ways (one long chromosome stays one; 24 single-leaf chromosomes stay 24; labels verbatim).

- **RATCHET PROVEN AGAINST CLEAN `origin/main`** (`3ebee07d8`), extracted with `git archive` rather than by switching the checkout: the new test module runs **14 failed / 1 passed** there, the failures being real `KeyError` on `'n_chromosomes'` / `'n_content'` and `AttributeError` on `genome_content` — not import errors. It imports only surfaces `origin/main` already publishes, so it RUNS there and disagrees. `fusion_test.py --ratchet` likewise reports 4 violations / exit 1 there and exits 0 here.

- **JPL.** The ratchet caught two violations in the new C and both were FIXED, not exempted: `genome_build_data` hit 67 lines (split into `genome_build_head_data` + `genome_carrier_name`, which also gives the on-disk head its own named function), and `srmech_genome_content_arena_bytes` had 0 asserts (given two real ones — nonzero budget, and at least `body_len`).

- **Ripple:** `tool_schema` ToolEntry, regenerated `_tool_docs.py` (510 tools) and `srmech_tool_registry.c`, the Rosetta ledger row (`non_compute`/`composes_c`, matching the rest of the genome family), and the `tools.total` pins 509 → 510 across 54 test files. `_c_claims.py` regenerated as a proven **no-op** (it covers `c_dispatched` ops; the genome family is `composes_c`). `srmech_carrier_registry.c` and the `srmech_invoke.c` arity guard are untouched — checked, not assumed: no carrier moved, and `srmech_invoke.c` carries no genome op at all. Regeneration is idempotent (second pass byte-identical).

## [0.9.0rc344]

_**`kron` documented itself as BYTE-IDENTICAL to an exact-integer parity oracle while riding float64 (`#T973`). The claim was false, and the ratchet guarding it compared `complex(g) == complex(w)` — rounding the exact oracle value to float64 before comparing, so it could never observe the loss. rc344 fixes the OP, not the claim. `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 10.**_

- **THE DEFECT.** `spectral_cascades.kron` claimed integer / Gaussian-integer input was "BYTE-IDENTICAL to the pure element loop (the parity oracle below)". That oracle is `_kron_ref` (`tests/test_residue_c_rc155.py`), which multiplies `a[i][j] * b[k][ell]` in native Python integer arithmetic — exact at any magnitude. `kron` routed the products through `laplacian.mat_matmul`, which is `array('d')`-backed on **both** its native and its pure-Python branch. So the claim was false for any product past float64's significand.

  A refutation that reads "parity oracle" as the pure-Python *fallback* does not save it: `mat_matmul`'s fallback also accumulates into `array("d")`, and `kron` has no pure fallback of its own. Both readings ride float.

- **THE MEASURED INVARIANT — significand width, NOT operand scale.** Generating code: `docs/srmech/notes/rc344_kron_significand_invariant.py`; re-derived in `tests/test_residue_c_rc155.py` on every run.

  | fixture | product bits | significand | float64-representable | exact pre-rc344 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `small_int` | 5 | 5 | yes | yes |
  | `gaussian_small` | 2 | 1 | yes | yes |
  | **`806bit_product_sig6`** (`7·2⁴⁰⁰ ⊗ 9·2⁴⁰⁰`) | **806** | **6** | yes | **yes** |
  | **`2**53+1_significand_54`** (`3 × 3002399751580331`) | 54 | **54** | no | **NO** |
  | `odd_square_significand_63` | 63 | 63 | no | **NO** |

  Exactness tracks `float64-representable` in every row. So `"kron exact" == "every entrywise product is float64-representable"`. This **refutes "goes wrong at operand scale 2²⁸"**: the 806-bit row multiplies 401-bit operands and is exact, because its significand is 6 bits. "Product exceeds 2⁵³" is closer but still wrong for the same row.

- **THE FIX — the op, not the docstring.** `kron` now runs an exact ℤ cascade for integer / Gaussian-integer input (`_int_components` + `_exact_kron`), mirroring how `dft` / `fft` in the same module already route integer signals through the exact `ℤ[ζ_N]` engine — *don't use floats for bit-exact math*. All-real integer input returns exact Python `int` at unbounded magnitude, so exactness survives the return value. Float input is untouched and still rides the C matmul (measured max error 0.0 vs the float oracle). **Measured cost: 1.19× at 64×64, 1.14× at 256×256, 0.97× (faster) at 576×576** — the exact path skips the `Mat` / interleaved-buffer marshalling, so it pays for itself at size. `kron` stays `composition_of_c`: the float path composes the C matmul, the exact path composes `srmech_bigint_mul`.

- **THE RATCHET WAS THE REAL DEFECT.** `complex(g) == complex(w)` coerces **both** sides — including the exact-integer oracle — into float64, so the assertion cannot see a lost integer regardless of fixture. Replaced with `_eq_exact`, which compares `.real`/`.imag` components directly and keeps Python `int`s on ℤ (Python's int-vs-float comparison is exact). Fixtures now span both sides of the significand, with `3 × 3002399751580331 == 2⁵³+1` — the smallest positive integer float64 cannot represent — pinned as the discriminating case. **Verified non-vacuous: the new ratchet run against clean `origin/main` fails 3 tests**, reporting `9007199254740992.0 != 9007199254740993`.

- **SIBLING AUDIT.** `tests/test_spectral_cascades_rc36.py::test_kron_matches_definition` carried the same float-blind comparison and a "bit-exact" comment, but against a FLOAT oracle (`complex(a) * complex(b)`) — so it was mislabelled rather than false. Comment corrected to say it tests float-path parity only, and a new `test_kron_is_exact_beyond_float64_significand` pins the exact contract there. `einsum` was checked and is **clean**: its docstring scopes "exact glue" to the gather/re-index (true — pure index permutation), it asserts against its oracle at `1e-9` tolerance, and it returns a `Mat`, so it never claimed byte-identity. No other op in `spectral_cascades.py` or `matrix_cascades.py` claims exactness against an exact-integer oracle while riding float; `curvature`'s `is_flat` certificate already scopes itself to "the exactly-float-representable entry regime".

## [0.9.0rc343]

_**rc339 replaced one false claim with a worse one: it gave the turn ceiling `bounded_by: "associativity"` — a RESTATEMENT OF THE DEFINITION — and published `max_dim: 4` as a GLOBAL statement that two rows in its own payload contradict (`#T972`). The ceiling is now PER-CARRIER, `bounded_by` names a MECHANISM, and the ratchet fails if any carrier row contradicts a stated bound. `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 10.**_

- **DEFECT 1 — `bounded_by: "associativity"` could not be falsified.** The same payload DEFINES `turn` as `L_x ∘ L_y == L_{x·y}`, i.e. `x·(y·z) == (x·y)·z for every z`. So turn composition **IS** associativity: anything associative turns, anything that turns is associative. The field could not discriminate between two carriers and no measurement could contradict it — the same false-green shape rc339 itself was written to remove, one turn further in.

- **DEFECT 2 — `max_dim: 4` was published globally and is false for any associative carrier at dimension.** Two rows in rc339's OWN `carriers` block contradict it, and both are MEASURED, not argued:

  | carrier | product | measurement | verdict |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | **`Mat`** | `mat_matmul` (associative at every dim) | `M_3(ℝ)` (algebra dim **9**): **81/81** turn-composing pairs, **42** of them NON-commuting. `M_4(ℝ)` (dim **16**): **256/256**, **108** non-commuting | turns fold, which-way intact, far above 4 |
  | **`Poly`** + `BiPoly`/`TriPoly`/`QPoly`/`QBiPoly` | polynomial multiply | `deg(p·q) == deg p + deg q` for every tested pair — an integral domain at unbounded degree | `compose: "full"` far above 8 |

  The turn ceiling of 4 is a **Cayley–Dickson** fact. Cayley–Dickson gives NON-COMMUTING turn **0/64** at dim 8 and **0/256** at dim 16 — the ceiling is real THERE. It was never a statement about every carrier srmech ships. **Root cause was a briefing error, not a code one:** "turns stop at ℍ / four real dimensions forever" was carried into rc339 as a GENERAL fact when it is a CD fact, and rc339 faithfully encoded the general form.

- **THE REPLACEMENT WITH ACTUAL EXPLANATORY CONTENT — the index/sign split.** MEASURED over the shipped `cd_basis_product` (generating code: `docs/srmech/notes/carrier_ceiling_rc343_falsification.py`; the split table re-derived in `tests/test_carrier_ceiling_rc343.py` on every run):

  | dim | index == a XOR b | negative signs (C(d,2)) | SIGN COCYCLE associative |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 2 | 4/4 | 1 (1) | 8/8 — **100%** |
  | 4 | 16/16 | 6 (6) | 64/64 — **100%** |
  | 8 | 64/64 | 28 (28) | 344/512 — **67%** |
  | 16 | 256/256 | 120 (120) | 2248/4096 — **55%** |
  | 32 | 1024/1024 | 496 (496) | (cost-skipped) |

  The CD product FACTORS into **(a)** an XOR on the **INDEX** — exact at EVERY rung, no exceptions — and **(b)** a **COCYCLE on the SIGN**. ℝ is value with no index; ℂ is value plus the first index bit; every subsequent doubling adds one index bit and extends the sign cocycle. So: **addressing is unbounded because XOR is associative at every dim forever; turns and composition break because THE SIGN COCYCLE stops being associative.** The wall was never in the addressing — which is also why rc298 (`#T933`) could lift `CD_MAX_DIM` 64 → 256 by DECOUPLING the caps.
